verses.text: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,

verses.raw: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
verses.text: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

verses.raw: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
verses.text: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

verses.raw: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what you do: for this man is a Roman.
verses.text: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what you do: for this man is a Roman.

verses.raw: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yea.
verses.text: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yea.

verses.raw: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
verses.text: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.

verses.raw: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
verses.text: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

verses.raw: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Yahudim (Jews), he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
verses.text: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Yahudim, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.

verses.raw: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before Elohim (God) until this day.
verses.text: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before Elohim until this day.

verses.raw: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
verses.text: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

verses.raw: Then said Paul unto him, Elohim (God) shall smite you, you whited wall: for sit you to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
verses.text: Then said Paul unto him, Elohim shall smite you, you whited wall: for sit you to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

verses.raw: And they that stood by said, Revilest you Elohim's (God’s) high priest?
verses.text: And they that stood by said, Revilest you Elohim's (God’s) high priest?

verses.raw: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.
verses.text: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.

verses.raw: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

verses.raw: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
verses.text: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

verses.raw: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

verses.raw: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against Elohim (God).
verses.text: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against Elohim.

verses.raw: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
verses.text: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

verses.raw: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem, so must you bear witness also at Rome.
verses.text: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem, so must you bear witness also at Rome.

verses.raw: And when it was day, certain of the Yahudim (Jews) banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
verses.text: And when it was day, certain of the Yahudim banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

verses.raw: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
verses.text: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

verses.raw: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.text: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

verses.raw: Now therefore you with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though you would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
verses.text: Now therefore you with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though you would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

verses.raw: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.text: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

verses.raw: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he has a certain thing to tell him.
verses.text: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he has a certain thing to tell him.

verses.raw: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto you, who has something to say unto you.
verses.text: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto you, who has something to say unto you.

verses.raw: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that you have to tell me?
verses.text: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that you have to tell me?

verses.raw: And he said, The Yahudim (Jews) have agreed to desire you that you would bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.text: And he said, The Yahudim have agreed to desire you that you would bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

verses.raw: But do not you yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from you.
verses.text: But do not you yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from you.

verses.raw: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See you tell no man that you have shewed these things to me.
verses.text: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See you tell no man that you have shewed these things to me.

verses.raw: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
verses.text: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

verses.raw: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

verses.text: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sends greeting.

verses.raw: This man was taken of the Yahudim (Jews), and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
verses.text: This man was taken of the Yahudim, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

verses.raw: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

verses.raw: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.text: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.raw: And when it was told me how that the Yahudim (Jews) laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to you, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before you what they had against him. Farewell.
verses.text: And when it was told me how that the Yahudim laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to you, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before you what they had against him. Farewell.

verses.raw: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

verses.raw: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.text: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

verses.raw: But this I confess unto you, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the Elohim (God) of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
verses.text: But this I confess unto you, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the Elohim of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

verses.raw: And have hope toward Elohim (God), which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
verses.text: And have hope toward Elohim, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

verses.raw: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward Elohim (God), and toward men.
verses.text: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward Elohim, and toward men.

verses.raw: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
verses.text: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

verses.raw: Whereupon certain Yahudim (Jews) from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
verses.text: Whereupon certain Yahudim from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

verses.raw: Who ought to have been here before you, and object, if they had ought against me.
verses.text: Who ought to have been here before you, and object, if they had ought against me.

verses.raw: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
verses.text: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

verses.raw: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
verses.text: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

verses.raw: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
verses.text: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

verses.raw: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
verses.text: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

verses.raw: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Messiah (Christ).
verses.text: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Messiah.

verses.raw: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go your way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for you.
verses.text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go your way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for you.

verses.raw: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
verses.text: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

verses.raw: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Yahudim (Jews) a pleasure, left Paul bound.
verses.text: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Yahudim a pleasure, left Paul bound.

verses.raw: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.
verses.text: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.

verses.raw: Then the high priest and the chief of the Yahudim (Jews) informed him against Paul, and besought him,
verses.text: Then the high priest and the chief of the Yahudim informed him against Paul, and besought him,

verses.raw: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
verses.text: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

verses.raw: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
verses.text: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.

verses.raw: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
verses.text: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

verses.raw: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.text: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

verses.raw: And when he was come, the Yahudim (Jews) which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
verses.text: And when he was come, the Yahudim which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

verses.raw: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Yahudim (Jews), neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.
verses.text: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Yahudim, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.

verses.raw: But Festus, willing to do the Yahudim (Jews) a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
verses.text: But Festus, willing to do the Yahudim a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

verses.raw: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Yahudim (Jews) have I done no wrong, as you very well know.
verses.text: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Yahudim have I done no wrong, as you very well know.

verses.raw: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
verses.text: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.

verses.raw: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Have you appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shall you go.
verses.text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Have you appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shall you go.

verses.raw: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.
verses.text: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.

verses.raw: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
verses.text: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

verses.raw: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Yahudim (Jews) informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
verses.text: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Yahudim informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.

verses.raw: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
verses.text: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

verses.raw: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
verses.text: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

verses.raw: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
verses.text: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

verses.raw: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Yahusha (Jesus), which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.text: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Yahusha, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

verses.raw: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
verses.text: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

verses.raw: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.
verses.text: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.

verses.raw: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, you shall hear him.
verses.text: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, you shall hear him.

verses.raw: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.
verses.text: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.

verses.raw: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Yahudim (Jews) have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.text: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Yahudim have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

verses.raw: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
verses.text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

verses.raw: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
verses.text: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

verses.raw: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
verses.text: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.

verses.raw: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, You are permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, You are permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

verses.raw: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before you touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Yahudim (Jews):
verses.text: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before you touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Yahudim:

verses.raw: Especially because I know you to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Yahudim (Jews): wherefore I beseech you to hear me patiently.
verses.text: Especially because I know you to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Yahudim: wherefore I beseech you to hear me patiently.

verses.raw: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among my own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Yahudim (Jews);
verses.text: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among my own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Yahudim;

verses.raw: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.text: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

verses.raw: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of Elohim (God) unto our fathers:
verses.text: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of Elohim unto our fathers:

verses.raw: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving Elohim (God) day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving Elohim day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that Elohim (God) should raise the dead?
verses.text: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that Elohim should raise the dead?

verses.raw: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Yahusha (Jesus) of Nazareth.
verses.text: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Yahusha of Nazareth.

verses.raw: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
verses.text: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.

verses.raw: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
verses.text: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

verses.raw: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.text: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

verses.raw: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.text: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

verses.raw: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me? it is hard for you to kick against the pricks.
verses.text: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me? it is hard for you to kick against the pricks.

verses.raw: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Yahusha (Jesus) whom you persecute.
verses.text: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Yahusha whom you persecute.

verses.raw: But rise, and stand upon your feet: for I have appeared unto you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto you;
verses.text: But rise, and stand upon your feet: for I have appeared unto you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto you;

verses.raw: Delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send you,
verses.text: Delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send you,

verses.raw: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto Elohim (God), that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.text: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto Elohim, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

verses.raw: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.text: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

verses.raw: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to Elohim (God), and do works meet for repentance.
verses.text: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to Elohim, and do works meet for repentance.

verses.raw: For these causes the Yahudim (Jews) caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
verses.text: For these causes the Yahudim caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.

verses.raw: Having therefore obtained help of Elohim (God), I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
verses.text: Having therefore obtained help of Elohim, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

verses.raw: That Messiah (Christ) should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
verses.text: That Messiah should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

verses.raw: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are beside thyself; much learning does make you mad.
verses.text: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are beside thyself; much learning does make you mad.

verses.raw: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
verses.text: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

verses.raw: For the king knows of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.text: For the king knows of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

verses.raw: King Agrippa, believe you the prophets? I know that you believe.
verses.text: King Agrippa, believe you the prophets? I know that you believe.

verses.raw: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost you persuadest me to be a Christian.
verses.text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost you persuadest me to be a Christian.

verses.raw: And Paul said, I would to Elohim (God), that not only you, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.text: And Paul said, I would to Elohim, that not only you, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

verses.raw: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.text: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

verses.raw: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.text: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.raw: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
verses.text: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.

verses.raw: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
verses.text: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.

verses.raw: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.text: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.raw: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.text: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

verses.raw: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.text: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

verses.raw: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.text: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

verses.raw: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

verses.raw: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.text: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

verses.raw: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.text: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

verses.raw: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.text: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,

verses.raw: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.text: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

verses.raw: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.text: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

verses.raw: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lies toward the south west and north west.
verses.text: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lies toward the south west and north west.

verses.raw: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

verses.raw: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
verses.text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

verses.raw: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
verses.text: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

verses.raw: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.text: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

verses.raw: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.text: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

verses.raw: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
verses.text: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

verses.raw: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.text: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

verses.raw: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.text: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

verses.raw: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, you should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
verses.text: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, you should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

verses.raw: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
verses.text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.

verses.raw: For there stood by me this night the angel of Elohim (God), whose I am, and whom I serve,
verses.text: For there stood by me this night the angel of Elohim, whose I am, and whom I serve,

verses.raw: Saying, Fear not, Paul; you must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, Elohim (God) has given you all them that sail with you.
verses.text: Saying, Fear not, Paul; you must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, Elohim has given you all them that sail with you.

verses.raw: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe Elohim (God), that it shall be even as it was told me.
verses.text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe Elohim, that it shall be even as it was told me.

verses.raw: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
verses.text: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

verses.raw: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
verses.text: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

verses.raw: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
verses.text: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

verses.raw: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
verses.text: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

verses.raw: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
verses.text: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

verses.raw: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, you cannot be saved.
verses.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, you cannot be saved.

verses.raw: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
verses.text: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

verses.raw: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.text: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

verses.raw: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
verses.text: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

verses.raw: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to Elohim (God) in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
verses.text: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to Elohim in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

verses.raw: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
verses.text: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

verses.raw: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
verses.text: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

verses.raw: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
verses.text: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

verses.raw: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
verses.text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

verses.raw: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
verses.text: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

verses.raw: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
verses.text: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

verses.raw: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
verses.text: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

verses.raw: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
verses.text: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:

verses.raw: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
verses.text: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.

verses.raw: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
verses.text: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

verses.raw: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
verses.text: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

verses.raw: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.text: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

verses.raw: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffers not to live.
verses.text: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffers not to live.

verses.raw: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
verses.text: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

verses.raw: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
verses.text: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

verses.raw: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
verses.text: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

verses.raw: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
verses.text: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

verses.raw: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
verses.text: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:

verses.raw: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
verses.text: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

verses.raw: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
verses.text: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

verses.raw: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
verses.text: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

verses.raw: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
verses.text: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

verses.raw: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
verses.text: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

verses.raw: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked Elohim (God), and took courage.
verses.text: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked Elohim, and took courage.

verses.raw: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
verses.text: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

verses.raw: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Yahudim (Jews) together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.text: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Yahudim together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

verses.raw: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
verses.text: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.raw: But when the Yahudim (Jews) spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
verses.text: But when the Yahudim spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

verses.raw: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Yashar'el (Israel) I am bound with this chain.
verses.text: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Yashar'el I am bound with this chain.

verses.raw: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning you, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of you.
verses.text: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning you, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of you.

verses.raw: But we desire to hear of you what you thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
verses.text: But we desire to hear of you what you thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

verses.raw: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of Elohim (God), persuading them concerning Yahusha (Jesus), both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.text: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of Elohim, persuading them concerning Yahusha, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.

verses.raw: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
verses.text: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

verses.raw: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
verses.text: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,

verses.raw: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see, and not perceive:
verses.text: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see, and not perceive:

verses.raw: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
verses.text: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

verses.raw: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of Elohim (God) is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
verses.text: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of Elohim is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.

verses.raw: And when he had said these words, the Yahudim (Jews) departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
verses.text: And when he had said these words, the Yahudim departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

verses.raw: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
verses.text: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

verses.raw: Preaching the kingdom of Elohim (God), and teaching those things which concern Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
verses.text: Preaching the kingdom of Elohim, and teaching those things which concern Lord Yahusha HaMashiach, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

verses.raw: Paul, a servant of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of Elohim (God),
verses.text: Paul, a servant of Yahusha HaMashiach, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of Elohim,

verses.raw: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)
verses.text: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

verses.raw: Concerning his Son Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
verses.text: Concerning his Son Yahusha HaMashiach our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;

verses.raw: And declared to be the Son of Elohim (God) with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:
verses.text: And declared to be the Son of Elohim with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:

verses.raw: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:
verses.text: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:

verses.raw: Among whom are you also the called of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):
verses.text: Among whom are you also the called of Yahusha HaMashiach:

verses.raw: To all that be in Rome, beloved of Elohim (God), called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from Elohim (God) our Father, and Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).
verses.text: To all that be in Rome, beloved of Elohim, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from Elohim our Father, and Lord Yahusha HaMashiach.

verses.raw: First, I thank my Elohim (God) through Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
verses.text: First, I thank my Elohim through Yahusha HaMashiach for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

verses.raw: For Elohim (God) is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;
verses.text: For Elohim is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;

verses.raw: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of Elohim (God) to come unto you.
verses.text: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of Elohim to come unto you.

verses.raw: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end you may be established;
verses.text: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end you may be established;

verses.raw: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.
verses.text: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

verses.raw: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.
verses.text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

verses.raw: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.
verses.text: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

verses.raw: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.
verses.text: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

verses.raw: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Messiah (Christ): for it is the power of Elohim (God) unto salvation to every one that believes; to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek.
verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Messiah: for it is the power of Elohim unto salvation to every one that believes; to the Yahudi first, and also to the Greek.

verses.raw: For therein is the righteousness of Elohim (God) revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The righteous shall live by faith.
verses.text: For therein is the righteousness of Elohim revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The righteous shall live by faith.

verses.raw: For the wrath of Elohim (God) is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;
verses.text: For the wrath of Elohim is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

verses.raw: Because that which may be known of Elohim (God) is manifest in them; for Elohim (God) has shewed it unto them.
verses.text: Because that which may be known of Elohim is manifest in them; for Elohim has shewed it unto them.

verses.raw: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:
verses.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

verses.raw: Because that, when they knew Elohim (God), they glorified him not as Elohim (God), neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.
verses.text: Because that, when they knew Elohim, they glorified him not as Elohim, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

verses.raw: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
verses.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

verses.raw: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible Elohim (God) into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.
verses.text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible Elohim into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

verses.raw: Wherefore Elohim (God) also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:
verses.text: Wherefore Elohim also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

verses.raw: Who changed the truth of Elohim (God) into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
verses.text: Who changed the truth of Elohim into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

verses.raw: For this cause Elohim (God) gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:
verses.text: For this cause Elohim gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:

verses.raw: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.
verses.text: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

verses.raw: And even as they did not like to retain Elohim (God) in their knowledge, Elohim (God) gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;
verses.text: And even as they did not like to retain Elohim in their knowledge, Elohim gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;

verses.raw: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
verses.text: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,

verses.raw: Backbiters, haters of Elohim (God), despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
verses.text: Backbiters, haters of Elohim, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

verses.raw: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:
verses.text: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:

verses.raw: Who knowing the judgment of Elohim (God), that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.
verses.text: Who knowing the judgment of Elohim, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.

verses.raw: Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, whosoever you are that judge: for wherein you judge another, you condemnest thyself; for you that judge do the same things.
verses.text: Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, whosoever you are that judge: for wherein you judge another, you condemnest thyself; for you that judge do the same things.

verses.raw: But we are sure that the judgment of Elohim (God) is according to truth against them which commit such things.
verses.text: But we are sure that the judgment of Elohim is according to truth against them which commit such things.

verses.raw: And thinkest you this, O man, that judge them which do such things, and do the same, that you shall escape the judgment of Elohim (God)?
verses.text: And thinkest you this, O man, that judge them which do such things, and do the same, that you shall escape the judgment of Elohim?

verses.raw: Or despisest you the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of Elohim (God) leads you to repentance?
verses.text: Or despisest you the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of Elohim leads you to repentance?

verses.raw: But after your hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim (God);
verses.text: But after your hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim;

verses.raw: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:
verses.text: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:

verses.raw: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:
verses.text: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:

verses.raw: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,
verses.text: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,

verses.raw: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that does evil, of the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also of the Gentile;
verses.text: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that does evil, of the Yahudi first, and also of the Gentile;

verses.raw: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that works good, to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Gentile:
verses.text: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that works good, to the Yahudi first, and also to the Gentile:

verses.raw: For there is no respect of persons with Elohim (God).
verses.text: For there is no respect of persons with Elohim.

verses.raw: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;
verses.text: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;

verses.raw: (For not the hearers of the law are just before Elohim (God), but the doers of the law shall be justified.
verses.text: (For not the hearers of the law are just before Elohim, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

verses.raw: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:
verses.text: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:

verses.raw: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)
verses.text: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)

verses.raw: In the day when Elohim (God) shall judge the secrets of men by Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) according to my gospel.
verses.text: In the day when Elohim shall judge the secrets of men by Yahusha HaMashiach according to my gospel.

verses.raw: Behold, you are called a Yahudi (Jew), and restest in the law, and make your boast of Elohim (God),
verses.text: Behold, you are called a Yahudi, and restest in the law, and make your boast of Elohim,

verses.raw: And know his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;
verses.text: And know his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;

verses.raw: And are confident that you thyself are a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,
verses.text: And are confident that you thyself are a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,

verses.raw: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which have the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
verses.text: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which have the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.

verses.raw: You therefore which teach another, teach you not thyself? you that preachest a man should not steal, do you steal?
verses.text: You therefore which teach another, teach you not thyself? you that preachest a man should not steal, do you steal?

verses.raw: You that say a man should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? you that abhorrest idols, do you commit sacrilege?
verses.text: You that say a man should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? you that abhorrest idols, do you commit sacrilege?

verses.raw: You that make your boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest you Elohim (God)?
verses.text: You that make your boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest you Elohim?

verses.raw: For the name of Elohim (God) is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.
verses.text: For the name of Elohim is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

verses.raw: For circumcision verily profiteth, if you keep the law: but if you be a breaker of the law, your circumcision is made uncircumcision.
verses.text: For circumcision verily profiteth, if you keep the law: but if you be a breaker of the law, your circumcision is made uncircumcision.

verses.raw: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
verses.text: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

verses.raw: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge you, who by the letter and circumcision do transgress the law?
verses.text: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge you, who by the letter and circumcision do transgress the law?

verses.raw: For he is not a Yahudi (Jew), which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:
verses.text: For he is not a Yahudi, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:

verses.raw: But he is a Yahudi (Jew), which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of Elohim (God).
verses.text: But he is a Yahudi, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of Elohim.

verses.raw: What advantage then has the Yahudi (Jew)? or what profit is there of circumcision?
verses.text: What advantage then has the Yahudi? or what profit is there of circumcision?

verses.raw: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of Elohim (God).
verses.text: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of Elohim.

verses.raw: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of Elohim (God) without effect?
verses.text: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of Elohim without effect?

verses.raw: Elohim (God) forbid: yea, let Elohim (God) be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That you might be justified in your sayings, and might overcome when you are judged.
verses.text: Elohim forbid: yea, let Elohim be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That you might be justified in your sayings, and might overcome when you are judged.

verses.raw: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of Elohim (God), what shall we say? Is Elohim (God) unrighteous who takes vengeance? (I speak as a man)
verses.text: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of Elohim, what shall we say? Is Elohim unrighteous who takes vengeance? (I speak as a man)

verses.raw: Elohim (God) forbid: for then how shall Elohim (God) judge the world?
verses.text: Elohim forbid: for then how shall Elohim judge the world?

verses.raw: For if the truth of Elohim (God) has more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
verses.text: For if the truth of Elohim has more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?

verses.raw: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.
verses.text: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.

verses.raw: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Yahudim (Jews) and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;
verses.text: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Yahudim and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;

verses.raw: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:
verses.text: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:

verses.raw: There is none that understands, there is none that seeks after Elohim (God).
verses.text: There is none that understands, there is none that seeks after Elohim.

verses.raw: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that does good, no, not one.
verses.text: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that does good, no, not one.

verses.raw: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:
verses.text: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:

verses.raw: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
verses.text: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:

verses.raw: Their feet are swift to shed blood:
verses.text: Their feet are swift to shed blood:

verses.raw: Destruction and misery are in their ways:
verses.text: Destruction and misery are in their ways:

verses.raw: And the way of peace have they not known:
verses.text: And the way of peace have they not known:

verses.raw: There is no fear of Elohim (God) before their eyes.
verses.text: There is no fear of Elohim before their eyes.

verses.raw: Now we know that what things soever the law says, it says to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before Elohim (God).
verses.text: Now we know that what things soever the law says, it says to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before Elohim.

verses.raw: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.
verses.text: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

verses.raw: But now the righteousness of Elohim (God) without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
verses.text: But now the righteousness of Elohim without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;

verses.raw: Even the righteousness of Elohim (God) which is by faith of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:
verses.text: Even the righteousness of Elohim which is by faith of Yahusha HaMashiach unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:

verses.raw: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God);
verses.text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim;

verses.raw: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus):
verses.text: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in HaMashiach Yahusha:

verses.raw: Whom Elohim (God) has set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of Elohim (God);
verses.text: Whom Elohim has set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of Elohim;

verses.raw: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believes in Yahusha (Jesus).
verses.text: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believes in Yahusha.

verses.raw: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.
verses.text: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

verses.raw: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
verses.text: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.

verses.raw: Is he the Elohim (God) of the Yahudim (Jews) only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:
verses.text: Is he the Elohim of the Yahudim only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:

verses.raw: Seeing it is one Elohim (God), which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
verses.text: Seeing it is one Elohim, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

verses.raw: Do we then make void the law through faith? Elohim (God) forbid: yea, we establish the law.
verses.text: Do we then make void the law through faith? Elohim forbid: yea, we establish the law.

verses.raw: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, has found?
verses.text: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, has found?

verses.raw: For if Abraham were justified by works, he has whereof to glory; but not before Elohim (God).
verses.text: For if Abraham were justified by works, he has whereof to glory; but not before Elohim.
