verses.raw: But received him honourably, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his men of war to be as obedient to him, as to himself.
verses.text: But received him honourably, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his men of war to be as obedient to him, as to himself.

verses.raw: To Jonathan also he said, Why have you brought all this people to so great trouble, seeing there is no war between us?
verses.text: To Jonathan also he said, Why have you brought all this people to so great trouble, seeing there is no war between us?

verses.raw: Therefore send them now home again, and choose a few men to wait on you, and come you with me to Ptolemais, for I will give it you, and the rest of the strong holds and forces, and all that have any charge: as for me, I will return and depart: for this is the cause of my coming.
verses.text: Therefore send them now home again, and choose a few men to wait on you, and come you with me to Ptolemais, for I will give it you, and the rest of the strong holds and forces, and all that have any charge: as for me, I will return and depart: for this is the cause of my coming.

verses.raw: So Jonathan believing him did as he told him, and sent away his host, who went into the land of Judea.
verses.text: So Jonathan believing him did as he told him, and sent away his host, who went into the land of Judea.

verses.raw: And with himself he retained but three thousand men, of whom he sent two thousand into Galilee, and one thousand went with him.
verses.text: And with himself he retained but three thousand men, of whom he sent two thousand into Galilee, and one thousand went with him.

verses.raw: Now as soon as Jonathan entered into Ptolemais, they of Ptolemais shut the gates and took him, and all them that came with him they slew with the sword.
verses.text: Now as soon as Jonathan entered into Ptolemais, they of Ptolemais shut the gates and took him, and all them that came with him they slew with the sword.

verses.raw: Then sent Tryphon an host of footmen and horsemen into Galilee, and into the great plain, to destroy all Jonathan’s company.
verses.text: Then sent Tryphon an host of footmen and horsemen into Galilee, and into the great plain, to destroy all Jonathan’s company.

verses.raw: But when they knew that Jonathan and they that were with him were taken and slain, they encouraged one another; and went close together, prepared to fight.
verses.text: But when they knew that Jonathan and they that were with him were taken and slain, they encouraged one another; and went close together, prepared to fight.

verses.raw: They therefore that followed upon them, perceiving that they were ready to fight for their lives, turned back again.
verses.text: They therefore that followed upon them, perceiving that they were ready to fight for their lives, turned back again.

verses.raw: Whereupon they all came into the land of Judea peaceably, and there they bewailed Jonathan, and them that were with him, and they were sore afraid; wherefore all Yashar'el (Israel) made great lamentation.
verses.text: Whereupon they all came into the land of Judea peaceably, and there they bewailed Jonathan, and them that were with him, and they were sore afraid; wherefore all Yashar'el made great lamentation.

verses.raw: Then all the heathen that were round about then sought to destroy them: for said they, They have no captain, nor any to help them: now therefore let us make war upon them, and take away their memorial from among men. ⸻
verses.text: Then all the heathen that were round about then sought to destroy them: for said they, They have no captain, nor any to help them: now therefore let us make war upon them, and take away their memorial from among men. ⸻

verses.raw: Now when Simon heard that Tryphon had gathered together a great host to invade the land of Judea, and destroy it,
verses.text: Now when Simon heard that Tryphon had gathered together a great host to invade the land of Judea, and destroy it,

verses.raw: And saw that the people was in great trembling and fear, he went up to Jerusalem, and gathered the people together,
verses.text: And saw that the people was in great trembling and fear, he went up to Jerusalem, and gathered the people together,

verses.raw: And gave them exhortation, saying, You yourselves know what great things I, and my brothers, and my father’s house, have done for the laws and the sanctuary, the battles also and troubles which we have seen.
verses.text: And gave them exhortation, saying, You yourselves know what great things I, and my brothers, and my father’s house, have done for the laws and the sanctuary, the battles also and troubles which we have seen.

verses.raw: By reason of which all my brothers are slain for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake, and I am left alone.
verses.text: By reason of which all my brothers are slain for Yashar'el’s sake, and I am left alone.

verses.raw: Now therefore be it far from me, that I should spare my own life in any time of trouble: for I am no better than my brothers.
verses.text: Now therefore be it far from me, that I should spare my own life in any time of trouble: for I am no better than my brothers.

verses.raw: Doubtless I will avenge my nation, and the sanctuary, and our wives, and our children: for all the heathen are gathered to destroy us of very malice.
verses.text: Doubtless I will avenge my nation, and the sanctuary, and our wives, and our children: for all the heathen are gathered to destroy us of very malice.

verses.raw: Now as soon as the people heard these words, their spirit revived.
verses.text: Now as soon as the people heard these words, their spirit revived.

verses.raw: And they answered with a loud voice, saying, You shall be our leader instead of Judas and Jonathan your brother.
verses.text: And they answered with a loud voice, saying, You shall be our leader instead of Judas and Jonathan your brother.

verses.raw: Fight you our battles, and whatsoever, you commandest us, that will we do.
verses.text: Fight you our battles, and whatsoever, you commandest us, that will we do.

verses.raw: So then he gathered together all the men of war, and made haste to finish the walls of Jerusalem, and he fortified it round about.
verses.text: So then he gathered together all the men of war, and made haste to finish the walls of Jerusalem, and he fortified it round about.

verses.raw: Also he sent Jonathan the son of Absolom, and with him a great power, to Joppa: who casting out them that were in it remained there in it.
verses.text: Also he sent Jonathan the son of Absolom, and with him a great power, to Joppa: who casting out them that were in it remained there in it.

verses.raw: So Tryphon removed from Ptolemaus with a great power to invade the land of Judea, and Jonathan was with him in ward.
verses.text: So Tryphon removed from Ptolemaus with a great power to invade the land of Judea, and Jonathan was with him in ward.

verses.raw: But Simon pitched his tents at Adida, over against the plain.
verses.text: But Simon pitched his tents at Adida, over against the plain.

verses.raw: Now when Tryphon knew that Simon was risen up instead of his brother Jonathan, and meant to join battle with him, he sent messengers to him, saying,
verses.text: Now when Tryphon knew that Simon was risen up instead of his brother Jonathan, and meant to join battle with him, he sent messengers to him, saying,

verses.raw: Whereas we have Jonathan your brother in hold, it is for money that he is owing to the king’s treasure, concerning the business that was committed to him.
verses.text: Whereas we have Jonathan your brother in hold, it is for money that he is owing to the king’s treasure, concerning the business that was committed to him.

verses.raw: Wherefore now send an hundred talents of silver, and two of his sons for hostages, that when he is at liberty he may not revolt from us, and we will let him go.
verses.text: Wherefore now send an hundred talents of silver, and two of his sons for hostages, that when he is at liberty he may not revolt from us, and we will let him go.

verses.raw: Hereupon Simon, albeit he perceived that they spoke deceitfully to him yet sent he the money and the children, lest perhaps he should procure to himself great hatred of the people:
verses.text: Hereupon Simon, albeit he perceived that they spoke deceitfully to him yet sent he the money and the children, lest perhaps he should procure to himself great hatred of the people:

verses.raw: Who might have said, Because I sent him not the money and the children, therefore is Jonathan dead.
verses.text: Who might have said, Because I sent him not the money and the children, therefore is Jonathan dead.

verses.raw: So he sent them the children and the hundred talents: howbeit Tryphon dissembled neither would he let Jonathan go.
verses.text: So he sent them the children and the hundred talents: howbeit Tryphon dissembled neither would he let Jonathan go.

verses.raw: And after this came Tryphon to invade the land, and destroy it, going round about by the way that leadeth to Adora: but Simon and his host marched against him in every place, wherever he went.
verses.text: And after this came Tryphon to invade the land, and destroy it, going round about by the way that leadeth to Adora: but Simon and his host marched against him in every place, wherever he went.

verses.raw: Now they that were in the tower sent messengers to Tryphon, to the end that he should hasten his coming to them by the wilderness, and send them victuals.
verses.text: Now they that were in the tower sent messengers to Tryphon, to the end that he should hasten his coming to them by the wilderness, and send them victuals.

verses.raw: Wherefore Tryphon made ready all his horsemen to come that night: but there fell a very great snow, by reason of which he came not. So he departed, and came into the country of Galaad.
verses.text: Wherefore Tryphon made ready all his horsemen to come that night: but there fell a very great snow, by reason of which he came not. So he departed, and came into the country of Galaad.

verses.raw: And when he came near to Bascama he slew Jonathan, who was buried there.
verses.text: And when he came near to Bascama he slew Jonathan, who was buried there.

verses.raw: Afterward Tryphon returned and went into his own land.
verses.text: Afterward Tryphon returned and went into his own land.

verses.raw: Then sent Simon, and took the bones of Jonathan his brother, and buried them in Modin, the city of his fathers.
verses.text: Then sent Simon, and took the bones of Jonathan his brother, and buried them in Modin, the city of his fathers.

verses.raw: And all Yashar'el (Israel) made great lamentation for him, and bewailed him many days.
verses.text: And all Yashar'el made great lamentation for him, and bewailed him many days.

verses.raw: Simon also built a monument upon the sepulchre of his father and his brothers, and raised it aloft to the sight, with hewn stone behind and before.
verses.text: Simon also built a monument upon the sepulchre of his father and his brothers, and raised it aloft to the sight, with hewn stone behind and before.

verses.raw: Moreover he set up seven pyramids, one against another, for his father, and his mother, and his four brothers.
verses.text: Moreover he set up seven pyramids, one against another, for his father, and his mother, and his four brothers.

verses.raw: And in these he made cunning devices, about the which he set great pillars, and upon the pillars he made all their armour for a perpetual memory, and by the armour ships carved, that they might be seen of all that sail on the sea.
verses.text: And in these he made cunning devices, about the which he set great pillars, and upon the pillars he made all their armour for a perpetual memory, and by the armour ships carved, that they might be seen of all that sail on the sea.

verses.raw: This is the sepulchre which he made at Modin, and it stands yet to this day.
verses.text: This is the sepulchre which he made at Modin, and it stands yet to this day.

verses.raw: Now Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young king Antiochus, and slew him.
verses.text: Now Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young king Antiochus, and slew him.

verses.raw: And he reigned in his stead, and crowned himself king of Asia, and brought a great calamity upon the land.
verses.text: And he reigned in his stead, and crowned himself king of Asia, and brought a great calamity upon the land.

verses.raw: Then Simon built up the strong holds in Judea, and fenced them about with high towers, and great walls, and gates, and bars, and laid up victuals in it.
verses.text: Then Simon built up the strong holds in Judea, and fenced them about with high towers, and great walls, and gates, and bars, and laid up victuals in it.

verses.raw: Moreover Simon chose men, and sent to king Demetrius, to the end he should give the land an immunity, because all that Tryphon did was to spoil.
verses.text: Moreover Simon chose men, and sent to king Demetrius, to the end he should give the land an immunity, because all that Tryphon did was to spoil.

verses.raw: To whom king Demetrius answered and wrote after this manner:
verses.text: To whom king Demetrius answered and wrote after this manner:

verses.raw: King Demetrius to Simon the high priest, and friend of kings, as also to the elders and nation of the Yahudim (Jews), sends greeting:
verses.text: King Demetrius to Simon the high priest, and friend of kings, as also to the elders and nation of the Yahudim, sends greeting:

verses.raw: The golden crown, and the scarlet robe, which you sent to us, we have received: and we are ready to make a stedfast peace with you, yes, and to write to our officers, to confirm the immunities which we have granted.
verses.text: The golden crown, and the scarlet robe, which you sent to us, we have received: and we are ready to make a stedfast peace with you, yes, and to write to our officers, to confirm the immunities which we have granted.

verses.raw: And whatsoever covenants we have made with you shall stand; and the strong holds, which you have builded, shall be your own.
verses.text: And whatsoever covenants we have made with you shall stand; and the strong holds, which you have builded, shall be your own.

verses.raw: As for any oversight or fault committed to this day, we forgive it, and the crown tax also, which you owe us: and if there were any other tribute paid in Jerusalem, it shall no more be paid.
verses.text: As for any oversight or fault committed to this day, we forgive it, and the crown tax also, which you owe us: and if there were any other tribute paid in Jerusalem, it shall no more be paid.

verses.raw: And look who are meet among you to be in our court, let then be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.
verses.text: And look who are meet among you to be in our court, let then be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.

verses.raw: Thus the yoke of the heathen was taken away from Yashar'el (Israel) in the hundred and seventieth year.
verses.text: Thus the yoke of the heathen was taken away from Yashar'el in the hundred and seventieth year.

verses.raw: Then the people of Yashar'el (Israel) began to write in their instruments and contracts, In the first year of Simon the high priest, the governor and leader of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: Then the people of Yashar'el began to write in their instruments and contracts, In the first year of Simon the high priest, the governor and leader of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: In those days Simon camped against Gaza and besieged it round about; he made also an engine of war, and set it by the city, and battered a certain tower, and took it.
verses.text: In those days Simon camped against Gaza and besieged it round about; he made also an engine of war, and set it by the city, and battered a certain tower, and took it.

verses.raw: And they that were in the engine leaped into the city; whereupon there was a great uproar in the city:
verses.text: And they that were in the engine leaped into the city; whereupon there was a great uproar in the city:

verses.raw: Insomuch as the people of the city rent their clothes, and climbed upon the walls with their wives and children, and cried with a loud voice, beseeching Simon to grant them peace.
verses.text: Insomuch as the people of the city rent their clothes, and climbed upon the walls with their wives and children, and cried with a loud voice, beseeching Simon to grant them peace.

verses.raw: And they said, Deal not with us according to our wickedness, but according to your mercy.
verses.text: And they said, Deal not with us according to our wickedness, but according to your mercy.

verses.raw: So Simon was appeased toward them, and fought no more against them, but put them out of the city, and cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and so entered into it with songs and thanksgiving.
verses.text: So Simon was appeased toward them, and fought no more against them, but put them out of the city, and cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and so entered into it with songs and thanksgiving.

verses.raw: Yea, he put all uncleanness out of it, and placed such men there as would keep the law, and made it stronger than it was before, and built in it a dwellingplace for himself.
verses.text: Yea, he put all uncleanness out of it, and placed such men there as would keep the law, and made it stronger than it was before, and built in it a dwellingplace for himself.

verses.raw: They also of the tower in Jerusalem were kept so strait, that they could neither come forth, nor go into the country, nor buy, nor sell: wherefore they were in great distress for want of victuals, and a great number of them perished through famine.
verses.text: They also of the tower in Jerusalem were kept so strait, that they could neither come forth, nor go into the country, nor buy, nor sell: wherefore they were in great distress for want of victuals, and a great number of them perished through famine.

verses.raw: Then cried they to Simon, beseeching him to be at one with them: which thing he granted them; and when he had put them out from thence, he cleansed the tower from pollutions:
verses.text: Then cried they to Simon, beseeching him to be at one with them: which thing he granted them; and when he had put them out from thence, he cleansed the tower from pollutions:

verses.raw: And entered into it the three and twentieth day of the second month in the hundred seventy and first year, with thanksgiving, and branches of palm trees, and with harps, and cymbals, and with viols, and hymns, and songs: because there was destroyed a great enemy out of Yashar'el (Israel).
verses.text: And entered into it the three and twentieth day of the second month in the hundred seventy and first year, with thanksgiving, and branches of palm trees, and with harps, and cymbals, and with viols, and hymns, and songs: because there was destroyed a great enemy out of Yashar'el.

verses.raw: He ordained also that that day should be kept every year with gladness. Moreover the hill of the temple that was by the tower he made stronger than it was, and there he dwelt himself with his company.
verses.text: He ordained also that that day should be kept every year with gladness. Moreover the hill of the temple that was by the tower he made stronger than it was, and there he dwelt himself with his company.

verses.raw: And when Simon saw that John his son was a valiant man, he made him captain of all the hosts; and he dwelt in Gazera. ⸻
verses.text: And when Simon saw that John his son was a valiant man, he made him captain of all the hosts; and he dwelt in Gazera. ⸻

verses.raw: Now in the hundred threescore and twelfth year king Demetrius gathered his forces together, and went into Media to get him help to fight against Tryphone.
verses.text: Now in the hundred threescore and twelfth year king Demetrius gathered his forces together, and went into Media to get him help to fight against Tryphone.

verses.raw: But when Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius was entered within his borders, he sent one of his princes to take him alive:
verses.text: But when Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius was entered within his borders, he sent one of his princes to take him alive:

verses.raw: Who went and struck the host of Demetrius, and took him, and brought him to Arsaces, by whom he was put in ward.
verses.text: Who went and struck the host of Demetrius, and took him, and brought him to Arsaces, by whom he was put in ward.

verses.raw: As for the land of Judea, that was quiet all the days of Simon; for he sought the good of his nation in such wise, as that evermore his authority and honour pleased them well.
verses.text: As for the land of Judea, that was quiet all the days of Simon; for he sought the good of his nation in such wise, as that evermore his authority and honour pleased them well.

verses.raw: And as he was honourable in all his acts, so in this, that he took Joppa for an haven, and made an entrance to the isles of the sea,
verses.text: And as he was honourable in all his acts, so in this, that he took Joppa for an haven, and made an entrance to the isles of the sea,

verses.raw: And enlarged the bounds of his nation, and recovered the country,
verses.text: And enlarged the bounds of his nation, and recovered the country,

verses.raw: And gathered together a great number of captives, and had the dominion of Gazera, and Bethsura, and the tower, out of the which he took all uncleaness, neither was there any that resisted him.
verses.text: And gathered together a great number of captives, and had the dominion of Gazera, and Bethsura, and the tower, out of the which he took all uncleaness, neither was there any that resisted him.

verses.raw: Then did they till their ground in peace, and the earth gave her increase, and the trees of the field their fruit.
verses.text: Then did they till their ground in peace, and the earth gave her increase, and the trees of the field their fruit.

verses.raw: The ancient men sat all in the streets, communing together of good things, and the young men put on glorious and warlike apparel.
verses.text: The ancient men sat all in the streets, communing together of good things, and the young men put on glorious and warlike apparel.

verses.raw: He provided victuals for the cities, and set in them all manner of munition, so that his honourable name was renowned to the end of the world.
verses.text: He provided victuals for the cities, and set in them all manner of munition, so that his honourable name was renowned to the end of the world.

verses.raw: He made peace in the land, and Yashar'el (Israel) rejoiced with great joy:
verses.text: He made peace in the land, and Yashar'el rejoiced with great joy:

verses.raw: For every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to fray them:
verses.text: For every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to fray them:

verses.raw: Neither was there any left in the land to fight against them: yes, the kings themselves were overthrown in those days.
verses.text: Neither was there any left in the land to fight against them: yes, the kings themselves were overthrown in those days.

verses.raw: Moreover he strengthened all those of his people that were brought low: the law he searched out; and every contemner of the law and wicked person he took away.
verses.text: Moreover he strengthened all those of his people that were brought low: the law he searched out; and every contemner of the law and wicked person he took away.

verses.raw: He beautified the sanctuary, and multiplied vessels of the temple.
verses.text: He beautified the sanctuary, and multiplied vessels of the temple.

verses.raw: Now when it was heard at Rome, and as far as Sparta, that Jonathan was dead, they were very sorry.
verses.text: Now when it was heard at Rome, and as far as Sparta, that Jonathan was dead, they were very sorry.

verses.raw: But as soon as they heard that his brother Simon was made high priest in his stead, and ruled the country, and the cities in it:
verses.text: But as soon as they heard that his brother Simon was made high priest in his stead, and ruled the country, and the cities in it:

verses.raw: They wrote to him in tables of brass, to renew the friendship and league which they had made with Judas and Jonathan his brothers:
verses.text: They wrote to him in tables of brass, to renew the friendship and league which they had made with Judas and Jonathan his brothers:

verses.raw: Which writings were read before the congregation at Jerusalem.
verses.text: Which writings were read before the congregation at Jerusalem.

verses.raw: And this is the copy of the letters that the Lacedemonians sent; The rulers of the Lacedemonians, with the city, to Simon the high priest, and the elders, and priests, and residue of the people of the Yahudim (Jews), our brothers, send greeting:
verses.text: And this is the copy of the letters that the Lacedemonians sent; The rulers of the Lacedemonians, with the city, to Simon the high priest, and the elders, and priests, and residue of the people of the Yahudim, our brothers, send greeting:

verses.raw: The ambassadors that were sent to our people certified us of your glory and honour: wherefore we were glad of their coming,
verses.text: The ambassadors that were sent to our people certified us of your glory and honour: wherefore we were glad of their coming,

verses.raw: And did register the things that they spoke in the council of the people in this manner; Numenius son of Antiochus, and Antipater son of Jason, the Yahudim (Jews)’ ambassadors, came to us to renew the friendship they had with us.
verses.text: And did register the things that they spoke in the council of the people in this manner; Numenius son of Antiochus, and Antipater son of Jason, the Yahudim’ ambassadors, came to us to renew the friendship they had with us.

verses.raw: And it pleased the people to entertain the men honourably, and to put the copy of their ambassage in publick records, to the end the people of the Lacedemonians might have a memorial thereof: furthermore we have written a copy thereof to Simon the high priest.
verses.text: And it pleased the people to entertain the men honourably, and to put the copy of their ambassage in publick records, to the end the people of the Lacedemonians might have a memorial thereof: furthermore we have written a copy thereof to Simon the high priest.

verses.raw: After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a great shield of gold of a thousand pound weight to confirm the league with them.
verses.text: After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a great shield of gold of a thousand pound weight to confirm the league with them.

verses.raw: Of which when the people heard, they said, What thanks shall we give to Simon and his sons?
verses.text: Of which when the people heard, they said, What thanks shall we give to Simon and his sons?

verses.raw: For he and his brothers and the house of his father have established Yashar'el (Israel), and chased away in fight their enemies from them, and confirmed their liberty.
verses.text: For he and his brothers and the house of his father have established Yashar'el, and chased away in fight their enemies from them, and confirmed their liberty.

verses.raw: So then they wrote it in tables of brass, which they set upon pillars in mount Sion: and this is the copy of the writing; The eighteenth day of the month Elul, in the hundred threescore and twelfth year, being the third year of Simon the high priest,
verses.text: So then they wrote it in tables of brass, which they set upon pillars in mount Sion: and this is the copy of the writing; The eighteenth day of the month Elul, in the hundred threescore and twelfth year, being the third year of Simon the high priest,

verses.raw: At Saramel in the great congregation of the priests, and people, and rulers of the nation, and elders of the country, were these things notified to us.
verses.text: At Saramel in the great congregation of the priests, and people, and rulers of the nation, and elders of the country, were these things notified to us.

verses.raw: Forasmuch as often there have been wars in the country, in which for the maintenance of their sanctuary, and the law, Simon the son of Mattathias, of the posterity of Jarib, together with his brothers, put themselves in jeopardy, and resisting the enemies of their nation did their nation great honour:
verses.text: Forasmuch as often there have been wars in the country, in which for the maintenance of their sanctuary, and the law, Simon the son of Mattathias, of the posterity of Jarib, together with his brothers, put themselves in jeopardy, and resisting the enemies of their nation did their nation great honour:

verses.raw: (For after that Jonathan, having gathered his nation together, and been their high priest, was added to his people,
verses.text: (For after that Jonathan, having gathered his nation together, and been their high priest, was added to his people,

verses.raw: Their enemies prepared to invade their country, that they might destroy it, and lay hands on the sanctuary:
verses.text: Their enemies prepared to invade their country, that they might destroy it, and lay hands on the sanctuary:

verses.raw: At which time Simon rose up, and fought for his nation, and spent much of his own substance, and armed the valiant men of his nation and gave them wages,
verses.text: At which time Simon rose up, and fought for his nation, and spent much of his own substance, and armed the valiant men of his nation and gave them wages,

verses.raw: And fortified the cities of Judea, together with Bethsura, that lieth upon the borders of Judea, where the armour of the enemies had been before; but he set a garrison of Yahudim (Jews) there:
verses.text: And fortified the cities of Judea, together with Bethsura, that lieth upon the borders of Judea, where the armour of the enemies had been before; but he set a garrison of Yahudim there:

verses.raw: Moreover he fortified Joppa, which lieth upon the sea, and Gazera, that bordereth upon Azotus, where the enemies had dwelt before: but he placed Yahudim (Jews) there, and furnished them with all things convenient for the reparation thereof.)
verses.text: Moreover he fortified Joppa, which lieth upon the sea, and Gazera, that bordereth upon Azotus, where the enemies had dwelt before: but he placed Yahudim there, and furnished them with all things convenient for the reparation thereof.)

verses.raw: The people therefore sang the acts of Simon, and to what glory he thought to bring his nation, made him their governor and chief priest, because he had done all these things, and for the justice and faith which he kept to his nation, and for that he sought by all means to exalt his people.
verses.text: The people therefore sang the acts of Simon, and to what glory he thought to bring his nation, made him their governor and chief priest, because he had done all these things, and for the justice and faith which he kept to his nation, and for that he sought by all means to exalt his people.

verses.raw: For in his time things prospered in his hands, so that the heathen were taken out of their country, and they also that were in the city of David in Jerusalem, who had made themselves a tower, out of which they issued, and polluted all about the sanctuary, and did much hurt in the holy place:
verses.text: For in his time things prospered in his hands, so that the heathen were taken out of their country, and they also that were in the city of David in Jerusalem, who had made themselves a tower, out of which they issued, and polluted all about the sanctuary, and did much hurt in the holy place:

verses.raw: But he placed Yahudim (Jews) in it. and fortified it for the safety of the country and the city, and raised up the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.text: But he placed Yahudim in it. and fortified it for the safety of the country and the city, and raised up the walls of Jerusalem.

verses.raw: King Demetrius also confirmed him in the high priesthood according to those things,
verses.text: King Demetrius also confirmed him in the high priesthood according to those things,

verses.raw: And made him one of his friends, and honoured him with great honour.
verses.text: And made him one of his friends, and honoured him with great honour.

verses.raw: For he had heard say, that the Romans had called the Yahudim (Jews) their friends and confederates and brothers; and that they had entertained the ambassadors of Simon honourably;
verses.text: For he had heard say, that the Romans had called the Yahudim their friends and confederates and brothers; and that they had entertained the ambassadors of Simon honourably;

verses.raw: Also that the Yahudim (Jews) and priests were well pleased that Simon should be their governor and high priest for ever, until there should arise a faithful prophet;
verses.text: Also that the Yahudim and priests were well pleased that Simon should be their governor and high priest for ever, until there should arise a faithful prophet;

verses.raw: Moreover that he should be their captain, and should take charge of the sanctuary, to set them over their works, and over the country, and over the armour, and over the fortresses, that, I say, he should take charge of the sanctuary;
verses.text: Moreover that he should be their captain, and should take charge of the sanctuary, to set them over their works, and over the country, and over the armour, and over the fortresses, that, I say, he should take charge of the sanctuary;

verses.raw: Beside this, that he should be obeyed of every man, and that all the writings in the country should be made in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple, and wear gold:
verses.text: Beside this, that he should be obeyed of every man, and that all the writings in the country should be made in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple, and wear gold:

verses.raw: Also that it should be lawful for none of the people or priests to break any of these things, or to gainsay his words, or to gather an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or wear a buckle of gold;
verses.text: Also that it should be lawful for none of the people or priests to break any of these things, or to gainsay his words, or to gather an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or wear a buckle of gold;

verses.raw: And whoever should do otherwise, or break any of these things, he should be punished.
verses.text: And whoever should do otherwise, or break any of these things, he should be punished.

verses.raw: Thus it liked all the people to deal with Simon, and to do as has been said.
verses.text: Thus it liked all the people to deal with Simon, and to do as has been said.

verses.raw: Then Simon accepted of this, and was well pleased to be high priest, and captain and governor of the Yahudim (Jews) and priests, and to defend them all.
verses.text: Then Simon accepted of this, and was well pleased to be high priest, and captain and governor of the Yahudim and priests, and to defend them all.

verses.raw: So they commanded that this writing should be put in tables of brass, and that they should be set up within the compass of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place;
verses.text: So they commanded that this writing should be put in tables of brass, and that they should be set up within the compass of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place;

verses.raw: Also that the copies thereof should be laid up in the treasury, to the end that Simon and his sons might have them. ⸻
verses.text: Also that the copies thereof should be laid up in the treasury, to the end that Simon and his sons might have them. ⸻

verses.raw: Moreover Antiochus son of Demetrius the king sent letters from the isles of the sea to Simon the priest and prince of the Yahudim (Jews), and to all the people;
verses.text: Moreover Antiochus son of Demetrius the king sent letters from the isles of the sea to Simon the priest and prince of the Yahudim, and to all the people;

verses.raw: The contents of which were these: King Antiochus to Simon the high priest and prince of his nation, and to the people of the Yahudim (Jews), greeting:
verses.text: The contents of which were these: King Antiochus to Simon the high priest and prince of his nation, and to the people of the Yahudim, greeting:

verses.raw: Forasmuch as certain pestilent men have usurped the kingdom of our fathers, and my purpose is to challenge it again, that I may restore it to the old estate, and to that end have gathered a multitude of foreign soldiers together, and prepared ships of war;
verses.text: Forasmuch as certain pestilent men have usurped the kingdom of our fathers, and my purpose is to challenge it again, that I may restore it to the old estate, and to that end have gathered a multitude of foreign soldiers together, and prepared ships of war;

verses.raw: My meaning also being to go through the country, that I may be avenged of them that have destroyed it, and made many cities in the kingdom desolate:
verses.text: My meaning also being to go through the country, that I may be avenged of them that have destroyed it, and made many cities in the kingdom desolate:

verses.raw: Now therefore I confirm to you all the oblations which the kings before me granted you, and whatsoever gifts besides they granted.
verses.text: Now therefore I confirm to you all the oblations which the kings before me granted you, and whatsoever gifts besides they granted.

verses.raw: I give you leave also to coin money for your country with your own stamp.
verses.text: I give you leave also to coin money for your country with your own stamp.

verses.raw: And as concerning Jerusalem and the sanctuary, let them be free; and all the armour that you have made, and fortresses that you have built, and keepest in yours hands, let them remain to you.
verses.text: And as concerning Jerusalem and the sanctuary, let them be free; and all the armour that you have made, and fortresses that you have built, and keepest in yours hands, let them remain to you.

verses.raw: And if anything be, or shall be, owing to the king, let it be forgiven you from this time forth for evermore.
verses.text: And if anything be, or shall be, owing to the king, let it be forgiven you from this time forth for evermore.

verses.raw: Furthermore, when we have obtained our kingdom, we will honour you, and your nation, and your temple, with great honour, so that your honour shall be known throughout the world.
verses.text: Furthermore, when we have obtained our kingdom, we will honour you, and your nation, and your temple, with great honour, so that your honour shall be known throughout the world.

verses.raw: In the hundred threescore and fourteenth year went Antiochus into the land of his fathers: at which time all the forces came together to him, so that few were left with Tryphon.
verses.text: In the hundred threescore and fourteenth year went Antiochus into the land of his fathers: at which time all the forces came together to him, so that few were left with Tryphon.

verses.raw: Wherefore being pursued by king Antiochus, he fled to Dora, which lieth by the sea side:
verses.text: Wherefore being pursued by king Antiochus, he fled to Dora, which lieth by the sea side:

verses.raw: For he saw that troubles came upon him all at once, and that his forces had forsaken him.
verses.text: For he saw that troubles came upon him all at once, and that his forces had forsaken him.

verses.raw: Then camped Antiochus against Dora, having with him an hundred and twenty thousand men of war, and eight thousand horsemen.
verses.text: Then camped Antiochus against Dora, having with him an hundred and twenty thousand men of war, and eight thousand horsemen.

verses.raw: And when he had compassed the city round about, and joined ships close to the town on the sea side, he vexed the city by land and by sea, neither suffered he any to go out or in.
verses.text: And when he had compassed the city round about, and joined ships close to the town on the sea side, he vexed the city by land and by sea, neither suffered he any to go out or in.

verses.raw: In the mean season came Numenius and his company from Rome, having letters to the kings and countries; in which were written these things:
verses.text: In the mean season came Numenius and his company from Rome, having letters to the kings and countries; in which were written these things:

verses.raw: Lucius, consul of the Romans to king Ptolemee, greeting:
verses.text: Lucius, consul of the Romans to king Ptolemee, greeting:

verses.raw: The Yahudim (Jews)’ ambassadors, our friends and confederates, came to us to renew the old friendship and league, being sent from Simon the high priest, and from the people of the Yahudim (Jews):
verses.text: The Yahudim’ ambassadors, our friends and confederates, came to us to renew the old friendship and league, being sent from Simon the high priest, and from the people of the Yahudim:

verses.raw: And they brought a shield of gold of a thousand pound.
verses.text: And they brought a shield of gold of a thousand pound.

verses.raw: We thought it good therefore to write to the kings and countries, that they should do them no harm, nor fight against them, their cities, or countries, nor yet aid their enemies against them.
verses.text: We thought it good therefore to write to the kings and countries, that they should do them no harm, nor fight against them, their cities, or countries, nor yet aid their enemies against them.

verses.raw: It seemed also good to us to receive the shield of them.
verses.text: It seemed also good to us to receive the shield of them.

verses.raw: If therefore there be any pestilent fellows, that have fled from their country to you, deliver them to Simon the high priest, that he may punish them according to their own law.
verses.text: If therefore there be any pestilent fellows, that have fled from their country to you, deliver them to Simon the high priest, that he may punish them according to their own law.

verses.raw: The same things wrote he likewise to Demetrius the king, and Attalus, to Ariarathes, and Arsaces,
verses.text: The same things wrote he likewise to Demetrius the king, and Attalus, to Ariarathes, and Arsaces,

verses.raw: And to all the countries and to Sampsames, and the Lacedemonians, and to Delus, and Myndus, and Sicyon, and Caria, and Samos, and Pamphylia, and Lycia, and Halicarnassus, and Rhodus, and Aradus, and Cos, and Side, and Aradus, and Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.
verses.text: And to all the countries and to Sampsames, and the Lacedemonians, and to Delus, and Myndus, and Sicyon, and Caria, and Samos, and Pamphylia, and Lycia, and Halicarnassus, and Rhodus, and Aradus, and Cos, and Side, and Aradus, and Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.

verses.raw: And the copy of this they wrote to Simon the high priest.
verses.text: And the copy of this they wrote to Simon the high priest.

verses.raw: So Antiochus the king camped against Dora the second day, assaulting it continually, and making engines, by which means he shut up Tryphon, that he could neither go out nor in.
verses.text: So Antiochus the king camped against Dora the second day, assaulting it continually, and making engines, by which means he shut up Tryphon, that he could neither go out nor in.

verses.raw: At that time Simon sent him two thousand chosen men to aid him; silver also, and gold, and much armour.
verses.text: At that time Simon sent him two thousand chosen men to aid him; silver also, and gold, and much armour.

verses.raw: Nevertheless he would not receive them, but brake all the covenants which he had made with him afore, and became strange to him.
verses.text: Nevertheless he would not receive them, but brake all the covenants which he had made with him afore, and became strange to him.

verses.raw: Furthermore he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to commune with him, and say, You withhold Joppa and Gazera; with the tower that is in Jerusalem, which are cities of my realm.
verses.text: Furthermore he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to commune with him, and say, You withhold Joppa and Gazera; with the tower that is in Jerusalem, which are cities of my realm.

verses.raw: The borders thereof you have wasted, and done great hurt in the land, and got the dominion of many places within my kingdom.
verses.text: The borders thereof you have wasted, and done great hurt in the land, and got the dominion of many places within my kingdom.

verses.raw: Now therefore deliver the cities which you have taken, and the tributes of the places, of which you have gotten dominion without the borders of Judea:
verses.text: Now therefore deliver the cities which you have taken, and the tributes of the places, of which you have gotten dominion without the borders of Judea:

verses.raw: Or else give me for them five hundred talents of silver; and for the harm that you have done, and the tributes of the cities, other five hundred talents: if not, we will come and fight against you
verses.text: Or else give me for them five hundred talents of silver; and for the harm that you have done, and the tributes of the cities, other five hundred talents: if not, we will come and fight against you

verses.raw: So Athenobius the king’s friend came to Jerusalem: and when he saw the glory of Simon, and the cupboard of gold and silver plate, and his great attendance, he was astonished, and told him the king’s message.
verses.text: So Athenobius the king’s friend came to Jerusalem: and when he saw the glory of Simon, and the cupboard of gold and silver plate, and his great attendance, he was astonished, and told him the king’s message.

verses.raw: Then answered Simon, and said to him, We have neither taken other men’s land, nor holden that which appertaineth to others, but the inheritance of our fathers, which our enemies had wrongfully in possession a certain time.
verses.text: Then answered Simon, and said to him, We have neither taken other men’s land, nor holden that which appertaineth to others, but the inheritance of our fathers, which our enemies had wrongfully in possession a certain time.

verses.raw: Wherefore we, having opportunity, hold the inheritance of our fathers.
verses.text: Wherefore we, having opportunity, hold the inheritance of our fathers.

verses.raw: And whereas you demandest Joppa and Gazera, albeit they did great harm to the people in our country, yet will we give you an hundred talents for them. To this Athenobius answered him not a word;
verses.text: And whereas you demandest Joppa and Gazera, albeit they did great harm to the people in our country, yet will we give you an hundred talents for them. To this Athenobius answered him not a word;

verses.raw: But returned in a rage to the king, and made report to him of these speeches, and of the glory of Simon, and of all that he had seen: whereupon the king was exceeding wroth.
verses.text: But returned in a rage to the king, and made report to him of these speeches, and of the glory of Simon, and of all that he had seen: whereupon the king was exceeding wroth.

verses.raw: In the mean time fled Tryphon by ship to Orthosias.
verses.text: In the mean time fled Tryphon by ship to Orthosias.

verses.raw: Then the king made Cendebeus captain of the sea coast, and gave him an host of footmen and horsemen,
verses.text: Then the king made Cendebeus captain of the sea coast, and gave him an host of footmen and horsemen,

verses.raw: And commanded him to remove his host toward Judea; also he commanded him to build up Cedron, and to fortify the gates, and to war against the people; but as for the king himself, he pursued Tryphon.
verses.text: And commanded him to remove his host toward Judea; also he commanded him to build up Cedron, and to fortify the gates, and to war against the people; but as for the king himself, he pursued Tryphon.

verses.raw: So Cendebeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people and to invade Judea, and to take the people prisoners, and slay them.
verses.text: So Cendebeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people and to invade Judea, and to take the people prisoners, and slay them.

verses.raw: And when he had built up Cedrou, he set horsemen there, and an host of footmen, to the end that issuing out they might make outroads upon the ways of Judea, as the king had commanded him. ⸻
verses.text: And when he had built up Cedrou, he set horsemen there, and an host of footmen, to the end that issuing out they might make outroads upon the ways of Judea, as the king had commanded him. ⸻

verses.raw: Then came up John from Gazera, and told Simon his father what Cendebeus had done.
verses.text: Then came up John from Gazera, and told Simon his father what Cendebeus had done.

verses.raw: Wherefore Simon called his two eldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, I, and my brothers, and my father’s house, have ever from my youth to this day fought against the enemies of Yashar'el (Israel); and things have prospered so well in our hands, that we have delivered Yashar'el (Israel) often.

verses.raw: But now I am old, and you, by the mercy of Yahuah (God), are of a sufficient age: be you instead of me and my brother, and go and fight for our nation, and the help from heaven be with you.

verses.raw: And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money, so that the multitude of their riches, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, was innumerable, and that it was possible to bring all into the king’s hand.
verses.text: And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money, so that the multitude of their riches, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, was innumerable, and that it was possible to bring all into the king’s hand.

verses.raw: Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had shewed him of the money of which he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money.
verses.text: Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had shewed him of the money of which he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money.

verses.raw: So forthwith Heliodorus took his journey; under a colour of visiting the cities of Celosyria and Phenice, but indeed to fulfil the king’s purpose.
verses.text: So forthwith Heliodorus took his journey; under a colour of visiting the cities of Celosyria and Phenice, but indeed to fulfil the king’s purpose.

verses.raw: And when he was come to Jerusalem, and had been courteously received of the high priest of the city, he told him what intelligence was given of the money, and declared wherefore he came, and asked if these things were so indeed.
verses.text: And when he was come to Jerusalem, and had been courteously received of the high priest of the city, he told him what intelligence was given of the money, and declared wherefore he came, and asked if these things were so indeed.

verses.raw: Then the high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children:
verses.text: Then the high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children:

verses.raw: And that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: the sum of which in all was four hundred talents of silver, and two hundred of gold:
verses.text: And that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: the sum of which in all was four hundred talents of silver, and two hundred of gold:

verses.raw: And that it was altogether impossible that such wrongs should be done to them, that had committed it to the holiness of the place, and to the majesty and inviolable sanctity of the temple, honoured over all the world.
verses.text: And that it was altogether impossible that such wrongs should be done to them, that had committed it to the holiness of the place, and to the majesty and inviolable sanctity of the temple, honoured over all the world.

verses.raw: But Heliodorus, because of the king’s commandment given him, said, That in any wise it must be brought into the king’s treasury.
verses.text: But Heliodorus, because of the king’s commandment given him, said, That in any wise it must be brought into the king’s treasury.

verses.raw: So at the day which he appointed he entered in to order this matter: wherefore there was no small agony throughout the whole city.
verses.text: So at the day which he appointed he entered in to order this matter: wherefore there was no small agony throughout the whole city.

verses.raw: But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called to heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to be kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept.
verses.text: But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called to heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to be kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept.

verses.raw: Then whoso had looked the high priest in the face, it would have wounded his heart: for his countenance and the changing of his colour declared the inward agony of his mind.
verses.text: Then whoso had looked the high priest in the face, it would have wounded his heart: for his countenance and the changing of his colour declared the inward agony of his mind.

verses.raw: For the man was so compassed with fear and horror of the body, that it was manifest to them that looked upon him, what sorrow he had now in his heart.
verses.text: For the man was so compassed with fear and horror of the body, that it was manifest to them that looked upon him, what sorrow he had now in his heart.

verses.raw: Others ran flocking out of their houses to the general supplication, because the place was like to come into contempt.
verses.text: Others ran flocking out of their houses to the general supplication, because the place was like to come into contempt.

verses.raw: And the women, girt with sackcloth under their breasts, abounded in the streets, and the virgins that were kept in ran, some to the gates, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows.
verses.text: And the women, girt with sackcloth under their breasts, abounded in the streets, and the virgins that were kept in ran, some to the gates, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows.

verses.raw: And all, holding their hands toward heaven, made supplication.
verses.text: And all, holding their hands toward heaven, made supplication.

verses.raw: Then it would have pitied a man to see the falling down of the multitude of all sorts, and the fear of the high priest being in such an agony.
verses.text: Then it would have pitied a man to see the falling down of the multitude of all sorts, and the fear of the high priest being in such an agony.

verses.raw: They then called upon the Almighty Yahuah (God) to keep the things committed of trust safe and sure for those that had committed them.
verses.text: They then called upon the Almighty Yahuah to keep the things committed of trust safe and sure for those that had committed them.

verses.raw: Nevertheless Heliodorus executed that which was decreed.
verses.text: Nevertheless Heliodorus executed that which was decreed.

verses.raw: Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, Yahuah (God) of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.
verses.text: Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, Yahuah of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of Yahuah, and fainted, and were sore afraid.

verses.raw: For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.
verses.text: For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.

verses.raw: Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.
verses.text: Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.

verses.raw: And Heliodorus fell suddenly to the ground, and was compassed with great darkness: but they that were with him took him up, and put him into a litter.
verses.text: And Heliodorus fell suddenly to the ground, and was compassed with great darkness: but they that were with him took him up, and put him into a litter.

verses.raw: Thus him, that lately came with a great train and with all his guard into the said treasury, they carried out, being unable to help himself with his weapons: and manifestly they acknowledged the power of Yahuah (God).
verses.text: Thus him, that lately came with a great train and with all his guard into the said treasury, they carried out, being unable to help himself with his weapons: and manifestly they acknowledged the power of Yahuah.

verses.raw: For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.
verses.text: For he by the hand of Yahuah was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.

verses.raw: But they praised Yahuah (God), that had miraculously honoured his own place: for the temple; which a little afore was full of fear and trouble, when the Almighty Yahuah (God) appeared, was filled with joy and gladness.
verses.text: But they praised Yahuah, that had miraculously honoured his own place: for the temple; which a little afore was full of fear and trouble, when the Almighty Yahuah appeared, was filled with joy and gladness.

verses.raw: Then straightways certain of Heliodorus’ friends prayed Onias, that he would call upon the Most High to grant him his life, who lay ready to give up the ghost.
verses.text: Then straightways certain of Heliodorus’ friends prayed Onias, that he would call upon the Most High to grant him his life, who lay ready to give up the ghost.

verses.raw: So the high priest, suspecting lest the king should misconceive that some treachery had been done to Heliodorus by the Yahudim (Jews), offered a sacrifice for the health of the man.
verses.text: So the high priest, suspecting lest the king should misconceive that some treachery had been done to Heliodorus by the Yahudim, offered a sacrifice for the health of the man.

verses.raw: Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake Yahuah (God) has granted you life:
verses.text: Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake Yahuah has granted you life:

verses.raw: And seeing that you have been scourged from heaven, declare to all men the mighty power of Yahuah (God). And when they had spoken these words, they appeared no more.
verses.text: And seeing that you have been scourged from heaven, declare to all men the mighty power of Yahuah. And when they had spoken these words, they appeared no more.

verses.raw: So Heliodorus, after he had offered sacrifice to Yahuah (God), and made great vows to him that had saved his life, and saluted Onias, returned with his host to the king.
verses.text: So Heliodorus, after he had offered sacrifice to Yahuah, and made great vows to him that had saved his life, and saluted Onias, returned with his host to the king.

verses.raw: Then testified he to all men the works of the great Yahuah (God), which he had seen with his eyes.
verses.text: Then testified he to all men the works of the great Yahuah, which he had seen with his eyes.

verses.raw: And when the king asked Heliodorus, who might be a fit man to be sent yet once again to Jerusalem, he said,
verses.text: And when the king asked Heliodorus, who might be a fit man to be sent yet once again to Jerusalem, he said,

verses.raw: If you have any enemy or traitor, send him thither, and you shall receive him well scourged, if he escape with his life: for in that place, no doubt, there is an especial power of Yahuah (God).
verses.text: If you have any enemy or traitor, send him thither, and you shall receive him well scourged, if he escape with his life: for in that place, no doubt, there is an especial power of Yahuah.

verses.raw: For he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defendeth it; and he beateth and destroys them that come to hurt it.
verses.text: For he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defendeth it; and he beateth and destroys them that come to hurt it.

verses.raw: And the things concerning Heliodorus, and the keeping of the treasury, fell out on this sort. ⸻
verses.text: And the things concerning Heliodorus, and the keeping of the treasury, fell out on this sort. ⸻

verses.raw: This Simon now, of whom we spoke afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus, and been the worker of these evils.
verses.text: This Simon now, of whom we spoke afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus, and been the worker of these evils.

verses.raw: Thus was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws.
verses.text: Thus was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws.

verses.raw: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed,
verses.text: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed,

verses.raw: Onias seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius, as being the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, did rage, and increase Simon’s malice,
verses.text: Onias seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius, as being the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, did rage, and increase Simon’s malice,

verses.raw: He went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private:
verses.text: He went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private:

verses.raw: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look to it.
verses.text: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look to it.

verses.raw: But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,
verses.text: But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,

verses.raw: Promising to the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:
verses.text: Promising to the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:

verses.raw: Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.
verses.text: Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.

verses.raw: Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.
verses.text: Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.

verses.raw: And the royal privileges granted of special favour to the Yahudim (Jews) by the means of John the father of Eupolemus, who went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, he took away; and putting down the governments which were according to the law, he brought up new customs against the law:
verses.text: And the royal privileges granted of special favour to the Yahudim by the means of John the father of Eupolemus, who went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, he took away; and putting down the governments which were according to the law, he brought up new customs against the law:

verses.raw: For he built gladly a place of exercise under the tower itself, and brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat.
verses.text: For he built gladly a place of exercise under the tower itself, and brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat.

verses.raw: Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;
verses.text: Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;

verses.raw: That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;
verses.text: That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;

verses.raw: Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.
verses.text: Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.

verses.raw: By reason of which sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly, and to whom they desired to be like in all things.
verses.text: By reason of which sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly, and to whom they desired to be like in all things.

verses.raw: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of Yahuah (God): but the time following shall declare these things.
verses.text: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of Yahuah: but the time following shall declare these things.

verses.raw: Now when the game that was used every fifth year was kept at Tyrus, the king being present,
verses.text: Now when the game that was used every fifth year was kept at Tyrus, the king being present,

verses.raw: This ungracious Jason sent special messengers from Jerusalem, who were Antiochians, to carry three hundred drachms of silver to the sacrifice of Hercules, which even the bearers thereof thought fit not to bestow upon the sacrifice, because it was not convenient, but to be reserved for other charges.
verses.text: This ungracious Jason sent special messengers from Jerusalem, who were Antiochians, to carry three hundred drachms of silver to the sacrifice of Hercules, which even the bearers thereof thought fit not to bestow upon the sacrifice, because it was not convenient, but to be reserved for other charges.

verses.raw: This money then, in regard of the sender, was appointed to Hercules’ sacrifice; but because of the bearers thereof, it was employed to the making of gallies.
verses.text: This money then, in regard of the sender, was appointed to Hercules’ sacrifice; but because of the bearers thereof, it was employed to the making of gallies.

verses.raw: Now when Apollonius the son of Menestheus was sent into Egypt for the coronation of king Ptolemeus Philometor, Antiochus, understanding him not to be well affected to his affairs, provided for his own safety: whereupon he came to Joppa, and from thence to Jerusalem:
verses.text: Now when Apollonius the son of Menestheus was sent into Egypt for the coronation of king Ptolemeus Philometor, Antiochus, understanding him not to be well affected to his affairs, provided for his own safety: whereupon he came to Joppa, and from thence to Jerusalem:

verses.raw: Where he was honourably received of Jason, and of the city, and was brought in with torch alight, and with great shoutings: and so afterward went with his host to Phenice.
verses.text: Where he was honourably received of Jason, and of the city, and was brought in with torch alight, and with great shoutings: and so afterward went with his host to Phenice.

verses.raw: Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother, to bear the money to the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters.
verses.text: Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother, to bear the money to the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters.

verses.raw: But he being brought to the presence of the king, when he had magnified him for the glorious appearance of his power, got the priesthood to himself, offering more than Jason by three hundred talents of silver.
verses.text: But he being brought to the presence of the king, when he had magnified him for the glorious appearance of his power, got the priesthood to himself, offering more than Jason by three hundred talents of silver.

verses.raw: So he came with the king’s mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.
verses.text: So he came with the king’s mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.

verses.raw: Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites.
verses.text: Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites.

verses.raw: So Menelaus got the principality: but as for the money that he had promised to the king, he took no good order for it, albeit Sostratis the ruler of the castle required it:
verses.text: So Menelaus got the principality: but as for the money that he had promised to the king, he took no good order for it, albeit Sostratis the ruler of the castle required it:

verses.raw: For to him appertained the gathering of the customs. Wherefore they were both called before the king.
verses.text: For to him appertained the gathering of the customs. Wherefore they were both called before the king.

verses.raw: Now Menelaus left his brother Lysimachus in his stead in the priesthood; and Sostratus left Crates, who was governor of the Cyprians.
verses.text: Now Menelaus left his brother Lysimachus in his stead in the priesthood; and Sostratus left Crates, who was governor of the Cyprians.

verses.raw: While those things were in doing, they of Tarsus and Mallos made insurrection, because they were given to the king’s concubine, called Antiochus.
verses.text: While those things were in doing, they of Tarsus and Mallos made insurrection, because they were given to the king’s concubine, called Antiochus.

verses.raw: Then came the king in all haste to appease matters, leaving Andronicus, a man in authority, for his deputy.
verses.text: Then came the king in all haste to appease matters, leaving Andronicus, a man in authority, for his deputy.

verses.raw: Now Menelaus, supposing that he had gotten a convenient time, stole certain vessels of gold out of the temple, and gave some of them to Andronicus, and some he sold into Tyrus and the cities round about.
verses.text: Now Menelaus, supposing that he had gotten a convenient time, stole certain vessels of gold out of the temple, and gave some of them to Andronicus, and some he sold into Tyrus and the cities round about.

verses.raw: Which when Onias knew of a surety, he reproved him, and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne, that lieth by Antiochia.
verses.text: Which when Onias knew of a surety, he reproved him, and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne, that lieth by Antiochia.

verses.raw: Wherefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed him to get Onias into his hands; who being persuaded to it, and coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice.
verses.text: Wherefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed him to get Onias into his hands; who being persuaded to it, and coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice.

verses.raw: For the which cause not only the Yahudim (Jews), but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man.
verses.text: For the which cause not only the Yahudim, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man.

verses.raw: And when the king was come again from the places about Cilicia, the Yahudim (Jews) that were in the city, and certain of the Greeks that abhorred the fact also, complained because Onias was slain without cause.
verses.text: And when the king was come again from the places about Cilicia, the Yahudim that were in the city, and certain of the Greeks that abhorred the fact also, complained because Onias was slain without cause.

verses.raw: Therefore Antiochus was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead.
verses.text: Therefore Antiochus was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead.

verses.raw: And being kindled with anger, forthwith he took away Andronicus his purple, and rent off his clothes, and leading him through the whole city to that very place, where he had committed impiety against Onias, there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus Yahuah (God) rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.
verses.text: And being kindled with anger, forthwith he took away Andronicus his purple, and rent off his clothes, and leading him through the whole city to that very place, where he had committed impiety against Onias, there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus Yahuah rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.

verses.raw: Now when many sacrileges had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the fruit thereof was spread abroad, the multitude gathered themselves together against Lysimachus, many vessels of gold being already carried away.
verses.text: Now when many sacrileges had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the fruit thereof was spread abroad, the multitude gathered themselves together against Lysimachus, many vessels of gold being already carried away.

verses.raw: Whereupon the common people rising, and being filled with rage, Lysimachus armed about three thousand men, and began first to offer violence; one Auranus being the leader, a man far gone in years, and no less in folly.
verses.text: Whereupon the common people rising, and being filled with rage, Lysimachus armed about three thousand men, and began first to offer violence; one Auranus being the leader, a man far gone in years, and no less in folly.

verses.raw: They then seeing the attempt of Lysimachus, some of them caught stones, some clubs, others taking handfuls of dust, that was next at hand, cast them all together upon Lysimachus, and those that set upon them.
verses.text: They then seeing the attempt of Lysimachus, some of them caught stones, some clubs, others taking handfuls of dust, that was next at hand, cast them all together upon Lysimachus, and those that set upon them.

verses.raw: Thus many of them they wounded, and some they struck to the ground, and all of them they forced to flee: but as for the churchrobber himself, him they killed beside the treasury.
verses.text: Thus many of them they wounded, and some they struck to the ground, and all of them they forced to flee: but as for the churchrobber himself, him they killed beside the treasury.

verses.raw: Of these matters therefore there was an accusation laid against Menelaus.
verses.text: Of these matters therefore there was an accusation laid against Menelaus.

verses.raw: Now when the king came to Tyrus, three men that were sent from the senate pleaded the cause before him:
verses.text: Now when the king came to Tyrus, three men that were sent from the senate pleaded the cause before him:

verses.raw: But Menelaus, being now convicted, promised Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes to give him much money, if he would pacify the king toward him.
verses.text: But Menelaus, being now convicted, promised Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes to give him much money, if he would pacify the king toward him.

verses.raw: Whereupon Ptolemee taking the king aside into a certain gallery, as it were to take the air, brought him to be of another mind:
verses.text: Whereupon Ptolemee taking the king aside into a certain gallery, as it were to take the air, brought him to be of another mind:

verses.raw: Insomuch that he discharged Menelaus from the accusations, who notwithstanding was cause of all the mischief: and those poor men, who, if they had told their cause, yes, before the Scythians, should have been judged innocent, them he condemned to death.
verses.text: Insomuch that he discharged Menelaus from the accusations, who notwithstanding was cause of all the mischief: and those poor men, who, if they had told their cause, yes, before the Scythians, should have been judged innocent, them he condemned to death.

verses.raw: Thus they that followed the matter for the city, and for the people, and for the holy vessels, did soon suffer unjust punishment.
verses.text: Thus they that followed the matter for the city, and for the people, and for the holy vessels, did soon suffer unjust punishment.
