verses.raw: Wherefore even they of Tyrus, moved with hatred of that wicked deed, caused them to be honourably buried.
verses.text: Wherefore even they of Tyrus, moved with hatred of that wicked deed, caused them to be honourably buried.

verses.raw: And so through the covetousness of them that were of power Menelaus remained still in authority, increasing in malice, and being a great traitor to the citizens. ⸻
verses.text: And so through the covetousness of them that were of power Menelaus remained still in authority, increasing in malice, and being a great traitor to the citizens. ⸻

verses.raw: About the same time Antiochus prepared his second voyage into Egypt:
verses.text: About the same time Antiochus prepared his second voyage into Egypt:

verses.raw: And then it happened, that through all the city, for the space almost of forty days, there were seen horsemen running in the air, in cloth of gold, and armed with lances, like a band of soldiers,
verses.text: And then it happened, that through all the city, for the space almost of forty days, there were seen horsemen running in the air, in cloth of gold, and armed with lances, like a band of soldiers,

verses.raw: And troops of horsemen in array, encountering and running one against another, with shaking of shields, and multitude of pikes, and drawing of swords, and casting of darts, and glittering of golden ornaments, and harness of all sorts.
verses.text: And troops of horsemen in array, encountering and running one against another, with shaking of shields, and multitude of pikes, and drawing of swords, and casting of darts, and glittering of golden ornaments, and harness of all sorts.

verses.raw: Wherefore every man prayed that that apparition might turn to good.
verses.text: Wherefore every man prayed that that apparition might turn to good.

verses.raw: Now when there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men, and suddenly made an assault upon the city; and they that were upon the walls being put back, and the city at length taken, Menelaus fled into the castle:
verses.text: Now when there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men, and suddenly made an assault upon the city; and they that were upon the walls being put back, and the city at length taken, Menelaus fled into the castle:

verses.raw: But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.
verses.text: But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.

verses.raw: Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites.
verses.text: Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites.

verses.raw: In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt.
verses.text: In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt.

verses.raw: Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred:
verses.text: Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred:

verses.raw: And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.
verses.text: And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.

verses.raw: Now when this that was done came to the king’s ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms,
verses.text: Now when this that was done came to the king’s ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms,

verses.raw: And commanded his men of war not to spare such as they met, and to slay such as went up upon the houses.
verses.text: And commanded his men of war not to spare such as they met, and to slay such as went up upon the houses.

verses.raw: Thus there was killing of young and old, making away of men, women, and children, slaying of virgins and infants.
verses.text: Thus there was killing of young and old, making away of men, women, and children, slaying of virgins and infants.

verses.raw: And there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, of which forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.
verses.text: And there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, of which forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.

verses.raw: Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide:
verses.text: Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide:

verses.raw: And taking the holy vessels with polluted hands, and with profane hands pulling down the things that were dedicated by other kings to the augmentation and glory and honour of the place, he gave them away.
verses.text: And taking the holy vessels with polluted hands, and with profane hands pulling down the things that were dedicated by other kings to the augmentation and glory and honour of the place, he gave them away.

verses.raw: And so haughty was Antiochus in mind, that he considered not that Yahuah (God) was angry for a while for the sins of them that dwelt in the city, and therefore his eye was not upon the place.
verses.text: And so haughty was Antiochus in mind, that he considered not that Yahuah was angry for a while for the sins of them that dwelt in the city, and therefore his eye was not upon the place.

verses.raw: For had they not been formerly wrapped in many sins, this man, as soon as he had come, had forthwith been scourged, and put back from his presumption, as Heliodorus was, whom Seleucus the king sent to view the treasury.
verses.text: For had they not been formerly wrapped in many sins, this man, as soon as he had come, had forthwith been scourged, and put back from his presumption, as Heliodorus was, whom Seleucus the king sent to view the treasury.

verses.raw: Nevertheless Yahuah (God) did not choose the people for the place’s sake, but the place for the people’s sake.
verses.text: Nevertheless Yahuah did not choose the people for the place’s sake, but the place for the people’s sake.

verses.raw: And therefore the place itself, that was partaker with them of the adversity that happened to the nation, did afterward communicate in the benefits sent from Yahuah (God): and as it was forsaken in the wrath of the Almighty, so again, the great Yahuah (God) being reconciled, it was set up with all glory.
verses.text: And therefore the place itself, that was partaker with them of the adversity that happened to the nation, did afterward communicate in the benefits sent from Yahuah: and as it was forsaken in the wrath of the Almighty, so again, the great Yahuah being reconciled, it was set up with all glory.

verses.raw: So when Antiochus had carried out of the temple a thousand and eight hundred talents, he departed in all haste to Antiochia, weening in his pride to make the land navigable, and the sea passable by foot: such was the haughtiness of his mind.
verses.text: So when Antiochus had carried out of the temple a thousand and eight hundred talents, he departed in all haste to Antiochia, weening in his pride to make the land navigable, and the sea passable by foot: such was the haughtiness of his mind.

verses.raw: And he left governors to vex the nation: at Jerusalem, Philip, for his country a Phrygian, and for manners more barbarous than he that set him there;
verses.text: And he left governors to vex the nation: at Jerusalem, Philip, for his country a Phrygian, and for manners more barbarous than he that set him there;

verses.raw: And at Garizim, Andronicus; and besides, Menelaus, who worse than all the rest bare an heavy hand over the citizens, having a malicious mind against his countrymen the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: And at Garizim, Andronicus; and besides, Menelaus, who worse than all the rest bare an heavy hand over the citizens, having a malicious mind against his countrymen the Yahudim.

verses.raw: He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius with an army of two and twenty thousand, commanding him to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort:
verses.text: He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius with an army of two and twenty thousand, commanding him to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort:

verses.raw: Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Yahudim (Jews) keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves.
verses.text: Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Yahudim keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves.

verses.raw: And so he slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the sabbath, and running through the city with weapons slew great multitudes.
verses.text: And so he slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the sabbath, and running through the city with weapons slew great multitudes.

verses.raw: But Judas Maccabeus with nine others, or thereabout, withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, with his company, who fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution. ⸻
verses.text: But Judas Maccabeus with nine others, or thereabout, withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, with his company, who fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution. ⸻

verses.raw: Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Yahudim (Jews) to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of Yahuah (God):
verses.text: Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Yahudim to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of Yahuah:

verses.raw: And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.
verses.text: And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.

verses.raw: The coming in of this mischief was sore and grievous to the people:
verses.text: The coming in of this mischief was sore and grievous to the people:

verses.raw: For the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful.
verses.text: For the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful.

verses.raw: The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbiddeth.
verses.text: The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbiddeth.

verses.raw: Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Yahudi (Jew).
verses.text: Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Yahudi.

verses.raw: And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices; and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Yahudim (Jews) were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.
verses.text: And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices; and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Yahudim were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.

verses.raw: Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Yahudim (Jews), that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices:
verses.text: Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Yahudim, that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices:

verses.raw: And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.
verses.text: And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.

verses.raw: For there were two women brought, who had circumcised their children; whom when they had openly led round about the city, the babes hanging at their breasts, they cast them down headlong from the wall.
verses.text: For there were two women brought, who had circumcised their children; whom when they had openly led round about the city, the babes hanging at their breasts, they cast them down headlong from the wall.

verses.raw: And others, that had run together into caves near by, to keep the sabbath day secretly, being discovered by Philip, were all burnt together, because they made a conscience to help themselves for the honour of the most sacred day.
verses.text: And others, that had run together into caves near by, to keep the sabbath day secretly, being discovered by Philip, were all burnt together, because they made a conscience to help themselves for the honour of the most sacred day.

verses.raw: Now I beseech those that read this book, that they be not discouraged for these calamities, but that they judge those punishments not to be for destruction, but for a chastening of our nation.
verses.text: Now I beseech those that read this book, that they be not discouraged for these calamities, but that they judge those punishments not to be for destruction, but for a chastening of our nation.

verses.raw: For it is a token of his great goodness, when wicked doers are not suffered any long time, but forthwith punished.
verses.text: For it is a token of his great goodness, when wicked doers are not suffered any long time, but forthwith punished.

verses.raw: For not as with other nations, whom Yahuah (God) patiently forbeareth to punish, till they be come to the fulness of their sins, so dealeth he with us,
verses.text: For not as with other nations, whom Yahuah patiently forbeareth to punish, till they be come to the fulness of their sins, so dealeth he with us,

verses.raw: Lest that, being come to the height of sin, afterwards he should take vengeance of us.
verses.text: Lest that, being come to the height of sin, afterwards he should take vengeance of us.

verses.raw: And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: and though he punish with adversity, yet does he never forsake his people.
verses.text: And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: and though he punish with adversity, yet does he never forsake his people.

verses.raw: But let this that we have spoken be for a warning to us. And now will we come to the declaring of the matter in a few words.
verses.text: But let this that we have spoken be for a warning to us. And now will we come to the declaring of the matter in a few words.

verses.raw: Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine’s flesh.
verses.text: Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine’s flesh.

verses.raw: But he, choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment,
verses.text: But he, choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment,

verses.raw: As it behoved them to come, that are resolute to stand out against such things, as are not lawful for love of life to be tasted.
verses.text: As it behoved them to come, that are resolute to stand out against such things, as are not lawful for love of life to be tasted.

verses.raw: But they that had the charge of that wicked feast, for the old acquaintance they had with the man, taking him aside, besought him to bring flesh of his own provision, such as was lawful for him to use, and make as if he did eat of the flesh taken from the sacrifice commanded by the king;
verses.text: But they that had the charge of that wicked feast, for the old acquaintance they had with the man, taking him aside, besought him to bring flesh of his own provision, such as was lawful for him to use, and make as if he did eat of the flesh taken from the sacrifice commanded by the king;

verses.raw: That in so doing he might be delivered from death, and for the old friendship with them find favour.
verses.text: That in so doing he might be delivered from death, and for the old friendship with them find favour.

verses.raw: But he began to consider discreetly, and as became his age, and the excellency of his ancient years, and the honour of his gray head, on which was come, and his most honest education from a child, or rather the holy law made and given by Yahuah (God): therefore he answered accordingly, and willed them straightways to send him to the grave.
verses.text: But he began to consider discreetly, and as became his age, and the excellency of his ancient years, and the honour of his gray head, on which was come, and his most honest education from a child, or rather the holy law made and given by Yahuah: therefore he answered accordingly, and willed them straightways to send him to the grave.

verses.raw: For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, by which many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion;
verses.text: For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, by which many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion;

verses.raw: And so they through my hypocrisy, and desire to live a little time and a moment longer, should be deceived by me, and I get a stain to my old age, and make it abominable.
verses.text: And so they through my hypocrisy, and desire to live a little time and a moment longer, should be deceived by me, and I get a stain to my old age, and make it abominable.

verses.raw: For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead.
verses.text: For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead.

verses.raw: Wherefore now, manfully changing this life, I will shew myself such an one as my age requires,
verses.text: Wherefore now, manfully changing this life, I will shew myself such an one as my age requires,

verses.raw: And leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honourable and holy laws. And when he had said these words, immediately he went to the torment:
verses.text: And leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honourable and holy laws. And when he had said these words, immediately he went to the torment:

verses.raw: They that led him changing the good will they bare him a little before into hatred, because the foresaid speeches proceeded, as they thought, from a desperate mind.
verses.text: They that led him changing the good will they bare him a little before into hatred, because the foresaid speeches proceeded, as they thought, from a desperate mind.

verses.raw: But when he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest to Yahuah (God), that has the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him.
verses.text: But when he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest to Yahuah, that has the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him.

verses.raw: And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only to young men, but to all his nation. ⸻
verses.text: And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only to young men, but to all his nation. ⸻

verses.raw: It came to pass also, that seven brothers with their mother were taken, and compelled by the king against the law to taste swine’s flesh, and were tormented with scourges and whips.
verses.text: It came to pass also, that seven brothers with their mother were taken, and compelled by the king against the law to taste swine’s flesh, and were tormented with scourges and whips.

verses.raw: But one of them that spoke first said thus, What wouldest you ask or learn of us? we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.
verses.text: But one of them that spoke first said thus, What wouldest you ask or learn of us? we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.

verses.raw: Then the king, being in a rage, commanded pans and caldrons to be made hot:
verses.text: Then the king, being in a rage, commanded pans and caldrons to be made hot:

verses.raw: Which forthwith being heated, he commanded to cut out the tongue of him that spoke first, and to cut off the utmost parts of his body, the rest of his brothers and his mother looking on.
verses.text: Which forthwith being heated, he commanded to cut out the tongue of him that spoke first, and to cut off the utmost parts of his body, the rest of his brothers and his mother looking on.

verses.raw: Now when he was thus maimed in all his members, he commanded him being yet alive to be brought to the fire, and to be fried in the pan: and as the vapour of the pan was for a good space dispersed, they exhorted one another with the mother to die manfully, saying thus,
verses.text: Now when he was thus maimed in all his members, he commanded him being yet alive to be brought to the fire, and to be fried in the pan: and as the vapour of the pan was for a good space dispersed, they exhorted one another with the mother to die manfully, saying thus,

verses.raw: Yahuah (God) looketh upon us, and in truth has comfort in us, as Moses in his song, which witnessed to their faces, declared, saying, And he shall be comforted in his servants.
verses.text: Yahuah looketh upon us, and in truth has comfort in us, as Moses in his song, which witnessed to their faces, declared, saying, And he shall be comforted in his servants.

verses.raw: So when the first was dead after this manner, they brought the second to make him a mocking stock: and when they had pulled off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him, Will you eat, before you be punished throughout every member of your body?
verses.text: So when the first was dead after this manner, they brought the second to make him a mocking stock: and when they had pulled off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him, Will you eat, before you be punished throughout every member of your body?

verses.raw: But he answered in his own language, and said, No. Wherefore he also received the next torment in order, as the former did.
verses.text: But he answered in his own language, and said, No. Wherefore he also received the next torment in order, as the former did.

verses.raw: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.
verses.text: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.

verses.raw: After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully.
verses.text: After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully.

verses.raw: And said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.
verses.text: And said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.

verses.raw: Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.
verses.text: Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.

verses.raw: Now when this man was dead also, they tormented and mangled the fourth in like manner.
verses.text: Now when this man was dead also, they tormented and mangled the fourth in like manner.

verses.raw: So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from Yahuah (God) to be raised up again by him: as for you, you shall have no resurrection to life.
verses.text: So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from Yahuah to be raised up again by him: as for you, you shall have no resurrection to life.

verses.raw: Afterward they brought the fifth also, and mangled him.
verses.text: Afterward they brought the fifth also, and mangled him.

verses.raw: Then looked he to the king, and said, You have power over men, you are corruptible, you do what you will; yet think not that our nation is forsaken of Yahuah (God);
verses.text: Then looked he to the king, and said, You have power over men, you are corruptible, you do what you will; yet think not that our nation is forsaken of Yahuah;

verses.raw: But abide a while, and behold his great power, how he will torment you and your seed.
verses.text: But abide a while, and behold his great power, how he will torment you and your seed.

verses.raw: After him also they brought the sixth, who being ready to die said, Be not deceived without cause: for we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against our Elohim (God): therefore marvellous things are done to us.
verses.text: After him also they brought the sixth, who being ready to die said, Be not deceived without cause: for we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against our Elohim: therefore marvellous things are done to us.

verses.raw: But think not you, that takest in hand to strive against Yahuah (God), that you shall escape unpunished.
verses.text: But think not you, that takest in hand to strive against Yahuah, that you shall escape unpunished.

verses.raw: But the mother was marvellous above all, and worthy of honourable memory: for when she saw her seven sons slain within the space of one day, she bare it with a good courage, because of the hope that she had in Yahuah (God).
verses.text: But the mother was marvellous above all, and worthy of honourable memory: for when she saw her seven sons slain within the space of one day, she bare it with a good courage, because of the hope that she had in Yahuah.

verses.raw: Yea, she exhorted every one of them in her own language, filled with courageous spirits; and stirring up her womanish thoughts with a manly stomach, she said to them,
verses.text: Yea, she exhorted every one of them in her own language, filled with courageous spirits; and stirring up her womanish thoughts with a manly stomach, she said to them,

verses.raw: I cannot tell how you came into my womb: for I neither gave you breath nor life, neither was it I that formed the members of every one of you;
verses.text: I cannot tell how you came into my womb: for I neither gave you breath nor life, neither was it I that formed the members of every one of you;

verses.raw: But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.
verses.text: But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.

verses.raw: Now Antiochus, thinking himself despised, and suspecting it to be a reproachful speech, while the youngest was yet alive, did not only exhort him by words, but also assured him with oaths, that he would make him both a rich and a happy man, if he would turn from the laws of his fathers; and that also he would take him for his friend, and trust him with affairs.
verses.text: Now Antiochus, thinking himself despised, and suspecting it to be a reproachful speech, while the youngest was yet alive, did not only exhort him by words, but also assured him with oaths, that he would make him both a rich and a happy man, if he would turn from the laws of his fathers; and that also he would take him for his friend, and trust him with affairs.

verses.raw: But when the young man would in no case hearken to him, the king called his mother, and exhorted her that she would counsel the young man to save his life.
verses.text: But when the young man would in no case hearken to him, the king called his mother, and exhorted her that she would counsel the young man to save his life.

verses.raw: And when he had exhorted her with many words, she promised him that she would counsel her son.
verses.text: And when he had exhorted her with many words, she promised him that she would counsel her son.

verses.raw: But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spoke in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare you nine months in my womb, and gave you suck three years, and nourished you, and brought you up to this age, and endured the troubles of education.
verses.text: But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spoke in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare you nine months in my womb, and gave you suck three years, and nourished you, and brought you up to this age, and endured the troubles of education.

verses.raw: I beseech you, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is in it, and consider that Yahuah (God) made them of things that were not; and so was mankind made likewise.
verses.text: I beseech you, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is in it, and consider that Yahuah made them of things that were not; and so was mankind made likewise.

verses.raw: Fear not this tormentor, but, being worthy of your brothers, take your death that I may receive you again in mercy with your brothers.
verses.text: Fear not this tormentor, but, being worthy of your brothers, take your death that I may receive you again in mercy with your brothers.

verses.raw: Whiles she was yet speaking these words, the young man said, Whom wait you for? I will not obey the king’s commandment: but I will obey the commandment of the law that was given to our fathers by Moses.
verses.text: Whiles she was yet speaking these words, the young man said, Whom wait you for? I will not obey the king’s commandment: but I will obey the commandment of the law that was given to our fathers by Moses.

verses.raw: And you, that have been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews, shall not escape the hands of Yahuah (God).
verses.text: And you, that have been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews, shall not escape the hands of Yahuah.

verses.raw: For we suffer because of our sins.
verses.text: For we suffer because of our sins.

verses.raw: And though the living Yahuah (God) be angry with us a little while for our chastening and correction, yet shall he be at one again with his servants.
verses.text: And though the living Yahuah be angry with us a little while for our chastening and correction, yet shall he be at one again with his servants.

verses.raw: But you, O godless man, and of all other most wicked, be not lifted up without a cause, nor puffed up with uncertain hopes, lifting up your hand against the servants of Yahuah (God):
verses.text: But you, O godless man, and of all other most wicked, be not lifted up without a cause, nor puffed up with uncertain hopes, lifting up your hand against the servants of Yahuah:

verses.raw: For you have not yet escaped the judgment of Almighty Yahuah (God), who seeth all things.
verses.text: For you have not yet escaped the judgment of Almighty Yahuah, who seeth all things.

verses.raw: For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.
verses.text: For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah, shall receive just punishment for your pride.

verses.raw: But I, as my brothers, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching Yahuah (God) that he would speedily be merciful to our nation; and that you by torments and plagues may confess, that he alone is Yahuah (God);
verses.text: But I, as my brothers, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching Yahuah that he would speedily be merciful to our nation; and that you by torments and plagues may confess, that he alone is Yahuah;

verses.raw: And that in me and my brothers the wrath of the Almighty, which is justly brought upon our nation, may cease.
verses.text: And that in me and my brothers the wrath of the Almighty, which is justly brought upon our nation, may cease.

verses.raw: Then the king being in a rage, handed him worse than all the rest, and took it grievously that he was mocked.
verses.text: Then the king being in a rage, handed him worse than all the rest, and took it grievously that he was mocked.

verses.raw: So this man died undefiled, and put his whole trust in Yahuah (God).
verses.text: So this man died undefiled, and put his whole trust in Yahuah.

verses.raw: Last of all after the sons the mother died.
verses.text: Last of all after the sons the mother died.

verses.raw: Let this be enough now to have spoken concerning the idolatrous feasts, and the extreme tortures. ⸻
verses.text: Let this be enough now to have spoken concerning the idolatrous feasts, and the extreme tortures. ⸻

verses.raw: Then Judas Maccabeus, and they that were with him, went privily into the towns, and called their kinsfolks together, and took to them all such as continued in the Yahudim (Jews)’ religion, and assembled about six thousand men.
verses.text: Then Judas Maccabeus, and they that were with him, went privily into the towns, and called their kinsfolks together, and took to them all such as continued in the Yahudim’ religion, and assembled about six thousand men.

verses.raw: And they called upon Yahuah (God), that he would look upon the people that was trodden down of all; and also pity the temple profaned of ungodly men;
verses.text: And they called upon Yahuah, that he would look upon the people that was trodden down of all; and also pity the temple profaned of ungodly men;

verses.raw: And that he would have compassion upon the city, sore defaced, and ready to be made even with the ground; and hear the blood that cried to him,
verses.text: And that he would have compassion upon the city, sore defaced, and ready to be made even with the ground; and hear the blood that cried to him,

verses.raw: And remember the wicked slaughter of harmless infants, and the blasphemies committed against his name; and that he would shew his hatred against the wicked.
verses.text: And remember the wicked slaughter of harmless infants, and the blasphemies committed against his name; and that he would shew his hatred against the wicked.

verses.raw: Now when Maccabeus had his company about him, he could not be withstood by the heathen: for the wrath of Yahuah (God) was turned into mercy.
verses.text: Now when Maccabeus had his company about him, he could not be withstood by the heathen: for the wrath of Yahuah was turned into mercy.

verses.raw: Therefore he came at unawares, and burnt up towns and cities, and got into his hands the most commodious places, and overcame and put to flight no small number of his enemies.
verses.text: Therefore he came at unawares, and burnt up towns and cities, and got into his hands the most commodious places, and overcame and put to flight no small number of his enemies.

verses.raw: But specially took he advantage of the night for such privy attempts, insomuch that the fruit of his holiness was spread every where.
verses.text: But specially took he advantage of the night for such privy attempts, insomuch that the fruit of his holiness was spread every where.

verses.raw: So when Philip saw that this man increased by little and little, and that things prospered with him still more and more, he wrote to Ptolemeus, the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, to yield more aid to the king’s affairs.
verses.text: So when Philip saw that this man increased by little and little, and that things prospered with him still more and more, he wrote to Ptolemeus, the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, to yield more aid to the king’s affairs.

verses.raw: Then forthwith choosing Nicanor the son of Patroclus, one of his special friends, he sent him with no fewer than twenty thousand of all nations under him, to root out the whole generation of the Yahudim (Jews); and with him he joined also Gorgias a captain, who in matters of war had great experience.
verses.text: Then forthwith choosing Nicanor the son of Patroclus, one of his special friends, he sent him with no fewer than twenty thousand of all nations under him, to root out the whole generation of the Yahudim; and with him he joined also Gorgias a captain, who in matters of war had great experience.

verses.raw: So Nicanor undertook to make so much money of the captive Yahudim (Jews), as should defray the tribute of two thousand talents, which the king was to pay to the Romans.
verses.text: So Nicanor undertook to make so much money of the captive Yahudim, as should defray the tribute of two thousand talents, which the king was to pay to the Romans.

verses.raw: Wherefore immediately he sent to the cities upon the sea coast, proclaiming a sale of the captive Yahudim (Jews), and promising that they should have fourscore and ten bodies for one talent, not expecting the vengeance that was to follow upon him from the Almighty Yahuah (God).
verses.text: Wherefore immediately he sent to the cities upon the sea coast, proclaiming a sale of the captive Yahudim, and promising that they should have fourscore and ten bodies for one talent, not expecting the vengeance that was to follow upon him from the Almighty Yahuah.

verses.raw: Now when word was brought to Judas of Nicanor’s coming, and he had imparted to those that were with him that the army was at hand,
verses.text: Now when word was brought to Judas of Nicanor’s coming, and he had imparted to those that were with him that the army was at hand,

verses.raw: They that were fearful, and distrusted the justice of Yahuah (God), fled, and conveyed themselves away.
verses.text: They that were fearful, and distrusted the justice of Yahuah, fled, and conveyed themselves away.

verses.raw: Others sold all that they had left, and withal besought Yahuah (God) to deliver them, sold by the wicked Nicanor before they met together:
verses.text: Others sold all that they had left, and withal besought Yahuah to deliver them, sold by the wicked Nicanor before they met together:

verses.raw: And if not for their own sakes, yet for the covenants he had made with their fathers, and for his holy and glorious name’s sake, by which they were called.
verses.text: And if not for their own sakes, yet for the covenants he had made with their fathers, and for his holy and glorious name’s sake, by which they were called.

verses.raw: So Maccabeus called his men together to the number of six thousand, and exhorted them not to be stricken with terror of the enemy, nor to fear the great multitude of the heathen, who came wrongly against them; but to fight manfully,
verses.text: So Maccabeus called his men together to the number of six thousand, and exhorted them not to be stricken with terror of the enemy, nor to fear the great multitude of the heathen, who came wrongly against them; but to fight manfully,

verses.raw: And to set before their eyes the injury that they had unjustly done to the holy place, and the cruel handling of the city, of which they made a mockery, and also the taking away of the government of their forefathers:
verses.text: And to set before their eyes the injury that they had unjustly done to the holy place, and the cruel handling of the city, of which they made a mockery, and also the taking away of the government of their forefathers:

verses.raw: For they, said he, trust in their weapons and boldness; but our confidence is in the Almighty who at a beck can cast down both them that come against us, and also all the world.
verses.text: For they, said he, trust in their weapons and boldness; but our confidence is in the Almighty who at a beck can cast down both them that come against us, and also all the world.

verses.raw: Moreover, he recounted to them what helps their forefathers had found, and how they were delivered, when under Sennacherib an hundred fourscore and five thousand perished.
verses.text: Moreover, he recounted to them what helps their forefathers had found, and how they were delivered, when under Sennacherib an hundred fourscore and five thousand perished.

verses.raw: And he told them of the battle that they had in Babylon with the Galatians, how they came but eight thousand in all to the business, with four thousand Macedonians, and that the Macedonians being perplexed, the eight thousand destroyed an hundred and twenty thousand because of the help that they had from heaven, and so received a great booty.
verses.text: And he told them of the battle that they had in Babylon with the Galatians, how they came but eight thousand in all to the business, with four thousand Macedonians, and that the Macedonians being perplexed, the eight thousand destroyed an hundred and twenty thousand because of the help that they had from heaven, and so received a great booty.

verses.raw: Thus when he had made them bold with these words, and ready to die for the law and the country, he divided his army into four parts;
verses.text: Thus when he had made them bold with these words, and ready to die for the law and the country, he divided his army into four parts;

verses.raw: And joined with himself his own brothers, leaders of each band, to wit Simon, and Joseph, and Jonathan, giving each one fifteen hundred men.
verses.text: And joined with himself his own brothers, leaders of each band, to wit Simon, and Joseph, and Jonathan, giving each one fifteen hundred men.

verses.raw: Also he appointed Eleazar to read the holy book: and when he had given them this watchword, The help of Yahuah (God); himself leading the first band,
verses.text: Also he appointed Eleazar to read the holy book: and when he had given them this watchword, The help of Yahuah; himself leading the first band,

verses.raw: And by the help of the Almighty they slew above nine thousand of their enemies, and wounded and maimed the most part of Nicanor’s host, and so put all to flight;
verses.text: And by the help of the Almighty they slew above nine thousand of their enemies, and wounded and maimed the most part of Nicanor’s host, and so put all to flight;

verses.raw: And took their money that came to buy them, and pursued them far: but lacking time they returned:
verses.text: And took their money that came to buy them, and pursued them far: but lacking time they returned:

verses.raw: For it was the day before the sabbath, and therefore they would no longer pursue them.
verses.text: For it was the day before the sabbath, and therefore they would no longer pursue them.

verses.raw: So when they had gathered their armour together, and spoiled their enemies, they occupied themselves about the sabbath, yielding exceeding praise and thanks to Yahuah (God), who had preserved them to that day, which was the beginning of mercy distilling upon them.
verses.text: So when they had gathered their armour together, and spoiled their enemies, they occupied themselves about the sabbath, yielding exceeding praise and thanks to Yahuah, who had preserved them to that day, which was the beginning of mercy distilling upon them.

verses.raw: And after the sabbath, when they had given part of the spoils to the maimed, and the widows, and orphans, the residue they divided among themselves and their servants.
verses.text: And after the sabbath, when they had given part of the spoils to the maimed, and the widows, and orphans, the residue they divided among themselves and their servants.

verses.raw: When this was done, and they had made a common supplication, they besought the merciful Yahuah (God) to be reconciled with his servants for ever.
verses.text: When this was done, and they had made a common supplication, they besought the merciful Yahuah to be reconciled with his servants for ever.

verses.raw: Moreover of those that were with Timotheus and Bacchides, who fought against them, they slew above twenty thousand, and very easily got high and strong holds, and divided among themselves many spoils more, and made the maimed, orphans, widows, yes, and the aged also, equal in spoils with themselves.
verses.text: Moreover of those that were with Timotheus and Bacchides, who fought against them, they slew above twenty thousand, and very easily got high and strong holds, and divided among themselves many spoils more, and made the maimed, orphans, widows, yes, and the aged also, equal in spoils with themselves.

verses.raw: And when they had gathered their armour together, they laid them up all carefully in convenient places, and the remnant of the spoils they brought to Jerusalem.
verses.text: And when they had gathered their armour together, they laid them up all carefully in convenient places, and the remnant of the spoils they brought to Jerusalem.

verses.raw: They slew also Philarches, that wicked person, who was with Timotheus, and had annoyed the Yahudim (Jews) many ways.
verses.text: They slew also Philarches, that wicked person, who was with Timotheus, and had annoyed the Yahudim many ways.

verses.raw: Furthermore at such time as they kept the feast for the victory in their country they burnt Callisthenes, that had set fire upon the holy gates, who had fled into a little house; and so he received a reward meet for his wickedness.
verses.text: Furthermore at such time as they kept the feast for the victory in their country they burnt Callisthenes, that had set fire upon the holy gates, who had fled into a little house; and so he received a reward meet for his wickedness.

verses.raw: As for that most ungracious Nicanor, who had brought a thousand merchants to buy the Yahudim (Jews),
verses.text: As for that most ungracious Nicanor, who had brought a thousand merchants to buy the Yahudim,

verses.raw: He was through the help of Yahuah (God) brought down by them, of whom he made least account; and putting off his glorious apparel, and discharging his company, he came like a fugitive servant through the midland to Antioch having very great dishonour, for that his host was destroyed.
verses.text: He was through the help of Yahuah brought down by them, of whom he made least account; and putting off his glorious apparel, and discharging his company, he came like a fugitive servant through the midland to Antioch having very great dishonour, for that his host was destroyed.

verses.raw: Thus he, that took upon him to make good to the Romans their tribute by means of captives in Jerusalem, told abroad, that the Yahudim (Jews) had Yahuah (God) to fight for them, and therefore they could not be hurt, because they followed the laws that he gave them. ⸻
verses.text: Thus he, that took upon him to make good to the Romans their tribute by means of captives in Jerusalem, told abroad, that the Yahudim had Yahuah to fight for them, and therefore they could not be hurt, because they followed the laws that he gave them. ⸻

verses.raw: About that time came Antiochus with dishonour out of the country of Persia
verses.text: About that time came Antiochus with dishonour out of the country of Persia

verses.raw: For he had entered the city called Persepolis, and went about to rob the temple, and to hold the city; whereupon the multitude running to defend themselves with their weapons put them to flight; and so it happened, that Antiochus being put to flight of the inhabitants returned with shame.
verses.text: For he had entered the city called Persepolis, and went about to rob the temple, and to hold the city; whereupon the multitude running to defend themselves with their weapons put them to flight; and so it happened, that Antiochus being put to flight of the inhabitants returned with shame.

verses.raw: Now when he came to Ecbatane, news was brought him what had happened to Nicanor and Timotheus.
verses.text: Now when he came to Ecbatane, news was brought him what had happened to Nicanor and Timotheus.

verses.raw: Then swelling with anger. he thought to avenge upon the Yahudim (Jews) the disgrace done to him by those that made him flee. Therefore commanded he his chariotman to drive without ceasing, and to dispatch the journey, the judgment of Yahuah (God) now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: Then swelling with anger. he thought to avenge upon the Yahudim the disgrace done to him by those that made him flee. Therefore commanded he his chariotman to drive without ceasing, and to dispatch the journey, the judgment of Yahuah now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: But Yahuah (God) Almighty, Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;
verses.text: But Yahuah Almighty, Yahuah of Yashar'el, struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;

verses.raw: And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.
verses.text: And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.

verses.raw: Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Yahudim (Jews), and commanding to haste the journey: but it came to pass that he fell down from his chariot, carried violently; so that having a sore fall, all the members of his body were much pained.
verses.text: Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Yahudim, and commanding to haste the journey: but it came to pass that he fell down from his chariot, carried violently; so that having a sore fall, all the members of his body were much pained.

verses.raw: And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground, and carried in an horselitter, shewing forth to all the manifest power of Yahuah (God).
verses.text: And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground, and carried in an horselitter, shewing forth to all the manifest power of Yahuah.

verses.raw: So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.
verses.text: So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.

verses.raw: And the man, that thought a little afore he could reach to the stars of heaven, no man could endure to carry for his intolerable stink.
verses.text: And the man, that thought a little afore he could reach to the stars of heaven, no man could endure to carry for his intolerable stink.

verses.raw: Here therefore, being plagued, he began to leave off his great pride, and to come to the knowledge of himself by the scourge of Yahuah (God), his pain increasing every moment.
verses.text: Here therefore, being plagued, he began to leave off his great pride, and to come to the knowledge of himself by the scourge of Yahuah, his pain increasing every moment.

verses.raw: And when he himself could not abide his own smell, he said these words, It is meet to be subject to Yahuah (God), and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were Yahuah (God).
verses.text: And when he himself could not abide his own smell, he said these words, It is meet to be subject to Yahuah, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were Yahuah.

verses.raw: This wicked person vowed also to Yahuah (God), who now no more would have mercy upon him, saying thus,
verses.text: This wicked person vowed also to Yahuah, who now no more would have mercy upon him, saying thus,

verses.raw: That the holy city (to the which he was going in haste to lay it even with the ground, and to make it a common buryingplace,) he would set at liberty:
verses.text: That the holy city (to the which he was going in haste to lay it even with the ground, and to make it a common buryingplace,) he would set at liberty:

verses.raw: And as touching the Yahudim (Jews), whom he had judged not worthy so much as to be buried, but to be cast out with their children to be devoured of the fowls and wild beasts, he would make them all equals to the citizens of Athens:
verses.text: And as touching the Yahudim, whom he had judged not worthy so much as to be buried, but to be cast out with their children to be devoured of the fowls and wild beasts, he would make them all equals to the citizens of Athens:

verses.raw: And the holy temple, which before he had spoiled, he would garnish with goodly gifts, and restore all the holy vessels with many more, and out of his own revenue defray the charges belonging to the sacrifices:
verses.text: And the holy temple, which before he had spoiled, he would garnish with goodly gifts, and restore all the holy vessels with many more, and out of his own revenue defray the charges belonging to the sacrifices:

verses.raw: Yea, and that also he would become a Yahudi (Jew) himself, and go through all the world that was inhabited, and declare the power of Yahuah (God).
verses.text: Yea, and that also he would become a Yahudi himself, and go through all the world that was inhabited, and declare the power of Yahuah.

verses.raw: But for all this his pains would not cease: for the just judgment of Yahuah (God) was come upon him: therefore despairing of his health, he wrote to the Yahudim (Jews) the letter underwritten, containing the form of a supplication, after this manner:
verses.text: But for all this his pains would not cease: for the just judgment of Yahuah was come upon him: therefore despairing of his health, he wrote to the Yahudim the letter underwritten, containing the form of a supplication, after this manner:

verses.raw: Antiochus, king and governor, to the good Yahudim (Jews) his citizens wisheth much joy, health, and prosperity:
verses.text: Antiochus, king and governor, to the good Yahudim his citizens wisheth much joy, health, and prosperity:

verses.raw: If you and your children fare well, and your affairs be to your contentment, I give very great thanks to Yahuah (God), having my hope in heaven.
verses.text: If you and your children fare well, and your affairs be to your contentment, I give very great thanks to Yahuah, having my hope in heaven.

verses.raw: As for me, I was weak, or else I would have remembered kindly your honour and good will returning out of Persia, and being taken with a grievous disease, I thought it necessary to care for the common safety of all:
verses.text: As for me, I was weak, or else I would have remembered kindly your honour and good will returning out of Persia, and being taken with a grievous disease, I thought it necessary to care for the common safety of all:

verses.raw: Not distrusting my health, but having great hope to escape this sickness.
verses.text: Not distrusting my health, but having great hope to escape this sickness.

verses.raw: But considering that even my father, at what time he led an army into the high countries. appointed a successor,
verses.text: But considering that even my father, at what time he led an army into the high countries. appointed a successor,

verses.raw: To the end that, if any thing fell out contrary to expectation, or if any tidings were brought that were grievous, they of the land, knowing to whom the state was left, might not be troubled:
verses.text: To the end that, if any thing fell out contrary to expectation, or if any tidings were brought that were grievous, they of the land, knowing to whom the state was left, might not be troubled:

verses.raw: Again, considering how that the princes that are borderers and neighbours to my kingdom wait for opportunities, and expect what shall be the event. I have appointed my son Antiochus king, whom I often committed and commended to many of you, when I went up into the high provinces; to whom I have written as followeth:
verses.text: Again, considering how that the princes that are borderers and neighbours to my kingdom wait for opportunities, and expect what shall be the event. I have appointed my son Antiochus king, whom I often committed and commended to many of you, when I went up into the high provinces; to whom I have written as followeth:

verses.raw: Therefore I pray and request you to remember the benefits that I have done to you generally, and in special, and that every man will be still faithful to me and my son.
verses.text: Therefore I pray and request you to remember the benefits that I have done to you generally, and in special, and that every man will be still faithful to me and my son.

verses.raw: For I am persuaded that he understanding my mind will favourably and graciously yield to your desires.
verses.text: For I am persuaded that he understanding my mind will favourably and graciously yield to your desires.

verses.raw: Thus the murderer and blasphemer having suffered most grievously, as he entreated other men, so died he a miserable death in a strange country in the mountains.
verses.text: Thus the murderer and blasphemer having suffered most grievously, as he entreated other men, so died he a miserable death in a strange country in the mountains.

verses.raw: And Philip, that was brought up with him, carried away his body, who also fearing the son of Antiochus went into Egypt to Ptolemeus Philometor. ⸻
verses.text: And Philip, that was brought up with him, carried away his body, who also fearing the son of Antiochus went into Egypt to Ptolemeus Philometor. ⸻

verses.raw: Now Maccabeus and his company, Yahuah (God) guiding them, recovered the temple and the city:
verses.text: Now Maccabeus and his company, Yahuah guiding them, recovered the temple and the city:

verses.raw: But the altars which the heathen had built in the open street, and also the chapels, they pulled down.
verses.text: But the altars which the heathen had built in the open street, and also the chapels, they pulled down.

verses.raw: And having cleansed the temple they made another altar, and striking stones they took fire out of them, and offered a sacrifice after two years, and set forth incense, and lights, and shewbread.
verses.text: And having cleansed the temple they made another altar, and striking stones they took fire out of them, and offered a sacrifice after two years, and set forth incense, and lights, and shewbread.

verses.raw: When that was done, they fell flat down, and besought Yahuah (God) that they might come no more into such troubles; but if they sinned any more against him, that he himself would chasten them with mercy, and that they might not be delivered to the blasphemous and barbarous nations.
verses.text: When that was done, they fell flat down, and besought Yahuah that they might come no more into such troubles; but if they sinned any more against him, that he himself would chasten them with mercy, and that they might not be delivered to the blasphemous and barbarous nations.

verses.raw: Now upon the same day that the strangers profaned the temple, on the very same day it was cleansed again, even the five and twentieth day of the same month, which is Casleu.
verses.text: Now upon the same day that the strangers profaned the temple, on the very same day it was cleansed again, even the five and twentieth day of the same month, which is Casleu.

verses.raw: And they kept the eight days with gladness, as in the feast of the tabernacles, remembering that not long afore they had held the feast of the tabernacles, when as they wandered in the mountains and dens like beasts.
verses.text: And they kept the eight days with gladness, as in the feast of the tabernacles, remembering that not long afore they had held the feast of the tabernacles, when as they wandered in the mountains and dens like beasts.

verses.raw: Therefore they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms to him that had given them good success in cleansing his place.
verses.text: Therefore they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms to him that had given them good success in cleansing his place.

verses.raw: They ordained also by a common statute and decree, That every year those days should be kept of the whole nation of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: They ordained also by a common statute and decree, That every year those days should be kept of the whole nation of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: And this was the end of Antiochus, called Epiphanes.
verses.text: And this was the end of Antiochus, called Epiphanes.

verses.raw: Now will we declare the acts of Antiochus Eupator, who was the son of this wicked man, gathering briefly the calamities of the wars.
verses.text: Now will we declare the acts of Antiochus Eupator, who was the son of this wicked man, gathering briefly the calamities of the wars.

verses.raw: So when he was come to the crown, he set one Lysias over the affairs of his realm, and appointed him his chief governor of Celosyria and Phenice.
verses.text: So when he was come to the crown, he set one Lysias over the affairs of his realm, and appointed him his chief governor of Celosyria and Phenice.

verses.raw: For Ptolemeus, that was called Macron, choosing rather to do justice to the Yahudim (Jews) for the wrong that had been done to them, endeavoured to continue peace with them.
verses.text: For Ptolemeus, that was called Macron, choosing rather to do justice to the Yahudim for the wrong that had been done to them, endeavoured to continue peace with them.

verses.raw: Whereupon being accused of the king’s friends before Eupator, and called traitor at every word because he had left Cyprus, that Philometor had committed to him, and departed to Antiochus Epiphanes, and seeing that he was in no honourable place, he was so discouraged, that he poisoned himself and died.
verses.text: Whereupon being accused of the king’s friends before Eupator, and called traitor at every word because he had left Cyprus, that Philometor had committed to him, and departed to Antiochus Epiphanes, and seeing that he was in no honourable place, he was so discouraged, that he poisoned himself and died.

verses.raw: But when Gorgias was governor of the holds, he hired soldiers, and nourished war continually with the Yahudim (Jews):
verses.text: But when Gorgias was governor of the holds, he hired soldiers, and nourished war continually with the Yahudim:

verses.raw: And therewithall the Idumeans, having gotten into their hands the most commodious holds, kept the Yahudim (Jews) occupied, and receiving those that were banished from Jerusalem, they went about to nourish war.
verses.text: And therewithall the Idumeans, having gotten into their hands the most commodious holds, kept the Yahudim occupied, and receiving those that were banished from Jerusalem, they went about to nourish war.

verses.raw: Then they that were with Maccabeus made supplication, and besought Yahuah (God) that he would be their helper; and so they ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans,
verses.text: Then they that were with Maccabeus made supplication, and besought Yahuah that he would be their helper; and so they ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans,

verses.raw: And assaulting them strongly, they won the holds, and kept off all that fought upon the wall, and slew all that fell into their hands, and killed no fewer than twenty thousand.
verses.text: And assaulting them strongly, they won the holds, and kept off all that fought upon the wall, and slew all that fell into their hands, and killed no fewer than twenty thousand.

verses.raw: And because certain, who were no less than nine thousand, were fled together into two very strong castles, having all manner of things convenient to sustain the siege,
verses.text: And because certain, who were no less than nine thousand, were fled together into two very strong castles, having all manner of things convenient to sustain the siege,

verses.raw: Maccabeus left Simon and Joseph, and Zaccheus also, and them that were with him, who were enough to besiege them, and departed himself to those places which more needed his help.
verses.text: Maccabeus left Simon and Joseph, and Zaccheus also, and them that were with him, who were enough to besiege them, and departed himself to those places which more needed his help.

verses.raw: Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape.
verses.text: Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape.

verses.raw: But when it was told Maccabeus what was done, he called the governors of the people together, and accused those men, that they had sold their brothers for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.
verses.text: But when it was told Maccabeus what was done, he called the governors of the people together, and accused those men, that they had sold their brothers for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.

verses.raw: So he slew those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles.
verses.text: So he slew those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles.

verses.raw: And having good success with his weapons in all things he took in hand, he slew in the two holds more than twenty thousand.
verses.text: And having good success with his weapons in all things he took in hand, he slew in the two holds more than twenty thousand.

verses.raw: Now Timotheus, whom the Yahudim (Jews) had overcome before, when he had gathered a great multitude of foreign forces, and horses out of Asia not a few, came as though he would take Jewry by force of arms.
verses.text: Now Timotheus, whom the Yahudim had overcome before, when he had gathered a great multitude of foreign forces, and horses out of Asia not a few, came as though he would take Jewry by force of arms.

verses.raw: But when he drew near, they that were with Maccabeus turned themselves to pray to Yahuah (God), and sprinkled earth upon their heads, and girded their loins with sackcloth,
verses.text: But when he drew near, they that were with Maccabeus turned themselves to pray to Yahuah, and sprinkled earth upon their heads, and girded their loins with sackcloth,

verses.raw: And fell down at the foot of the altar, and besought him to be merciful to them, and to be an enemy to their enemies, and an adversary to their adversaries, as the law declareth.
verses.text: And fell down at the foot of the altar, and besought him to be merciful to them, and to be an enemy to their enemies, and an adversary to their adversaries, as the law declareth.

verses.raw: So after the prayer they took their weapons, and went on further from the city: and when they drew near to their enemies, they kept by themselves.
verses.text: So after the prayer they took their weapons, and went on further from the city: and when they drew near to their enemies, they kept by themselves.

verses.raw: Now the sun being newly risen, they joined both together; the one part having together with their virtue their refuge also to Yahuah (God) for a pledge of their success and victory: the other side making their rage leader of their battle
verses.text: Now the sun being newly risen, they joined both together; the one part having together with their virtue their refuge also to Yahuah for a pledge of their success and victory: the other side making their rage leader of their battle

verses.raw: But when the battle waxed strong, there appeared to the enemies from heaven five comely men upon horses, with bridles of gold, and two of them led the Yahudim (Jews),
verses.text: But when the battle waxed strong, there appeared to the enemies from heaven five comely men upon horses, with bridles of gold, and two of them led the Yahudim,

verses.raw: And took Maccabeus between them, and covered him on every side weapons, and kept him safe, but shot arrows and lightnings against the enemies: so that being confounded with blindness, and full of trouble, they were killed.
verses.text: And took Maccabeus between them, and covered him on every side weapons, and kept him safe, but shot arrows and lightnings against the enemies: so that being confounded with blindness, and full of trouble, they were killed.

verses.raw: And there were slain of footmen twenty thousand and five hundred, and six hundred horsemen.
verses.text: And there were slain of footmen twenty thousand and five hundred, and six hundred horsemen.

verses.raw: As for Timotheus himself, he fled into a very strong hold, called Gawra, where Chereas was governor.
verses.text: As for Timotheus himself, he fled into a very strong hold, called Gawra, where Chereas was governor.

verses.raw: But they that were with Maccabeus laid siege against the fortress courageously four days.
verses.text: But they that were with Maccabeus laid siege against the fortress courageously four days.

verses.raw: And they that were within, trusting to the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly, and uttered wicked words.
verses.text: And they that were within, trusting to the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly, and uttered wicked words.

verses.raw: Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus’ company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal.
verses.text: Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus’ company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal.

verses.raw: Others likewise ascending after them, whiles they were busied with them that were within, burnt the towers, and kindling fires burnt the blasphemers alive; and others broke open the gates, and, having received in the rest of the army, took the city,
verses.text: Others likewise ascending after them, whiles they were busied with them that were within, burnt the towers, and kindling fires burnt the blasphemers alive; and others broke open the gates, and, having received in the rest of the army, took the city,

verses.raw: And killed Timotheus, that was hid in a certain pit, and Chereas his brother, with Apollophanes.
verses.text: And killed Timotheus, that was hid in a certain pit, and Chereas his brother, with Apollophanes.

verses.raw: When this was done, they praised Yahuah (God) with psalms and thanksgiving, who had done so great things for Yashar'el (Israel), and given them the victory. ⸻
verses.text: When this was done, they praised Yahuah with psalms and thanksgiving, who had done so great things for Yashar'el, and given them the victory. ⸻

verses.raw: Not long after this, Lysias the king’s protector and cousin, who also managed the affairs, took sore displeasure for the things that were done.
verses.text: Not long after this, Lysias the king’s protector and cousin, who also managed the affairs, took sore displeasure for the things that were done.

verses.raw: And when he had gathered about fourscore thousand with all the horsemen, he came against the Yahudim (Jews), thinking to make the city an habitation of the Gentiles,
verses.text: And when he had gathered about fourscore thousand with all the horsemen, he came against the Yahudim, thinking to make the city an habitation of the Gentiles,

verses.raw: And to make a gain of the temple, as of the other chapels of the heathen, and to set the high priesthood to sale every year:
verses.text: And to make a gain of the temple, as of the other chapels of the heathen, and to set the high priesthood to sale every year:

verses.raw: Not at all considering the power of Yahuah (God) but puffed up with his ten thousands of footmen, and his thousands of horsemen, and his fourscore elephants.
verses.text: Not at all considering the power of Yahuah but puffed up with his ten thousands of footmen, and his thousands of horsemen, and his fourscore elephants.

verses.raw: So he came to Judea, and drew near to Bethsura, which was a strong town, but distant from Jerusalem about five furlongs, and he laid sore siege to it.
verses.text: So he came to Judea, and drew near to Bethsura, which was a strong town, but distant from Jerusalem about five furlongs, and he laid sore siege to it.

verses.raw: Now when they that were with Maccabeus heard that he besieged the holds, they and all the people with lamentation and tears besought Yahuah (God) that he would send a good angel to deliver Yashar'el (Israel).
verses.text: Now when they that were with Maccabeus heard that he besieged the holds, they and all the people with lamentation and tears besought Yahuah that he would send a good angel to deliver Yashar'el.

verses.raw: Then Maccabeus himself first of all took weapons, exhorting the other that they would jeopard themselves together with him to help their brothers: so they went forth together with a willing mind.
verses.text: Then Maccabeus himself first of all took weapons, exhorting the other that they would jeopard themselves together with him to help their brothers: so they went forth together with a willing mind.

verses.raw: And as they were at Jerusalem, there appeared before them on horseback one in white clothing, shaking his armour of gold.
verses.text: And as they were at Jerusalem, there appeared before them on horseback one in white clothing, shaking his armour of gold.

verses.raw: Then they praised the merciful Yahuah (God) all together, and took heart, insomuch that they were ready not only to fight with men, but with most cruel beasts, and to pierce through walls of iron.
verses.text: Then they praised the merciful Yahuah all together, and took heart, insomuch that they were ready not only to fight with men, but with most cruel beasts, and to pierce through walls of iron.

verses.raw: Thus they marched forward in their armour, having an helper from heaven: for Yahuah (God) was merciful to them
verses.text: Thus they marched forward in their armour, having an helper from heaven: for Yahuah was merciful to them

verses.raw: And giving a charge upon their enemies like lions, they slew eleven thousand footmen, and sixteen hundred horsemen, and put all the other to flight.
verses.text: And giving a charge upon their enemies like lions, they slew eleven thousand footmen, and sixteen hundred horsemen, and put all the other to flight.

verses.raw: Many of them also being wounded escaped naked; and Lysias himself fled away shamefully, and so escaped.
verses.text: Many of them also being wounded escaped naked; and Lysias himself fled away shamefully, and so escaped.

verses.raw: Who, as he was a man of understanding, casting with himself what loss he had had, and considering that the Hebrews could not be overcome, because the Almighty Yahuah (God) helped them, he sent to them,
verses.text: Who, as he was a man of understanding, casting with himself what loss he had had, and considering that the Hebrews could not be overcome, because the Almighty Yahuah helped them, he sent to them,

verses.raw: And persuaded them to agree to all reasonable conditions, and promised that he would persuade the king that he must needs be a friend to them.
verses.text: And persuaded them to agree to all reasonable conditions, and promised that he would persuade the king that he must needs be a friend to them.
