verses.raw: Then Maccabeus consented to all that Lysias desired, being careful of the common good; and whatsoever Maccabeus wrote to Lysias concerning the Yahudim (Jews), the king granted it.
verses.text: Then Maccabeus consented to all that Lysias desired, being careful of the common good; and whatsoever Maccabeus wrote to Lysias concerning the Yahudim, the king granted it.

verses.raw: For there were letters written to the Yahudim (Jews) from Lysias to this effect: Lysias to the people of the Yahudim (Jews) sends greeting:
verses.text: For there were letters written to the Yahudim from Lysias to this effect: Lysias to the people of the Yahudim sends greeting:

verses.raw: John and Absolom, who were sent from you, delivered me the petition subscribed, and made request for the performance of the contents thereof.
verses.text: John and Absolom, who were sent from you, delivered me the petition subscribed, and made request for the performance of the contents thereof.

verses.raw: Therefore what things soever were meet to be reported to the king, I have declared them, and he has granted as much as might be.
verses.text: Therefore what things soever were meet to be reported to the king, I have declared them, and he has granted as much as might be.

verses.raw: And if then you will keep yourselves loyal to the state, hereafter also will I endeavour to be a means of your good.
verses.text: And if then you will keep yourselves loyal to the state, hereafter also will I endeavour to be a means of your good.

verses.raw: But of the particulars I have given order both to these and the other that came from me, to commune with you.
verses.text: But of the particulars I have given order both to these and the other that came from me, to commune with you.

verses.raw: Fare you well. The hundred and eight and fortieth year, the four and twentieth day of the month Dioscorinthius.
verses.text: Fare you well. The hundred and eight and fortieth year, the four and twentieth day of the month Dioscorinthius.

verses.raw: Now the king’s letter contained these words: King Antiochus to his brother Lysias sends greeting:
verses.text: Now the king’s letter contained these words: King Antiochus to his brother Lysias sends greeting:

verses.raw: Since our father is translated to the gods, our will is, that they that are in our realm live quietly, that every one may attend upon his own affairs.
verses.text: Since our father is translated to the gods, our will is, that they that are in our realm live quietly, that every one may attend upon his own affairs.

verses.raw: We understand also that the Yahudim (Jews) would not consent to our father, for to be brought to the custom of the Gentiles, but had rather keep their own manner of living: for the which cause they require of us, that we should suffer them to live after their own laws.
verses.text: We understand also that the Yahudim would not consent to our father, for to be brought to the custom of the Gentiles, but had rather keep their own manner of living: for the which cause they require of us, that we should suffer them to live after their own laws.

verses.raw: Wherefore our mind is, that this nation shall be in rest, and we have determined to restore them their temple, that they may live according to the customs of their forefathers.
verses.text: Wherefore our mind is, that this nation shall be in rest, and we have determined to restore them their temple, that they may live according to the customs of their forefathers.

verses.raw: You shall do well therefore to send to them, and grant them peace, that when they are certified of our mind, they may be of good comfort, and ever go cheerfully about their own affairs.
verses.text: You shall do well therefore to send to them, and grant them peace, that when they are certified of our mind, they may be of good comfort, and ever go cheerfully about their own affairs.

verses.raw: And the letter of the king to the nation of the Yahudim (Jews) was after this manner: King Antiochus sends greeting to the council, and the rest of the Yahudim (Jews):
verses.text: And the letter of the king to the nation of the Yahudim was after this manner: King Antiochus sends greeting to the council, and the rest of the Yahudim:

verses.raw: If you fare well, we have our desire; we are also in good health.
verses.text: If you fare well, we have our desire; we are also in good health.

verses.raw: Menelaus declared to us, that your desire was to return home, and to follow your own business:
verses.text: Menelaus declared to us, that your desire was to return home, and to follow your own business:

verses.raw: Wherefore they that will depart shall have safe conduct till the thirtieth day of Xanthicus with security.
verses.text: Wherefore they that will depart shall have safe conduct till the thirtieth day of Xanthicus with security.

verses.raw: And the Yahudim (Jews) shall use their own kind of meats and laws, as before; and none of them any manner of ways shall be molested for things ignorantly done.
verses.text: And the Yahudim shall use their own kind of meats and laws, as before; and none of them any manner of ways shall be molested for things ignorantly done.

verses.raw: I have sent also Menelaus, that he may comfort you.
verses.text: I have sent also Menelaus, that he may comfort you.

verses.raw: Fare you well. In the hundred forty and eighth year, and the fifteenth day of the month Xanthicus.
verses.text: Fare you well. In the hundred forty and eighth year, and the fifteenth day of the month Xanthicus.

verses.raw: The Romans also sent to them a letter containing these words: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manlius, ambassadors of the Romans, send greeting to the people of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: The Romans also sent to them a letter containing these words: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manlius, ambassadors of the Romans, send greeting to the people of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: Whatsoever Lysias the king’s cousin has granted, with it we also are well pleased.
verses.text: Whatsoever Lysias the king’s cousin has granted, with it we also are well pleased.

verses.raw: But touching such things as he judged to be referred to the king, after you have advised thereof, send one forthwith, that we may declare as it is convenient for you: for we are now going to Antioch.
verses.text: But touching such things as he judged to be referred to the king, after you have advised thereof, send one forthwith, that we may declare as it is convenient for you: for we are now going to Antioch.

verses.raw: Therefore send some with speed, that we may know what is your mind.
verses.text: Therefore send some with speed, that we may know what is your mind.

verses.raw: Farewell. This hundred and eight and fortieth year, the fifteenth day of the month Xanthicus. ⸻
verses.text: Farewell. This hundred and eight and fortieth year, the fifteenth day of the month Xanthicus. ⸻

verses.raw: When these covenants were made, Lysias went to the king, and the Yahudim (Jews) were about their husbandry.
verses.text: When these covenants were made, Lysias went to the king, and the Yahudim were about their husbandry.

verses.raw: But of the governours of several places, Timotheus, and Apollonius the son of Genneus, also Hieronymus, and Demophon, and beside them Nicanor the governor of Cyprus, would not suffer them to be quiet and live in peace.
verses.text: But of the governours of several places, Timotheus, and Apollonius the son of Genneus, also Hieronymus, and Demophon, and beside them Nicanor the governor of Cyprus, would not suffer them to be quiet and live in peace.

verses.raw: The men of Joppa also did such an ungodly deed: they prayed the Yahudim (Jews) that dwelt among them to go with their wives and children into the boats which they had prepared, as though they had meant them no hurt.
verses.text: The men of Joppa also did such an ungodly deed: they prayed the Yahudim that dwelt among them to go with their wives and children into the boats which they had prepared, as though they had meant them no hurt.

verses.raw: Who accepted of it according to the common decree of the city, as being desirous to live in peace, and suspecting nothing: but when they were gone forth into the deep, they drowned no less than two hundred of them.
verses.text: Who accepted of it according to the common decree of the city, as being desirous to live in peace, and suspecting nothing: but when they were gone forth into the deep, they drowned no less than two hundred of them.

verses.raw: When Judas heard of this cruelty done to his countrymen, he commanded those that were with him to make them ready.
verses.text: When Judas heard of this cruelty done to his countrymen, he commanded those that were with him to make them ready.

verses.raw: And calling upon Yahuah (God) the righteous Judge, he came against those murderers of his brothers, and burnt the haven by night, and set the boats on fire, and those that fled thither he slew.
verses.text: And calling upon Yahuah the righteous Judge, he came against those murderers of his brothers, and burnt the haven by night, and set the boats on fire, and those that fled thither he slew.

verses.raw: And when the town was shut up, he went backward, as if he would return to root out all them of the city of Joppa.
verses.text: And when the town was shut up, he went backward, as if he would return to root out all them of the city of Joppa.

verses.raw: But when he heard that the Jamnites were minded to do in like manner to the Yahudim (Jews) that dwelt among them,
verses.text: But when he heard that the Jamnites were minded to do in like manner to the Yahudim that dwelt among them,

verses.raw: He came upon the Jamnites also by night, and set fire on the haven and the navy, so that the light of the fire was seen at Jerusalem two hundred and forty furlongs off.
verses.text: He came upon the Jamnites also by night, and set fire on the haven and the navy, so that the light of the fire was seen at Jerusalem two hundred and forty furlongs off.

verses.raw: Now when they were gone from thence nine furlongs in their journey toward Timotheus, no fewer than five thousand men on foot and five hundred horsemen of the Arabians set upon him.
verses.text: Now when they were gone from thence nine furlongs in their journey toward Timotheus, no fewer than five thousand men on foot and five hundred horsemen of the Arabians set upon him.

verses.raw: Whereupon there was a very sore battle; but Judas’ side by the help of Yahuah (God) got the victory; so that the Nomades of Arabia, being overcome, besought Judas for peace, promising both to give him cattle, and to pleasure him otherwise.
verses.text: Whereupon there was a very sore battle; but Judas’ side by the help of Yahuah got the victory; so that the Nomades of Arabia, being overcome, besought Judas for peace, promising both to give him cattle, and to pleasure him otherwise.

verses.raw: Then Judas, thinking indeed that they would be profitable in many things, granted them peace: whereupon they shook hands, and so they departed to their tents.
verses.text: Then Judas, thinking indeed that they would be profitable in many things, granted them peace: whereupon they shook hands, and so they departed to their tents.

verses.raw: He went also about to make a bridge to a certain strong city, which was fenced about with walls, and inhabited by people of divers countries; and the name of it was Caspis.
verses.text: He went also about to make a bridge to a certain strong city, which was fenced about with walls, and inhabited by people of divers countries; and the name of it was Caspis.

verses.raw: But they that were within it put such trust in the strength of the walls and provision of victuals, that they behaved themselves rudely toward them that were with Judas, railing and blaspheming, and uttering such words as were not to be spoken.
verses.text: But they that were within it put such trust in the strength of the walls and provision of victuals, that they behaved themselves rudely toward them that were with Judas, railing and blaspheming, and uttering such words as were not to be spoken.

verses.raw: Wherefore Judas with his company, calling upon the great Yahuah (God) of the world, who without rams or engines of war did cast down Jericho in the time of Joshua, gave a fierce assault against the walls,
verses.text: Wherefore Judas with his company, calling upon the great Yahuah of the world, who without rams or engines of war did cast down Jericho in the time of Joshua, gave a fierce assault against the walls,

verses.raw: And took the city by the will of Yahuah (God), and made unspeakable slaughters, insomuch that a lake two furlongs broad near adjoining to it, being filled full, was seen running with blood.
verses.text: And took the city by the will of Yahuah, and made unspeakable slaughters, insomuch that a lake two furlongs broad near adjoining to it, being filled full, was seen running with blood.

verses.raw: Then departed they from thence seven hundred and fifty furlongs, and came to Characa to the Yahudim (Jews) that are called Tubieni.
verses.text: Then departed they from thence seven hundred and fifty furlongs, and came to Characa to the Yahudim that are called Tubieni.

verses.raw: But as for Timotheus, they found him not in the places: for before he had dispatched any thing, he departed from thence, having left a very strong garrison in a certain hold.
verses.text: But as for Timotheus, they found him not in the places: for before he had dispatched any thing, he departed from thence, having left a very strong garrison in a certain hold.

verses.raw: Howbeit Dositheus and Sosipater, who were of Maccabeus’ captains, went forth, and slew those that Timotheus had left in the fortress, above ten thousand men.
verses.text: Howbeit Dositheus and Sosipater, who were of Maccabeus’ captains, went forth, and slew those that Timotheus had left in the fortress, above ten thousand men.

verses.raw: And Maccabeus ranged his army by bands, and set them over the bands, and went against Timotheus, who had about him an hundred and twenty thousand men of foot, and two thousand and five hundred horsemen.
verses.text: And Maccabeus ranged his army by bands, and set them over the bands, and went against Timotheus, who had about him an hundred and twenty thousand men of foot, and two thousand and five hundred horsemen.

verses.raw: Now when Timotheus had knowledge of Judas’ coming, he sent the women and children and the other baggage to a fortress called Carnion: for the town was hard to besiege, and uneasy to come to, by reason of the straitness of all the places.
verses.text: Now when Timotheus had knowledge of Judas’ coming, he sent the women and children and the other baggage to a fortress called Carnion: for the town was hard to besiege, and uneasy to come to, by reason of the straitness of all the places.

verses.raw: But when Judas his first band came in sight, the enemies, being struck with fear and terror through the appearing of him who seeth all things, fled amain, one running into this way, another that way, so as that they were often hurt of their own men, and wounded with the points of their own swords.
verses.text: But when Judas his first band came in sight, the enemies, being struck with fear and terror through the appearing of him who seeth all things, fled amain, one running into this way, another that way, so as that they were often hurt of their own men, and wounded with the points of their own swords.

verses.raw: Judas also was very earnest in pursuing them, killing those wicked wretches, of whom he slew about thirty thousand men.
verses.text: Judas also was very earnest in pursuing them, killing those wicked wretches, of whom he slew about thirty thousand men.

verses.raw: Moreover Timotheus himself fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he besought with much craft to let him go with his life, because he had many of the Yahudim (Jews)’ parents, and the brothers of some of them, who, if they put him to death, should not be regarded.
verses.text: Moreover Timotheus himself fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he besought with much craft to let him go with his life, because he had many of the Yahudim’ parents, and the brothers of some of them, who, if they put him to death, should not be regarded.

verses.raw: So when he had assured them with many words that he would restore them without hurt, according to the agreement, they let him go for the saving of their brothers.
verses.text: So when he had assured them with many words that he would restore them without hurt, according to the agreement, they let him go for the saving of their brothers.

verses.raw: Then Maccabeus marched forth to Carnion, and to the temple of Atargatis, and there he slew five and twenty thousand persons.
verses.text: Then Maccabeus marched forth to Carnion, and to the temple of Atargatis, and there he slew five and twenty thousand persons.

verses.raw: And after he had put to flight and destroyed them, Judas removed the host toward Ephron, a strong city, in which Lysias abode, and a great multitude of divers nations, and the strong young men kept the walls, and defended them mightily: in which also was great provision of engines and darts.
verses.text: And after he had put to flight and destroyed them, Judas removed the host toward Ephron, a strong city, in which Lysias abode, and a great multitude of divers nations, and the strong young men kept the walls, and defended them mightily: in which also was great provision of engines and darts.

verses.raw: But when Judas and his company had called upon Almighty Yahuah (God), who with his power breaks the strength of his enemies, they won the city, and slew twenty and five thousand of them that were within,
verses.text: But when Judas and his company had called upon Almighty Yahuah, who with his power breaks the strength of his enemies, they won the city, and slew twenty and five thousand of them that were within,

verses.raw: From thence they departed to Scythopolis, which lieth six hundred furlongs from Jerusalem,
verses.text: From thence they departed to Scythopolis, which lieth six hundred furlongs from Jerusalem,

verses.raw: But when the Yahudim (Jews) that dwelt there had testified that the Scythopolitans dealt lovingly with them, and entreated them kindly in the time of their adversity;
verses.text: But when the Yahudim that dwelt there had testified that the Scythopolitans dealt lovingly with them, and entreated them kindly in the time of their adversity;

verses.raw: They gave them thanks, desiring them to be friendly still to them: and so they came to Jerusalem, the feast of the weeks approaching.
verses.text: They gave them thanks, desiring them to be friendly still to them: and so they came to Jerusalem, the feast of the weeks approaching.

verses.raw: And after the feast, called Pentecost, they went forth against Gorgias the governor of Idumea,
verses.text: And after the feast, called Pentecost, they went forth against Gorgias the governor of Idumea,

verses.raw: Who came out with three thousand men of foot and four hundred horsemen.
verses.text: Who came out with three thousand men of foot and four hundred horsemen.

verses.raw: And it happened that in their fighting together a few of the Yahudim (Jews) were slain.
verses.text: And it happened that in their fighting together a few of the Yahudim were slain.

verses.raw: At which time Dositheus, one of Bacenor’s company, who was on horseback, and a strong man, was still upon Gorgias, and taking hold of his coat drew him by force; and when he would have taken that cursed man alive, a horseman of Thracia coming upon him struck off his shoulder, so that Gorgias fled to Marisa.
verses.text: At which time Dositheus, one of Bacenor’s company, who was on horseback, and a strong man, was still upon Gorgias, and taking hold of his coat drew him by force; and when he would have taken that cursed man alive, a horseman of Thracia coming upon him struck off his shoulder, so that Gorgias fled to Marisa.

verses.raw: Now when they that were with Gorgias had fought long, and were weary, Judas called upon Yahuah (God), that he would shew himself to be their helper and leader of the battle.
verses.text: Now when they that were with Gorgias had fought long, and were weary, Judas called upon Yahuah, that he would shew himself to be their helper and leader of the battle.

verses.raw: And with that he began in his own language, and sung psalms with a loud voice, and rushing unawares upon Gorgias’ men, he put them to flight.
verses.text: And with that he began in his own language, and sung psalms with a loud voice, and rushing unawares upon Gorgias’ men, he put them to flight.

verses.raw: So Judas gathered his host, and came into the city of Odollam, And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.
verses.text: So Judas gathered his host, and came into the city of Odollam, And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.

verses.raw: And upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain, and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.
verses.text: And upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain, and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.

verses.raw: Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Yahudim (Jews) by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
verses.text: Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Yahudim by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.

verses.raw: All men therefore praising Yahuah (God), the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid,
verses.text: All men therefore praising Yahuah, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid,

verses.raw: Betook themselves to prayer, and besought him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance. Besides, that noble Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, forsomuch as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain.
verses.text: Betook themselves to prayer, and besought him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance. Besides, that noble Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, forsomuch as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain.

verses.raw: And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing in it very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection:
verses.text: And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing in it very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection:

verses.raw: For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead.
verses.text: For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead.

verses.raw: And also in that he perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin. ⸻
verses.text: And also in that he perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin. ⸻

verses.raw: In the hundred forty and ninth year it was told Judas, that Antiochus Eupator was coming with a great power into Judea,
verses.text: In the hundred forty and ninth year it was told Judas, that Antiochus Eupator was coming with a great power into Judea,

verses.raw: And with him Lysias his protector, and ruler of his affairs, having either of them a Grecian power of footmen, an hundred and ten thousand, and horsemen five thousand and three hundred, and elephants two and twenty, and three hundred chariots armed with hooks.
verses.text: And with him Lysias his protector, and ruler of his affairs, having either of them a Grecian power of footmen, an hundred and ten thousand, and horsemen five thousand and three hundred, and elephants two and twenty, and three hundred chariots armed with hooks.

verses.raw: Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor.
verses.text: Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor.

verses.raw: But the King of kings moved Antiochus’ mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him to Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place.
verses.text: But the King of kings moved Antiochus’ mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him to Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place.

verses.raw: Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes.
verses.text: Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes.

verses.raw: And whoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him to death.
verses.text: And whoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him to death.

verses.raw: Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly:
verses.text: Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly:

verses.raw: For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.
verses.text: For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.

verses.raw: Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Yahudim (Jews), than had been done in his father’s time.
verses.text: Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Yahudim, than had been done in his father’s time.

verses.raw: Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon Yahuah (God) night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple:
verses.text: Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon Yahuah night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple:

verses.raw: And that he would not suffer the people, that had even now been but a little refreshed, to be in subjection to the blasphemous nations.
verses.text: And that he would not suffer the people, that had even now been but a little refreshed, to be in subjection to the blasphemous nations.

verses.raw: So when they had all done this together, and besought the merciful Yahuah (God) with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness.
verses.text: So when they had all done this together, and besought the merciful Yahuah with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness.

verses.raw: And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king’s host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of Yahuah (God).
verses.text: And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king’s host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of Yahuah.

verses.raw: So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even to death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin:
verses.text: So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even to death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin:

verses.raw: And having given the watchword to them that were about him, Victory is of Yahuah (God); with the most valiant and choice young men he went in into the king’s tent by night, and slew in the camp about four thousand men, and the chiefest of the elephants, with all that were upon him.
verses.text: And having given the watchword to them that were about him, Victory is of Yahuah; with the most valiant and choice young men he went in into the king’s tent by night, and slew in the camp about four thousand men, and the chiefest of the elephants, with all that were upon him.

verses.raw: And at last they filled the camp with fear and tumult, and departed with good success.
verses.text: And at last they filled the camp with fear and tumult, and departed with good success.

verses.raw: This was done in the break of the day, because the protection of Yahuah (God) did help him.
verses.text: This was done in the break of the day, because the protection of Yahuah did help him.

verses.raw: Now when the king had taken a taste of the manliness of the Yahudim (Jews), he went about to take the holds by policy,
verses.text: Now when the king had taken a taste of the manliness of the Yahudim, he went about to take the holds by policy,

verses.raw: And marched toward Bethsura, which was a strong hold of the Yahudim (Jews): but he was put to flight, failed, and lost of his men:
verses.text: And marched toward Bethsura, which was a strong hold of the Yahudim: but he was put to flight, failed, and lost of his men:

verses.raw: For Judas had conveyed to them that were in it such things as were necessary.
verses.text: For Judas had conveyed to them that were in it such things as were necessary.

verses.raw: But Rhodocus, who was in the Yahudim (Jews)’ host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison.
verses.text: But Rhodocus, who was in the Yahudim’ host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison.

verses.raw: The king treated with them in Bethsum the second time, gave his hand, took their’s, departed, fought with Judas, was overcome;
verses.text: The king treated with them in Bethsum the second time, gave his hand, took their’s, departed, fought with Judas, was overcome;

verses.raw: Heard that Philip, who was left over the affairs in Antioch, was desperately bent, confounded, intreated the Yahudim (Jews), submitted himself, and sware to all equal conditions, agreed with them, and offered sacrifice, honoured the temple, and dealt kindly with the place,
verses.text: Heard that Philip, who was left over the affairs in Antioch, was desperately bent, confounded, intreated the Yahudim, submitted himself, and sware to all equal conditions, agreed with them, and offered sacrifice, honoured the temple, and dealt kindly with the place,

verses.raw: And accepted well of Maccabeus, made him principal governor from Ptolemais to the Gerrhenians;
verses.text: And accepted well of Maccabeus, made him principal governor from Ptolemais to the Gerrhenians;

verses.raw: Came to Ptolemais: the people there were grieved for the covenants; for they stormed, because they would make their covenants void:
verses.text: Came to Ptolemais: the people there were grieved for the covenants; for they stormed, because they would make their covenants void:

verses.raw: Lysias went up to the judgment seat, said as much as could be in defence of the cause, persuaded, pacified, made them well affected, returned to Antioch. Thus it went touching the king’s coming and departing. ⸻
verses.text: Lysias went up to the judgment seat, said as much as could be in defence of the cause, persuaded, pacified, made them well affected, returned to Antioch. Thus it went touching the king’s coming and departing. ⸻

verses.raw: After three years was Judas informed, that Demetrius the son of Seleucus, having entered by the haven of Tripolis with a great power and navy,
verses.text: After three years was Judas informed, that Demetrius the son of Seleucus, having entered by the haven of Tripolis with a great power and navy,

verses.raw: Had taken the country, and killed Antiochus, and Lysias his protector.
verses.text: Had taken the country, and killed Antiochus, and Lysias his protector.

verses.raw: Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar,
verses.text: Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar,

verses.raw: Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting to him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.
verses.text: Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting to him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.

verses.raw: Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Yahudim (Jews) stood affected, and what they intended, he answered to it:
verses.text: Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Yahudim stood affected, and what they intended, he answered to it:

verses.raw: Those of the Yahudim (Jews) that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.
verses.text: Those of the Yahudim that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.

verses.raw: Therefore I, being deprived of my ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:
verses.text: Therefore I, being deprived of my ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:

verses.raw: First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of my own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforersaid.
verses.text: First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of my own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforersaid.

verses.raw: Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that you readily shewest to all.
verses.text: Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that you readily shewest to all.

verses.raw: For as long as Judas lives, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.
verses.text: For as long as Judas lives, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.

verses.raw: This was no sooner spoken of him, but others of the king’s friends, being maliciously set against Judas, did more incense Demetrius.
verses.text: This was no sooner spoken of him, but others of the king’s friends, being maliciously set against Judas, did more incense Demetrius.

verses.raw: And forthwith calling Nicanor, who had been master of the elephants, and making him governor over Judea, he sent him forth,
verses.text: And forthwith calling Nicanor, who had been master of the elephants, and making him governor over Judea, he sent him forth,

verses.raw: Commanding him to slay Judas, and to scatter them that were with him, and to make Alcimus high priest of the great temple.
verses.text: Commanding him to slay Judas, and to scatter them that were with him, and to make Alcimus high priest of the great temple.

verses.raw: Then the heathen, that had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the harm and calamities of the Yahudim (Jews) to be their welfare.
verses.text: Then the heathen, that had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the harm and calamities of the Yahudim to be their welfare.

verses.raw: Now when the Yahudim (Jews) heard of Nicanor’s coming, and that the heathen were up against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him that had established his people for ever, and who always helps his portion with manifestation of his presence.
verses.text: Now when the Yahudim heard of Nicanor’s coming, and that the heathen were up against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him that had established his people for ever, and who always helps his portion with manifestation of his presence.

verses.raw: So at the commandment of the captain they removed straightways from thence, and came near to them at the town of Dessau.
verses.text: So at the commandment of the captain they removed straightways from thence, and came near to them at the town of Dessau.

verses.raw: Now Simon, Judas’ brother, had joined battle with Nicanor, but was somewhat discomfited through the sudden silence of his enemies.
verses.text: Now Simon, Judas’ brother, had joined battle with Nicanor, but was somewhat discomfited through the sudden silence of his enemies.

verses.raw: Nevertheless Nicanor, hearing of the manliness of them that were with Judas, and the courageousness that they had to fight for their country, durst not try the matter by the sword.
verses.text: Nevertheless Nicanor, hearing of the manliness of them that were with Judas, and the courageousness that they had to fight for their country, durst not try the matter by the sword.

verses.raw: Wherefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotus, and Mattathias, to make peace.
verses.text: Wherefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotus, and Mattathias, to make peace.

verses.raw: So when they had taken long advisement thereupon, and the captain had made the multitude acquainted with it, and it appeared that they were all of one mind, they consented to the covenants,
verses.text: So when they had taken long advisement thereupon, and the captain had made the multitude acquainted with it, and it appeared that they were all of one mind, they consented to the covenants,

verses.raw: And appointed a day to meet in together by themselves: and when the day came, and stools were set for either of them,
verses.text: And appointed a day to meet in together by themselves: and when the day came, and stools were set for either of them,

verses.raw: Ludas placed armed men ready in convenient places, lest some treachery should be suddenly practised by the enemies: so they made a peaceable conference.
verses.text: Ludas placed armed men ready in convenient places, lest some treachery should be suddenly practised by the enemies: so they made a peaceable conference.

verses.raw: Now Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no hurt, but sent away the people that came flocking to him.
verses.text: Now Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no hurt, but sent away the people that came flocking to him.

verses.raw: And he would not willingly have Judas out of his sight: for he love the man from his heart
verses.text: And he would not willingly have Judas out of his sight: for he love the man from his heart

verses.raw: He prayed him also to take a wife, and to beget children: so he married, was quiet, and took part of this life.
verses.text: He prayed him also to take a wife, and to beget children: so he married, was quiet, and took part of this life.

verses.raw: But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was between them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.
verses.text: But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was between them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.

verses.raw: Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste to Antioch.
verses.text: Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste to Antioch.

verses.raw: When this came to Nicanor’s hearing, he was much confounded in himself, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles which were agreed upon, the man being in no fault.
verses.text: When this came to Nicanor’s hearing, he was much confounded in himself, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles which were agreed upon, the man being in no fault.

verses.raw: But because there was no dealing against the king, he watched his time to accomplish this thing by policy.
verses.text: But because there was no dealing against the king, he watched his time to accomplish this thing by policy.

verses.raw: Notwithstanding, when Maccabeus saw that Nicanor began to be churlish to him, and that he entreated him more roughly than he was wont, perceiving that such sour behaviour came not of good, he gathered together not a few of his men, and withdrew himself from Nicanor.
verses.text: Notwithstanding, when Maccabeus saw that Nicanor began to be churlish to him, and that he entreated him more roughly than he was wont, perceiving that such sour behaviour came not of good, he gathered together not a few of his men, and withdrew himself from Nicanor.

verses.raw: But the other, knowing that he was notably prevented by Judas’ policy, came into the great and holy temple, and commanded the priests, that were offering their usual sacrifices, to deliver him the man.
verses.text: But the other, knowing that he was notably prevented by Judas’ policy, came into the great and holy temple, and commanded the priests, that were offering their usual sacrifices, to deliver him the man.

verses.raw: And when they sware that they could not tell where the man was whom he sought,
verses.text: And when they sware that they could not tell where the man was whom he sought,

verses.raw: He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If you will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of Yahuah (God) even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple to Bacchus.
verses.text: He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If you will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of Yahuah even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple to Bacchus.

verses.raw: After these words he departed. Then the priests lifted up their hands toward heaven, and besought him that was ever a defender of their nation, saying in this manner;
verses.text: After these words he departed. Then the priests lifted up their hands toward heaven, and besought him that was ever a defender of their nation, saying in this manner;

verses.raw: You, O Yahuah (God) of all things, who have need of nothing, were pleased that the temple of yours habitation should be among us:
verses.text: You, O Yahuah of all things, who have need of nothing, were pleased that the temple of yours habitation should be among us:

verses.raw: Therefore now, O holy Yahuah (God) of all holiness, keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth.
verses.text: Therefore now, O holy Yahuah of all holiness, keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth.

verses.raw: Now was there accused to Nicanor one Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen, and a man of very good report, who for his kindness was called a father of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: Now was there accused to Nicanor one Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen, and a man of very good report, who for his kindness was called a father of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles, he had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles, he had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: So Nicanor, willing to declare the hate that he bare to the Yahudim (Jews), sent above five hundred men of war to take him:
verses.text: So Nicanor, willing to declare the hate that he bare to the Yahudim, sent above five hundred men of war to take him:

verses.raw: For he thought by taking him to do the Yahudim (Jews) much hurt.
verses.text: For he thought by taking him to do the Yahudim much hurt.

verses.raw: Now when the multitude would have taken the tower, and violently broken into the outer door, and told that fire should be brought to burn it, he being ready to be taken on every side fell upon his sword;
verses.text: Now when the multitude would have taken the tower, and violently broken into the outer door, and told that fire should be brought to burn it, he being ready to be taken on every side fell upon his sword;

verses.raw: And behold I call to witness against you this day the Elohim (God) of heaven, that ye walk not in the ignorance of youth and fornication, wherein I was poured out, and defiled the bed of my father Jacob.

verses.raw: And I tell you that He smote me with a sore plague in my loins for seven months; and had not my father Jacob prayed for me to Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord) would have destroyed me.

verses.raw: For I was thirty years old when I wrought the evil thing before Yahuah (Lord), and for seven months I was sick unto death.

verses.raw: And after this I repented with set purpose of my soul for seven years before Yahuah (Lord).
verses.text: And after this I repented with set purpose of my soul for seven years before Yahuah.

verses.raw: And wine and strong drink I drank not, and flesh entered not into my mouth, and I eat no pleasant food; but I mourned over my sin, for it was great, such as had not been in Yashar'el (Israel).

verses.raw: The third, the spirit of fighting, in the liver and gall. The fourth is the spirit of obsequiousness and chicanery, that through officious attention one may be fair in seeming.

verses.raw: The fifth is the spirit of pride, that one may be boastful and arrogant. The sixth is the spirit of lying, in perdition and in jealousy, to practise deceits, and concealments from kindred and friends.

verses.raw: And now, my children, love the truth, and it will preserve you: hear ye the words of Reuben your father.
verses.text: And now, my children, love the truth, and it will preserve you: hear ye the words of Reuben your father.

verses.raw: Pay no heed to the face of a woman, Nor associate with another man's wife, Nor meddle with affairs of womankind.
verses.text: Pay no heed to the face of a woman, Nor associate with another man's wife, Nor meddle with affairs of womankind.

verses.raw: For had I not seen Bilhah bathing in a covered place, I had not fallen into this great iniquity.
verses.text: For had I not seen Bilhah bathing in a covered place, I had not fallen into this great iniquity.

verses.raw: For my mind taking in the thought of the woman's nakedness, suffered me not to sleep until I had wrought the abominable thing.
verses.text: For my mind taking in the thought of the woman's nakedness, suffered me not to sleep until I had wrought the abominable thing.

verses.raw: For while Jacob our father had gone to Isaac his father, when we were in Eder, near to Ephrath in Bethlehem, Bilhah became drunk and was asleep uncovered in her chamber.
verses.text: For while Jacob our father had gone to Isaac his father, when we were in Eder, near to Ephrath in Bethlehem, Bilhah became drunk and was asleep uncovered in her chamber.

verses.raw: Having therefore gone in and beheld her nakedness, I wrought the impiety without her perceiving it, and leaving her sleeping I departed.
verses.text: Having therefore gone in and beheld her nakedness, I wrought the impiety without her perceiving it, and leaving her sleeping I departed.

verses.raw: And forthwith an angel of Elohim (God) revealed to my father concerning my impiety, and he came and mourned over me, and touched her no more.
verses.text: And forthwith an angel of Elohim revealed to my father concerning my impiety, and he came and mourned over me, and touched her no more.

verses.raw: Pay no heed, therefore, my children, to the beauty of women, nor set your mind on their affairs; but walk in singleness of heart in the fear of Yahuah (Lord), and expend labour on good works, and on study and on your flocks, until Yahuah (Lord) give you a wife, whom He will, that ye suffer not as I did.
verses.text: Pay no heed, therefore, my children, to the beauty of women, nor set your mind on their affairs; but walk in singleness of heart in the fear of Yahuah, and expend labour on good works, and on study and on your flocks, until Yahuah give you a wife, whom He will, that ye suffer not as I did.

verses.raw: For until my father's death I had not boldness to look in his face, or to speak to any of my brethren, because of the reproach.
verses.text: For until my father's death I had not boldness to look in his face, or to speak to any of my brethren, because of the reproach.

verses.raw: Even until now my conscience causeth me anguish on account of my impiety.
verses.text: Even until now my conscience causeth me anguish on account of my impiety.

verses.raw: And yet my father comforted me much, and prayed for me unto Yahuah (Lord), that the anger of Yahuah (Lord) might pass from me, even as Yahuah (Lord) showed. And thenceforth until now I have been on my guard and sinned not.
verses.text: And yet my father comforted me much, and prayed for me unto Yahuah, that the anger of Yahuah might pass from me, even as Yahuah showed. And thenceforth until now I have been on my guard and sinned not.

verses.raw: Therefore, my children, I say unto you, observe all things whatsoever I command you, and ye shall not sin.
verses.text: Therefore, my children, I say unto you, observe all things whatsoever I command you, and ye shall not sin.

verses.raw: For a pit unto the soul is the sin of fornication, separating it from Elohim (God), and bringing it near to idols, because it deceiveth the mind and understanding, and leadeth down young men into Hades before their time.
verses.text: For a pit unto the soul is the sin of fornication, separating it from Elohim, and bringing it near to idols, because it deceiveth the mind and understanding, and leadeth down young men into Hades before their time.

verses.raw: For many hath fornication destroyed; because, though a man be old or noble, or rich or poor, he bringeth reproach upon himself with the sons of men and derision with Beliar.
verses.text: For many hath fornication destroyed; because, though a man be old or noble, or rich or poor, he bringeth reproach upon himself with the sons of men and derision with Beliar.

verses.raw: For hear ye regarding Joseph how he guarded himself from a woman, and purged his thoughts from all fornication, and found favour in the sight of Elohim (God) and men.
verses.text: For hear ye regarding Joseph how he guarded himself from a woman, and purged his thoughts from all fornication, and found favour in the sight of Elohim and men.

verses.raw: For the Egyptian woman did many things unto him, and summoned magicians, and offered him love potions, but the purpose of his soul admitted no evil desire.
verses.text: For the Egyptian woman did many things unto him, and summoned magicians, and offered him love potions, but the purpose of his soul admitted no evil desire.

verses.raw: Therefore the Elohim (God) of your fathers delivered him from every evil (and) hidden death.
verses.text: Therefore the Elohim of your fathers delivered him from every evil (and) hidden death.

verses.raw: For if fornication overcomes not your mind, neither can Beliar overcome you.
verses.text: For if fornication overcomes not your mind, neither can Beliar overcome you.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: For evil are women, my children; and since they have no power or strength over man, they use wiles by outward attractions that they may draw him to themselves.
verses.text: For evil are women, my children; and since they have no power or strength over man, they use wiles by outward attractions that they may draw him to themselves.

verses.raw: And whom they cannot bewitch by outward attractions, him they overcome by craft.
verses.text: And whom they cannot bewitch by outward attractions, him they overcome by craft.

verses.raw: For moreover, concerning them, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) told me, and taught me, that women are overcome by the spirit of fornication more than men, and in their heart they plot against men; and by means of their adornment they deceive first their minds, and by the glance of the eye instil the poison, and then through the accomplished act they take them captive.
verses.text: For moreover, concerning them, the angel of Yahuah told me, and taught me, that women are overcome by the spirit of fornication more than men, and in their heart they plot against men; and by means of their adornment they deceive first their minds, and by the glance of the eye instil the poison, and then through the accomplished act they take them captive.

verses.raw: For a woman cannot force a man openly, but by a harlot's bearing she beguiles him.
verses.text: For a woman cannot force a man openly, but by a harlot's bearing she beguiles him.

verses.raw: Flee, therefore, fornication, my children, and command your wives and your daughters, that they adorn not their heads and faces to deceive the mind; because every woman who useth these wiles hath been reserved for eternal punishment.
verses.text: Flee, therefore, fornication, my children, and command your wives and your daughters, that they adorn not their heads and faces to deceive the mind; because every woman who useth these wiles hath been reserved for eternal punishment.

verses.raw: For thus they allured the Watchers who were before the flood; for as these continually beheld them, they lusted after them, and they conceived the act in their mind; for they changed themselves into the shape of men, and appeared to them when they were with their husbands.
verses.text: For thus they allured the Watchers who were before the flood; for as these continually beheld them, they lusted after them, and they conceived the act in their mind; for they changed themselves into the shape of men, and appeared to them when they were with their husbands.

verses.raw: And the women lusting in their minds after their forms, gave birth to giants, for the Watchers appeared to them as reaching even unto heaven.
verses.text: And the women lusting in their minds after their forms, gave birth to giants, for the Watchers appeared to them as reaching even unto heaven.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: Beware, therefore, of fornication; and if you wish to be pure in mind, guard your senses from every woman.
verses.text: Beware, therefore, of fornication; and if you wish to be pure in mind, guard your senses from every woman.

verses.raw: And command the women likewise not to associate with men, that they also may be pure in mind.
verses.text: And command the women likewise not to associate with men, that they also may be pure in mind.

verses.raw: For constant meetings, even though the ungodly deed be not wrought, are to them an irremediable disease, and to us a destruction of Beliar and an eternal reproach.
verses.text: For constant meetings, even though the ungodly deed be not wrought, are to them an irremediable disease, and to us a destruction of Beliar and an eternal reproach.

verses.raw: For in fornication there is neither understanding nor godliness, and all jealousy dwelleth in the lust thereof.
verses.text: For in fornication there is neither understanding nor godliness, and all jealousy dwelleth in the lust thereof.

verses.raw: Therefore, then, I say unto you, ye will be jealous against the sons of Levi, and will seek to be exalted over them; but ye shall not be able.
verses.text: Therefore, then, I say unto you, ye will be jealous against the sons of Levi, and will seek to be exalted over them; but ye shall not be able.

verses.raw: For Elohim (God) will avenge them, and ye shall die by an evil death.
verses.text: For Elohim will avenge them, and ye shall die by an evil death.

verses.raw: For to Levi Elohim (God) gave the sovereignty [and to Yahudah (Judah) with him and to me also, and to Dan and Joseph, that we should be for rulers].
verses.text: For to Levi Elohim gave the sovereignty [and to Yahudah with him and to me also, and to Dan and Joseph, that we should be for rulers].

verses.raw: Therefore I command you to hearken to Levi, because he shall know the law of Yahuah (Lord), and shall give ordinances for judgment and shall sacrifice for all Yashar'el (Israel) until the consummation of the times, as the anointed High Priest, of whom Yahuah (Lord) spake.
verses.text: Therefore I command you to hearken to Levi, because he shall know the law of Yahuah, and shall give ordinances for judgment and shall sacrifice for all Yashar'el until the consummation of the times, as the anointed High Priest, of whom Yahuah spake.

verses.raw: I adjure you by the Elohim (God) of heaven to do truth each one unto his neighbour and to entertain love each one for his brother.
verses.text: I adjure you by the Elohim of heaven to do truth each one unto his neighbour and to entertain love each one for his brother.

verses.raw: And draw ye near to Levi in humbleness of heart, that ye may receive a blessing from his mouth.
verses.text: And draw ye near to Levi in humbleness of heart, that ye may receive a blessing from his mouth.

verses.raw: For he shall bless Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), because him hath Yahuah (Lord) chosen to be king over all the nation.
verses.text: For he shall bless Yashar'el and Yahudah, because him hath Yahuah chosen to be king over all the nation.

verses.raw: And bow down before his seed, for on our behalf it will die in wars visible and invisible, and will be among you an eternal king.
verses.text: And bow down before his seed, for on our behalf it will die in wars visible and invisible, and will be among you an eternal king.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: And Reuben died, having given these commands to his sons.
verses.text: And Reuben died, having given these commands to his sons.

verses.raw: And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.
verses.text: And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: The copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph, his brother, died.
verses.text: The copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph, his brother, died.

verses.raw: For when Simeon was sick, his sons came to visit him, and he strengthened himself and sat up and kissed them, and said:—
verses.text: For when Simeon was sick, his sons came to visit him, and he strengthened himself and sat up and kissed them, and said:—

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: Hearken, my children, to Simeon your father, And I will declare unto you what things I have in my heart.
verses.text: Hearken, my children, to Simeon your father, And I will declare unto you what things I have in my heart.

verses.raw: I was born of Jacob as my father's second son; And my mother Leah called me Simeon, Because Yahuah (Lord) had heard her prayer.
verses.text: I was born of Jacob as my father's second son; And my mother Leah called me Simeon, Because Yahuah had heard her prayer.

verses.raw: Moreover, I became strong exceedingly; I shrank from no achievement, Nor was I afraid of ought.
verses.text: Moreover, I became strong exceedingly; I shrank from no achievement, Nor was I afraid of ought.

verses.raw: For my heart was hard, And my liver was immovable, And my bowels without compassion.
verses.text: For my heart was hard, And my liver was immovable, And my bowels without compassion.

verses.raw: Because valour also has been given from the El Elyon (Most High) to men in soul and body.
verses.text: Because valour also has been given from the El Elyon to men in soul and body.

verses.raw: For in the time of my youth I was jealous 'in many things' of Joseph, because my father loved him 'beyond all'.
verses.text: For in the time of my youth I was jealous 'in many things' of Joseph, because my father loved him 'beyond all'.

verses.raw: And I set my mind against him to destroy him, because the prince of deceit sent forth the spirit of jealousy and blinded my mind, so that I regarded him not as a brother, nor did I spare even Jacob my father.
verses.text: And I set my mind against him to destroy him, because the prince of deceit sent forth the spirit of jealousy and blinded my mind, so that I regarded him not as a brother, nor did I spare even Jacob my father.

verses.raw: But his Elohim (God) and the Elohim (God) of his fathers sent forth His angel, and delivered him out of my hands.
verses.text: But his Elohim and the Elohim of his fathers sent forth His angel, and delivered him out of my hands.

verses.raw: For when I went to Shechem to bring ointment for the flocks, and Reuben to Dothan, where were our necessaries and all our stores, Yahudah (Judah) my brother sold him to the Ishmaelites.
verses.text: For when I went to Shechem to bring ointment for the flocks, and Reuben to Dothan, where were our necessaries and all our stores, Yahudah my brother sold him to the Ishmaelites.

verses.raw: And when Reuben heard these things he was grieved, for he wished to restore him to his father.
verses.text: And when Reuben heard these things he was grieved, for he wished to restore him to his father.

verses.raw: But on hearing this I was 'exceedingly' wroth against Yahudah (Judah) in that he let him go away alive, and for five months I continued wrathful against him.
verses.text: But on hearing this I was 'exceedingly' wroth against Yahudah in that he let him go away alive, and for five months I continued wrathful against him.

verses.raw: But Yahuah (Lord) restrained me, and withheld 'from me' the power of my hands; for my right hand was half withered for seven days.
verses.text: But Yahuah restrained me, and withheld 'from me' the power of my hands; for my right hand was half withered for seven days.

verses.raw: And I knew, my children, that because of Joseph this had befallen me, and I repented and wept; and I besought Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) that my hand might be restored, and that I might hold aloof from all pollution and envy, 'and from all folly'.
verses.text: And I knew, my children, that because of Joseph this had befallen me, and I repented and wept; and I besought Yahuah Elohim that my hand might be restored, and that I might hold aloof from all pollution and envy, 'and from all folly'.

verses.raw: For I knew that I had devised an evil thing before Yahuah (Lord) and Jacob my father, on account of Joseph my brother, in that I envied him.
verses.text: For I knew that I had devised an evil thing before Yahuah and Jacob my father, on account of Joseph my brother, in that I envied him.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: And now, my children, 'hearken unto me and' beware of the spirit of deceit and of envy.
verses.text: And now, my children, 'hearken unto me and' beware of the spirit of deceit and of envy.

verses.raw: For envy ruleth over the whole mind of a man, and suffereth him 'neither to eat nor to drink', nor to do any good thing.
verses.text: For envy ruleth over the whole mind of a man, and suffereth him 'neither to eat nor to drink', nor to do any good thing.

verses.raw: But it ever suggesteth (to him) to destroy him that he envieth; and so long as he that is envied flourisheth, he that envieth fadeth away.
verses.text: But it ever suggesteth (to him) to destroy him that he envieth; and so long as he that is envied flourisheth, he that envieth fadeth away.

verses.raw: Two years 'therefore' I afflicted my soul with fasting in the fear of Yahuah (Lord), and I learnt that deliverance from envy cometh by the fear of Elohim (God).
verses.text: Two years 'therefore' I afflicted my soul with fasting in the fear of Yahuah, and I learnt that deliverance from envy cometh by the fear of Elohim.

verses.raw: For if a man flee to Yahuah (Lord), the evil spirit runneth away from him, and his mind is lightened.
verses.text: For if a man flee to Yahuah, the evil spirit runneth away from him, and his mind is lightened.

verses.raw: And henceforward he sympathiseth with him whom he envied and agreeth with those who love him, and so ceaseth from his envy.
verses.text: And henceforward he sympathiseth with him whom he envied and agreeth with those who love him, and so ceaseth from his envy.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: And my father asked 'concerning me', because he saw that I was sad; and I said unto him, I am pained in my liver.
verses.text: And my father asked 'concerning me', because he saw that I was sad; and I said unto him, I am pained in my liver.

verses.raw: For I mourned more than they all, because I was guilty of the selling of Joseph.
verses.text: For I mourned more than they all, because I was guilty of the selling of Joseph.

verses.raw: And when we went down into Egypt, and he bound me as a spy, I knew that I was suffering justly, and I grieved not.
verses.text: And when we went down into Egypt, and he bound me as a spy, I knew that I was suffering justly, and I grieved not.

verses.raw: Now Joseph was a good man, and had the Spirit of Elohim (God) within him: being compassionate and pitiful, he bore no malice against me; but loved me even as the rest of his brethren.
verses.text: Now Joseph was a good man, and had the Spirit of Elohim within him: being compassionate and pitiful, he bore no malice against me; but loved me even as the rest of his brethren.

verses.raw: Beware, therefore, my children, of all jealousy and envy, and walk in singleness of heart, soul and with good heart, keeping in mind Joseph your father's brother, that Elohim (God) may give 'you also' grace and glory, and blessing upon your heads, even as ye saw in Joseph's case.
verses.text: Beware, therefore, my children, of all jealousy and envy, and walk in singleness of heart, soul and with good heart, keeping in mind Joseph your father's brother, that Elohim may give 'you also' grace and glory, and blessing upon your heads, even as ye saw in Joseph's case.

verses.raw: All his days he reproached us not concerning this thing, but loved us as his own soul, and beyond his own sons glorified us, and gave us riches, and cattle and fruits.
verses.text: All his days he reproached us not concerning this thing, but loved us as his own soul, and beyond his own sons glorified us, and gave us riches, and cattle and fruits.

verses.raw: Do ye also, my children, love each one his brother with a good heart, and the spirit of envy will withdraw from you.
verses.text: Do ye also, my children, love each one his brother with a good heart, and the spirit of envy will withdraw from you.

verses.raw: For this maketh savage the soul and destroyeth the body; it causeth anger and war in the mind, and stirreth up unto deeds of blood, and leadeth the mind into frenzy, 'and suffereth not prudence to act in men; moreover, it taketh away sleep', [and causeth tumult to the soul and trembling to the body].
verses.text: For this maketh savage the soul and destroyeth the body; it causeth anger and war in the mind, and stirreth up unto deeds of blood, and leadeth the mind into frenzy, 'and suffereth not prudence to act in men; moreover, it taketh away sleep', [and causeth tumult to the soul and trembling to the body].

verses.raw: For even in sleep some malicious jealousy, deluding him, gnaweth, and with wicked spirits disturbeth his soul, and causeth the body to be troubled, and waketh the mind from sleep in confusion; and as a wicked and poisonous spirit, so appeareth it to men.
verses.text: For even in sleep some malicious jealousy, deluding him, gnaweth, and with wicked spirits disturbeth his soul, and causeth the body to be troubled, and waketh the mind from sleep in confusion; and as a wicked and poisonous spirit, so appeareth it to men.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: Therefore was Joseph comely in appearance, and goodly to look upon, because no wickedness dwelt in him; for some of the trouble of the spirit the face manifesteth.
verses.text: Therefore was Joseph comely in appearance, and goodly to look upon, because no wickedness dwelt in him; for some of the trouble of the spirit the face manifesteth.

verses.raw: And now, my children, Make your hearts good before Yahuah (Lord), And your ways straight before men, And ye shall find grace before Yahuah (Lord) and men.
verses.text: And now, my children, Make your hearts good before Yahuah, And your ways straight before men, And ye shall find grace before Yahuah and men.

verses.raw: Beware, therefore, of fornication, For fornication is mother of all evils, Separating from Elohim (God), and bringing near to Beliar.
verses.text: Beware, therefore, of fornication, For fornication is mother of all evils, Separating from Elohim, and bringing near to Beliar.

verses.raw: For I have seen it inscribed in the writing of Enoch that your sons shall be corrupted in fornication, and shall do harm to the sons of Levi with the sword.
verses.text: For I have seen it inscribed in the writing of Enoch that your sons shall be corrupted in fornication, and shall do harm to the sons of Levi with the sword.

verses.raw: But they shall not be able to withstand Levi; for he shall wage the war of Yahuah (Lord), and shall conquer 'all' your hosts.
verses.text: But they shall not be able to withstand Levi; for he shall wage the war of Yahuah, and shall conquer 'all' your hosts.

verses.raw: And they shall be few in number, divided in Levi and Yahudah (Judah), and there shall be none of you for sovereignty, even as also our father prophesied in his blessings.
verses.text: And they shall be few in number, divided in Levi and Yahudah, and there shall be none of you for sovereignty, even as also our father prophesied in his blessings.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: Behold I have told you all things, that I may be acquitted of your sin.
verses.text: Behold I have told you all things, that I may be acquitted of your sin.

verses.raw: Now, if ye remove from you your envy and all stiff-neckedness, As a rose shall my bones flourish in Yashar'el (Israel), And as a lily my flesh in Jacob, And my odour shall be as the odour of Libanus; And as cedars shall holy ones be multiplied from me for ever, And their branches shall stretch afar off.
verses.text: Now, if ye remove from you your envy and all stiff-neckedness, As a rose shall my bones flourish in Yashar'el, And as a lily my flesh in Jacob, And my odour shall be as the odour of Libanus; And as cedars shall holy ones be multiplied from me for ever, And their branches shall stretch afar off.

verses.raw: Then shall perish the seed of Canaan, And a remnant shall not be unto Amalek, [And all the Cappadocians shall perish, And all the Hittites shall be utterly destroyed.
verses.text: Then shall perish the seed of Canaan, And a remnant shall not be unto Amalek, [And all the Cappadocians shall perish, And all the Hittites shall be utterly destroyed.

verses.raw: Then shall fail the land of Ham, And all the people shall perish. Then shall all the earth rest from trouble, And all the world under heaven from war.
verses.text: Then shall fail the land of Ham, And all the people shall perish. Then shall all the earth rest from trouble, And all the world under heaven from war.

verses.raw: Then the Mighty One of Yashar'el (Israel) shall glorify Shem, For Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) shall appear on earth, And save the sons of men.
verses.text: Then the Mighty One of Yashar'el shall glorify Shem, For Yahuah Elohim shall appear on earth, And save the sons of men.

verses.raw: Then shall all the spirits of deceit be given to be trodden under foot, And men shall rule over wicked spirits.
verses.text: Then shall all the spirits of deceit be given to be trodden under foot, And men shall rule over wicked spirits.

verses.raw: Then shall I arise in joy, And will bless the El Elyon (Most High) because of His marvellous works, [Because Elohim (God) hath taken a body and eaten with men and saved men].
verses.text: Then shall I arise in joy, And will bless the El Elyon because of His marvellous works, [Because Elohim hath taken a body and eaten with men and saved men].

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: And now, my children, obey Levi and Yahudah (Judah), and be not lifted up against these two tribes, for from them shall arise unto you the salvation of Elohim (God).
verses.text: And now, my children, obey Levi and Yahudah, and be not lifted up against these two tribes, for from them shall arise unto you the salvation of Elohim.

verses.raw: For Yahuah (Lord) shall raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Yahudah (Judah) as it were a King [Elohim (God) and man], He shall save all [the Gentiles and] the race of Yashar'el (Israel).
verses.text: For Yahuah shall raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Yahudah as it were a King [Elohim and man], He shall save all [the Gentiles and] the race of Yashar'el.

verses.raw: Therefore I give you these commands that ye also may command your children, that they may observe them throughout their generations.
verses.text: Therefore I give you these commands that ye also may command your children, that they may observe them throughout their generations.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: And when Simeon had made an end of commanding his sons, he slept with his fathers, being an hundred and twenty years old.
verses.text: And when Simeon had made an end of commanding his sons, he slept with his fathers, being an hundred and twenty years old.

verses.raw: And they laid him in a wooden coffin, to take up his bones to Hebron. And they took them up secretly during a war of the Egyptians.
verses.text: And they laid him in a wooden coffin, to take up his bones to Hebron. And they took them up secretly during a war of the Egyptians.

verses.raw: For the bones of Joseph the Egyptians guarded in the tombs of the Kings.
verses.text: For the bones of Joseph the Egyptians guarded in the tombs of the Kings.

verses.raw: For the sorcerers told them, that on the departure of the bones of Joseph there should be throughout all the land darkness and gloom, and an exceeding great plague to the Egyptians, so that even with a lamp a man should not recognise his brother.
verses.text: For the sorcerers told them, that on the departure of the bones of Joseph there should be throughout all the land darkness and gloom, and an exceeding great plague to the Egyptians, so that even with a lamp a man should not recognise his brother.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: And the sons of Simeon bewailed their father.
verses.text: And the sons of Simeon bewailed their father.

verses.raw: And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.
verses.text: And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: The copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained unto his sons, according to all that they should do, and what things should befall them until the day of judgment.
verses.text: The copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained unto his sons, according to all that they should do, and what things should befall them until the day of judgment.

verses.raw: He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die. And when they were gathered together he said to them:
verses.text: He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die. And when they were gathered together he said to them:

title: The Testaments of the XII Patriarchs

verses.raw: I, Levi, was born in Haran, and I came with my father to Shechem.
verses.text: I, Levi, was born in Haran, and I came with my father to Shechem.

verses.raw: And I was young, about twenty years of age, when, with Simeon, I wrought vengeance on Hamor for our sister Dinah.
verses.text: And I was young, about twenty years of age, when, with Simeon, I wrought vengeance on Hamor for our sister Dinah.

verses.raw: And when I was feeding the flocks in Abel-Maul, the spirit of understanding of Yahuah (Lord) came upon me, and I saw all men corrupting their way, and that unrighteousness had built for itself walls, and lawlessness sat upon towers.
