verses.text: And the angel said to me, Listen, Baruch: All things whatsoever I showed thee are in the first and second heaven, and in the third heaven the sun passes through and gives light to the world. But wait, and thou shalt see the glory of Elohim.

verses.raw: And while I was conversing with him, I saw the bird, and he appeared in front, and grew less and less, and at length returned to his full size.
verses.text: And while I was conversing with him, I saw the bird, and he appeared in front, and grew less and less, and at length returned to his full size.

verses.raw: And behind him I saw the shining sun, and the angels which draw it, and a crown upon its head, the sight of which we were not able to gaze upon, and behold.
verses.text: And behind him I saw the shining sun, and the angels which draw it, and a crown upon its head, the sight of which we were not able to gaze upon, and behold.

verses.raw: And as soon as the sun shone, the Phoenix also stretched out his wings. But I, when I beheld such great glory, was brought low with great fear, and I fled and hid in the wings of the angel.
verses.text: And as soon as the sun shone, the Phoenix also stretched out his wings. But I, when I beheld such great glory, was brought low with great fear, and I fled and hid in the wings of the angel.

verses.raw: And the angel said to me, Fear not, Baruch, but wait and thou shalt also see their setting.
verses.text: And the angel said to me, Fear not, Baruch, but wait and thou shalt also see their setting.

verses.raw: And he took me and led me towards the west; and when the time of the setting came, I saw again the bird coming before it, and as soon as he came I saw the angels, and they lifted the crown from its head.
verses.text: And he took me and led me towards the west; and when the time of the setting came, I saw again the bird coming before it, and as soon as he came I saw the angels, and they lifted the crown from its head.

verses.raw: But the bird stood exhausted and with wings contracted.
verses.text: But the bird stood exhausted and with wings contracted.

verses.raw: And beholding these things, I said, Yahuah (Lord), wherefore did they lift the crown from the head of the sun, and wherefore is the bird so exhausted?
verses.text: And beholding these things, I said, Yahuah, wherefore did they lift the crown from the head of the sun, and wherefore is the bird so exhausted?

verses.raw: And the angel said to me, The crown of the sun, when it has run through the day—four angels take it, and bear it up to heaven, and renew it, because it and its rays have been defiled upon earth; moreover it is so renewed each day. And I Baruch said, Yahuah (Lord), and wherefore are its beams defiled upon earth?
verses.text: And the angel said to me, The crown of the sun, when it has run through the day—four angels take it, and bear it up to heaven, and renew it, because it and its rays have been defiled upon earth; moreover it is so renewed each day. And I Baruch said, Yahuah, and wherefore are its beams defiled upon earth?

verses.raw: And the angel said to me, Because it beholds the lawlessness and unrighteousness of men, namely fornications, adulteries, thefts, extortions, idolatries, drunkenness, murders, strife, jealousies, evil-speakings, murmurings, whisperings, divinations, and such like, which are not well-pleasing to Elohim (God). On account of these things is it defiled, and therefore is it renewed.
verses.text: And the angel said to me, Because it beholds the lawlessness and unrighteousness of men, namely fornications, adulteries, thefts, extortions, idolatries, drunkenness, murders, strife, jealousies, evil-speakings, murmurings, whisperings, divinations, and such like, which are not well-pleasing to Elohim. On account of these things is it defiled, and therefore is it renewed.

verses.raw: But thou askest concerning the bird, how it is exhausted. Because by restraining the rays of the sun through the fire and burning heat of the whole day, it is exhausted thereby.

verses.raw: I have proved, accordingly, that not only have men triumphed over their sufferings, but that a woman also has despised the most dreadful tortures.

verses.raw: ‘ Ah, thrice wretched me, and more than thrice wretched !
verses.text: ‘ Ah, thrice wretched me, and more than thrice wretched !

verses.raw: Seven children have I borne and am left childless! In vain was I seven times with child, and to no profit was my ten months’ burden seven times borne, and fruitless have been my nursings, and sorrowful my sucklings.
verses.text: Seven children have I borne and am left childless! In vain was I seven times with child, and to no profit was my ten months’ burden seven times borne, and fruitless have been my nursings, and sorrowful my sucklings.

verses.raw: In vain for you, O my sons, did I endure the many pangs of labour, and the more difficult cares of your upbringing.
verses.text: In vain for you, O my sons, did I endure the many pangs of labour, and the more difficult cares of your upbringing.

verses.raw: Alas, for my sons, that some were yet unwed, and those that were wedded had begotten no children; I shall never see children of yours, nor shall I be called by the name of grandparent.
verses.text: Alas, for my sons, that some were yet unwed, and those that were wedded had begotten no children; I shall never see children of yours, nor shall I be called by the name of grandparent.

verses.raw: Ah me, that had many beautiful children, and am a widow and desolate in my woe!
verses.text: Ah me, that had many beautiful children, and am a widow and desolate in my woe!

verses.raw: Neither will there be any son to bury me when I am dead!’
verses.text: Neither will there be any son to bury me when I am dead!’

verses.raw: but, as though she had a soul of adamant and were bringing forth the number of her sons, for a second time, into immortal life, she besought rather and entreated of them that they should die for religion’s sake.

verses.raw: O mother, warrior of Elohim (God) in the cause of religion, old and a woman, thou didst both defeat the tyrant by thy endurance, and wast found stronger than a man, in deeds as well as words.
verses.text: O mother, warrior of Elohim in the cause of religion, old and a woman, thou didst both defeat the tyrant by thy endurance, and wast found stronger than a man, in deeds as well as words.

verses.raw: For verily when thou wast put in bonds with thy sons, thou stoodest there seeing Eleazar being tortured, and thou spakest to thy sons in the Hebrew tongue:

verses.raw: ‘ My sons, noble is the fight; and do ye, being called thereto to bear witness for our nation, fight therein zealously on behalf of the Law of our fathers.
verses.text: ‘ My sons, noble is the fight; and do ye, being called thereto to bear witness for our nation, fight therein zealously on behalf of the Law of our fathers.

verses.raw: For it would be shameful if, while this aged man endured the agony for religion’s sake, you that are young men shrank before the pain.
verses.text: For it would be shameful if, while this aged man endured the agony for religion’s sake, you that are young men shrank before the pain.

verses.raw: Remember that for the sake of Elohim (God) ye have come into the world, and have enjoyed life, and that therefore ye owe it to Elohim (God) to endure all pain for his sake;
verses.text: Remember that for the sake of Elohim ye have come into the world, and have enjoyed life, and that therefore ye owe it to Elohim to endure all pain for his sake;

verses.raw: for whom also our father Abraham made haste to sacrifice his son Isaac, the ancestor of our nation; and Isaac, seeing his father’s hand lifting the knife against him, did not shrink.

verses.text: Now these are the words that the mother of the seven sons, the righteous woman, spake to her children:

verses.raw: “ I was a pure maiden, and I strayed not from my father’s house, and I kept guard over the rib that was builded into Eve.
verses.text: “ I was a pure maiden, and I strayed not from my father’s house, and I kept guard over the rib that was builded into Eve.

verses.text: No seducer of the desert, no deceiver in the field, corrupted me;

verses.text: Happy was he; for he lived a life blessed with children, and he never knew the pain of their loss.

verses.raw: Who, while he was yet with us, taught you the Law and the prophets. He read to us of Abel who was slain by Cain, and of Isaac who was offered as a burnt-offering, and of Joseph in the prison.
verses.text: Who, while he was yet with us, taught you the Law and the prophets. He read to us of Abel who was slain by Cain, and of Isaac who was offered as a burnt-offering, and of Joseph in the prison.

verses.text: And he spake to us of Phineas, the zealous priest, and he taught you the song of Ananias, Azarias, and Mishael in the fire.

verses.text: He quoted to us the proverb of Solomon, “ He is a tree of life to all them that do his will.’

verses.raw: O Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord), King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who exulteth in his confidence and strength.

verses.raw: It is thou, the Creator of all, Yahuah (Lord) of the universe, who art a righteous Governor, and judgest all who act with pride and insolence.

verses.text: Whoever shall inform against the Yahudim , besides receiving the property of the person charged, shall be presented with two thousand drachmæ from the royal treasury, shall be made free, and shall be crowned.

verses.raw: Whatever place shall shelter a Yahudi (Jew), shall, when he is hunted forth, be put under the ban of fire, and be for ever rendered useless to every living being for all time to come.
verses.text: Whatever place shall shelter a Yahudi, shall, when he is hunted forth, be put under the ban of fire, and be for ever rendered useless to every living being for all time to come.

verses.raw: Such was the purport of the king's letter.
verses.text: Such was the purport of the king's letter.

verses.raw: Wherever this decree was received, the people kept up a revelry of joy and shouting; as if their long-pent-up, hardened hatred, were now to shew itself openly.
verses.text: Wherever this decree was received, the people kept up a revelry of joy and shouting; as if their long-pent-up, hardened hatred, were now to shew itself openly.

verses.raw: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
verses.text: The Yahudim suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.

verses.raw: What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation?
verses.text: What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation?

verses.raw: They were sent out unanimously by the generals in the several cities, with such stern and pitiless feeling, that the exceptional nature of the infliction moved even some of their enemies. These, influenced by sentiments of common humanity, and reflecting upon the uncertain issue of life, shed tears at this their miserable expulsion.

These, influenced by sentiments of common humanity, and reflecting upon the uncertain issue of life, shed tears at this their miserable expulsion.

verses.raw: A multitude of aged hoary-haired men, were driven along with halting bending feet, urged onward by the impulse of a violent, shameless force to quick speed.
verses.text: A multitude of aged hoary-haired men, were driven along with halting bending feet, urged onward by the impulse of a violent, shameless force to quick speed.

verses.raw: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled, and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn.
verses.text: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled, and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn.

verses.raw: Bound, and exposed to public gaze, they were hurried violently on board ship.
verses.text: Bound, and exposed to public gaze, they were hurried violently on board ship.

verses.raw: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand.
verses.text: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand.

verses.raw: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
verses.text: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.

verses.raw: The planks of the deck above them barred out the light, and shut out the day on every side, so that they might be treated like traitors during the whole voyage.
verses.text: The planks of the deck above them barred out the light, and shut out the day on every side, so that they might be treated like traitors during the whole voyage.

verses.raw: They were conveyed accordingly in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces; nay, were deemed unworthy of any civilized accommodation.

verses.raw: When this was done, the king, hearing that their brethren in the city often went out and lamented the melancholy distress of these victims,
verses.text: When this was done, the king, hearing that their brethren in the city often went out and lamented the melancholy distress of these victims,

verses.raw: was full of rage, and commanded that they should be carefully subjected to the same (and not one whit milder) treatment.
verses.text: was full of rage, and commanded that they should be carefully subjected to the same (and not one whit milder) treatment.

verses.raw: The whole nation was now to be registered. Every individual was to be specified by name; not for that hard servitude of labour which we have a little before mentioned, but that he might expose them to the before-mentioned tortures; and finally, in the short space of a day, might extirpate them by his cruelties.
verses.text: The whole nation was now to be registered. Every individual was to be specified by name; not for that hard servitude of labour which we have a little before mentioned, but that he might expose them to the before-mentioned tortures; and finally, in the short space of a day, might extirpate them by his cruelties.

verses.raw: The registering of these men was carried on cruelly, zealously, assiduously, from the rising of the sun to its going down, and was not brought to an end in forty days.
verses.text: The registering of these men was carried on cruelly, zealously, assiduously, from the rising of the sun to its going down, and was not brought to an end in forty days.

verses.raw: The king was filled with great and constant joy, and celebrated banquets before the temple idols. His erring heart, far from the truth, and his profane mouth, gave glory to idols, deaf and incapable of speaking or aiding, and uttered unworthy speech against the Greatest Elohim (God).
verses.text: The king was filled with great and constant joy, and celebrated banquets before the temple idols. His erring heart, far from the truth, and his profane mouth, gave glory to idols, deaf and incapable of speaking or aiding, and uttered unworthy speech against the Greatest Elohim.

verses.raw: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Yahudim (Jews) was too great for registration,
verses.text: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Yahudim was too great for registration,

verses.raw: inasmuch as there were many still left in the land, of whom some were in inhabited houses, and others were scattered about in various places; so that all the commanders in Egypt were insufficient for the work.
verses.text: inasmuch as there were many still left in the land, of whom some were in inhabited houses, and others were scattered about in various places; so that all the commanders in Egypt were insufficient for the work.

verses.raw: The king threatened them, and charged them with taking bribes, in order to contrive the escape of the Yahudim (Jews) : but was clearly convinced of the truth of what had been said.
verses.text: The king threatened them, and charged them with taking bribes, in order to contrive the escape of the Yahudim : but was clearly convinced of the truth of what had been said.

verses.raw: They said, and proved, that paper and pens had failed them for the carrying out of their purpose.
verses.text: They said, and proved, that paper and pens had failed them for the carrying out of their purpose.

verses.raw: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
verses.text: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim from heaven.

verses.raw: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
verses.text: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,

verses.raw: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine and handfuls of incense [infused] to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious draughts of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Yahudim (Jews).

verses.raw: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Yahudim (Jews) the most.
verses.text: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Yahudim the most.

verses.raw: The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually.
verses.text: The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually.

verses.raw: The underlings appointed for the purpose went out about eventide and bound the hands of the miserable victims, and took other precautions for their security at night, thinking that the whole race would perish together.
verses.text: The underlings appointed for the purpose went out about eventide and bound the hands of the miserable victims, and took other precautions for their security at night, thinking that the whole race would perish together.

verses.raw: The heathen believed the Yahudim (Jews) to be destitute of all protection; for chains fettered them about.
verses.text: The heathen believed the Yahudim to be destitute of all protection; for chains fettered them about.

verses.raw: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah (Lord), and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim (God) and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah (Lord) of every power,
verses.text: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah, and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah of every power,

verses.raw: to overthrow the evil purpose which was gone out against them, and to deliver them by extraordinary manifestation from that death which was in store for them.
verses.text: to overthrow the evil purpose which was gone out against them, and to deliver them by extraordinary manifestation from that death which was in store for them.

verses.raw: Their litany so earnest went up to heaven.
verses.text: Their litany so earnest went up to heaven.

verses.raw: Then Hermon, who had filled his merciless elephants with copious draughts of mingled wine and frankincense, came early to the palace to certify the king thereof.
verses.text: Then Hermon, who had filled his merciless elephants with copious draughts of mingled wine and frankincense, came early to the palace to certify the king thereof.

verses.raw: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time, by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion thereof [now] upon the king.
verses.text: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time, by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion thereof [now] upon the king.

verses.raw: By this sweet and profound influence of Yahuah (Lord) he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.
verses.text: By this sweet and profound influence of Yahuah he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.

verses.raw: But the Yahudim (Jews), having escaped the hour which had been fixed, praised their holy Elohim (God), and again prayed him who is easily reconciled to display the power of his powerful hand to the overweening Gentiles.
verses.text: But the Yahudim, having escaped the hour which had been fixed, praised their holy Elohim, and again prayed him who is easily reconciled to display the power of his powerful hand to the overweening Gentiles.

verses.raw: The middle of the tenth hour had well nigh arrived, when the master-bidder, seeing the guests who were bidden collected, came and shook the king.
verses.text: The middle of the tenth hour had well nigh arrived, when the master-bidder, seeing the guests who were bidden collected, came and shook the king.

verses.raw: He gained his attention with difficulty, and hinting that the mealtime was getting past, talked the matter over with him.
verses.text: He gained his attention with difficulty, and hinting that the mealtime was getting past, talked the matter over with him.

verses.raw: The king listened to this, and then turning aside to his potations, commanded the guests to sit down before him.
verses.text: The king listened to this, and then turning aside to his potations, commanded the guests to sit down before him.

verses.raw: This done, he asked them to enjoy themselves, and to indulge in mirth at this somewhat late hour of the banquet.
verses.text: This done, he asked them to enjoy themselves, and to indulge in mirth at this somewhat late hour of the banquet.

verses.raw: Conversation grew on, and the king sent for Hermon, and enquired of him, with fierce denunciations, why the Yahudim (Jews) had been allowed to outlive that day.
verses.text: Conversation grew on, and the king sent for Hermon, and enquired of him, with fierce denunciations, why the Yahudim had been allowed to outlive that day.

verses.raw: Hermon explained that he had done his bidding over night; and in this he was confirmed by his friends.
verses.text: Hermon explained that he had done his bidding over night; and in this he was confirmed by his friends.

verses.raw: The king, then, with a barbarity exceeding that of Phalaris, said, That they might thank his sleep of that day. Lose no time, and get ready the elephants against to-morrow, as you did before, for the destruction of these accursed Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: The king, then, with a barbarity exceeding that of Phalaris, said, That they might thank his sleep of that day. Lose no time, and get ready the elephants against to-morrow, as you did before, for the destruction of these accursed Yahudim.

verses.raw: When the king said this, the company present were glad, and approved; and then each man went to his own home.
verses.text: When the king said this, the company present were glad, and approved; and then each man went to his own home.

verses.raw: Nor did they employ the night in sleep, so much as in contriving cruel mockeries for those deemed miserable.
verses.text: Nor did they employ the night in sleep, so much as in contriving cruel mockeries for those deemed miserable.

verses.raw: The morning cock had just crowed, and Hermon, having harnessed the brutes, was stimulating them in the great colonnade.
verses.text: The morning cock had just crowed, and Hermon, having harnessed the brutes, was stimulating them in the great colonnade.

verses.raw: The city crowds were collected together to see the hideous spectacle, and waited impatiently for the dawn.
verses.text: The city crowds were collected together to see the hideous spectacle, and waited impatiently for the dawn.

verses.raw: The Yahudim (Jews), breathless with momentary suspense, stretched forth their hands, and prayed the Greatest Elohim (God), in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.
verses.text: The Yahudim, breathless with momentary suspense, stretched forth their hands, and prayed the Greatest Elohim, in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.

verses.raw: The sun's rays were not yet shed abroad, and the king was waiting for his friends, when Hermon came to him, calling him out, and saying, That his desires could now be realized.
verses.text: The sun's rays were not yet shed abroad, and the king was waiting for his friends, when Hermon came to him, calling him out, and saying, That his desires could now be realized.

verses.raw: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unwonted exit; and, overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, enquired the object of this earnest preparation.
verses.text: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unwonted exit; and, overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, enquired the object of this earnest preparation.

verses.raw: But this was the working of that El Shaddai (Almighty God) who had made him forget all his purpose.
verses.text: But this was the working of that El Shaddai who had made him forget all his purpose.

verses.raw: Hermon, and all his friends, pointed out the preparation of the animals. They are ready, O king, according to your own strict injunction.
verses.text: Hermon, and all his friends, pointed out the preparation of the animals. They are ready, O king, according to your own strict injunction.

verses.raw: The king was filled with fierce anger at these words; for, by the Providence of Elohim (God) regarding these things, his mind had become entirely confused. He looked hard at Hermon, and threatened him as follows:
verses.text: The king was filled with fierce anger at these words; for, by the Providence of Elohim regarding these things, his mind had become entirely confused. He looked hard at Hermon, and threatened him as follows:

verses.raw: Your parents, or your children, were they here, to these wild beasts a large repast they should have furnished; not these innocent Yahudim (Jews), who me and my forefathers loyally have served.
verses.text: Your parents, or your children, were they here, to these wild beasts a large repast they should have furnished; not these innocent Yahudim, who me and my forefathers loyally have served.

verses.raw: Had it not been for familiar friendship, and the claims of your office, your life should have gone for theirs.
verses.text: Had it not been for familiar friendship, and the claims of your office, your life should have gone for theirs.

verses.raw: Hermon, being threatened in this unexpected and alarming manner, was troubled in visage, and depressed in countenance.
verses.text: Hermon, being threatened in this unexpected and alarming manner, was troubled in visage, and depressed in countenance.

verses.raw: The friends, too, stole out one by one, and dismissed the assembled multitudes to their occupations.
verses.text: The friends, too, stole out one by one, and dismissed the assembled multitudes to their occupations.

verses.raw: The Yahudim (Jews), having heard of these events, praised the glorious Elohim (God) and King of kings, because they had obtained this help, too, from him.
verses.text: The Yahudim, having heard of these events, praised the glorious Elohim and King of kings, because they had obtained this help, too, from him.

verses.raw: Now the king arranged another banquet after the same manner, and proclaimed an invitation to mirth.
verses.text: Now the king arranged another banquet after the same manner, and proclaimed an invitation to mirth.

verses.raw: And he summoned Hermon to his presence, and said, with threats, How often, O wretch, must I repeat my orders to thee about these same persons?
verses.text: And he summoned Hermon to his presence, and said, with threats, How often, O wretch, must I repeat my orders to thee about these same persons?

verses.raw: Once more, arm the elephants against the morrow for the extermination of the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: Once more, arm the elephants against the morrow for the extermination of the Yahudim.

verses.raw: His kinsmen, who were reclining with him, wondered at his instability, and thus expressed themselves:
verses.text: His kinsmen, who were reclining with him, wondered at his instability, and thus expressed themselves:

verses.raw: O king, how long dost thou make trial of us, as of men bereft of reason? This is the third time that thou hast ordered their destruction. When the thing is to be done, thou changest thy mind, and recallest thy instructions.
verses.text: O king, how long dost thou make trial of us, as of men bereft of reason? This is the third time that thou hast ordered their destruction. When the thing is to be done, thou changest thy mind, and recallest thy instructions.

verses.raw: For this cause the feeling of expectation causes tumult in the city: it swarms with factions; and is continually on the point of being plundered.
verses.text: For this cause the feeling of expectation causes tumult in the city: it swarms with factions; and is continually on the point of being plundered.

verses.raw: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Yahudim (Jews). He swore a fruitless oath, and determined forthwith to send them to Hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.
verses.text: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Yahudim. He swore a fruitless oath, and determined forthwith to send them to Hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.

verses.raw: He would also invade Judea, and level its towns with fire and the sword; and destroy that temple which the heathen might not enter, and prevent sacrifices ever after being offered up there.
verses.text: He would also invade Judea, and level its towns with fire and the sword; and destroy that temple which the heathen might not enter, and prevent sacrifices ever after being offered up there.

verses.raw: Joyfully his friends broke up, together with his kinsmen; and, trusting in his determination, arranged their forces in guard at the most convenient places of the city.
verses.text: Joyfully his friends broke up, together with his kinsmen; and, trusting in his determination, arranged their forces in guard at the most convenient places of the city.

verses.raw: And the master of the elephants urged the beasts into an almost maniacal state, drenched them with incense and wine, and decked them with frightful instruments.
verses.text: And the master of the elephants urged the beasts into an almost maniacal state, drenched them with incense and wine, and decked them with frightful instruments.

verses.raw: About early morning, when the city was now filled with an immense number of people at the hippodrome, he entered the palace, and called the king to the business in hand.
verses.text: About early morning, when the city was now filled with an immense number of people at the hippodrome, he entered the palace, and called the king to the business in hand.

verses.raw: The king's heart teemed with impious rage; and he rushed forth with the mass, along with the elephants. With feelings unsoftened, and eyes pitiless, he longed to gaze at the hard and wretched doom of the above-mentioned Yahudim (Jews) .

verses.raw: But the Yahudim (Jews) , when the elephants went out at the gate, followed by the armed force; and when they saw the dust raised by the throng, and heard the loud cries of the crowd,
verses.text: But the Yahudim , when the elephants went out at the gate, followed by the armed force; and when they saw the dust raised by the throng, and heard the loud cries of the crowd,

verses.raw: thought that they had come to the last moment of their lives, to the end of what they had tremblingly expected. They gave way, therefore, to lamentations and moans: they kissed each other: those nearest of kin to each other hung about one another's necks: fathers about their sons, mothers their daughters: other women held their infants to their breasts, which drew what seemed their last milk.

verses.raw: sent up an exceeding great cry, entreating Yahuah (Lord) of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of Hades.
verses.text: sent up an exceeding great cry, entreating Yahuah of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of Hades.

verses.raw: And Eleazar, an illustrious priest of the country, who had attained to length of days, and whose life had been adorned with virtue, caused the presbyters who were about him to cease to cry out to the holy Elohim (God), and prayed thus:
verses.text: And Eleazar, an illustrious priest of the country, who had attained to length of days, and whose life had been adorned with virtue, caused the presbyters who were about him to cease to cry out to the holy Elohim, and prayed thus:

verses.raw: O King, mighty in power, most high, El Shaddai (Almighty God), who regulatest the whole creation with thy tender mercy,
verses.text: O King, mighty in power, most high, El Shaddai, who regulatest the whole creation with thy tender mercy,

verses.raw: look upon the seed of Abraham, upon the children of the sanctified Jacob, thy sanctified inheritance, O Father, now being wrongfully destroyed as strangers in a strange land.
verses.text: look upon the seed of Abraham, upon the children of the sanctified Jacob, thy sanctified inheritance, O Father, now being wrongfully destroyed as strangers in a strange land.

verses.raw: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.
verses.text: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el, thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.

verses.raw: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah (Lord), didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.
verses.text: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah, didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.

verses.raw: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.
verses.text: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.

verses.raw: It was thou who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, didst bring him back again unhurt to light.
verses.text: It was thou who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, didst bring him back again unhurt to light.

verses.raw: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
verses.text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.

verses.raw: And now, thou who hatest insolence; thou who dost abound in mercy; thou who art the protector of all things; appear quickly to those of the race of Yashar'el (Israel), who are insulted by abhorred, lawless Gentiles.
verses.text: And now, thou who hatest insolence; thou who dost abound in mercy; thou who art the protector of all things; appear quickly to those of the race of Yashar'el, who are insulted by abhorred, lawless Gentiles.

verses.raw: If our life has during our exile been stained with iniquity, deliver us from the hand of the enemy, and destroy us, O Yahuah (Lord), by the death which thou preferrest.
verses.text: If our life has during our exile been stained with iniquity, deliver us from the hand of the enemy, and destroy us, O Yahuah, by the death which thou preferrest.

verses.raw: Let not the vain-minded congratulate vain idols at the destruction of thy beloved, saying, Neither did their Elohim (God) deliver them.
verses.text: Let not the vain-minded congratulate vain idols at the destruction of thy beloved, saying, Neither did their Elohim deliver them.

verses.raw: Thou who art All-powerful and Almighty, O Eternal One, behold! have mercy upon us who are being withdrawn from life, like traitors, by the unreasoning insolence of lawless men.
verses.text: Thou who art All-powerful and Almighty, O Eternal One, behold! have mercy upon us who are being withdrawn from life, like traitors, by the unreasoning insolence of lawless men.

verses.raw: Let the heathen cower before thy invincible might to-day, O glorious One, who hast all power to save the race of Jacob.
verses.text: Let the heathen cower before thy invincible might to-day, O glorious One, who hast all power to save the race of Jacob.

verses.raw: The whole band of infants and their parents with tears beseech thee.
verses.text: The whole band of infants and their parents with tears beseech thee.

verses.raw: Let it be shewn to all the nations that thou art with us, O Yahuah (Lord), and hast not turned thy face away from us; but as thou saidst that thou wouldst not forget them even in the land of their enemies, so do thou fulfil this saying, O Yahuah (Lord).
verses.text: Let it be shewn to all the nations that thou art with us, O Yahuah, and hast not turned thy face away from us; but as thou saidst that thou wouldst not forget them even in the land of their enemies, so do thou fulfil this saying, O Yahuah.

verses.raw: Now, at the time that Eleazar had ended his prayer, the king came along to the hippodrome, with the wild beasts, and with his tumultuous power.
verses.text: Now, at the time that Eleazar had ended his prayer, the king came along to the hippodrome, with the wild beasts, and with his tumultuous power.

verses.raw: When the Yahudim (Jews) saw this, they uttered a loud cry to heaven, so that the adjacent valleys resounded, and caused an irrepressible lamentation throughout the army.
verses.text: When the Yahudim saw this, they uttered a loud cry to heaven, so that the adjacent valleys resounded, and caused an irrepressible lamentation throughout the army.

verses.raw: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
verses.text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim, displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim.

verses.raw: And they stood opposite, and filled the enemies' host with confusion and cowardice; and bound them with immoveable fetters.
verses.text: And they stood opposite, and filled the enemies' host with confusion and cowardice; and bound them with immoveable fetters.

verses.raw: And a cold shudder came over the person of the king, and oblivion paralysed the vehemence of his spirit.
verses.text: And a cold shudder came over the person of the king, and oblivion paralysed the vehemence of his spirit.

verses.raw: They turned back the animals upon the armed forces which followed them; and the animals trod them down, and destroyed them.
verses.text: They turned back the animals upon the armed forces which followed them; and the animals trod them down, and destroyed them.

verses.raw: The king's wrath was converted into compassion; and he wept at his own machinations.
verses.text: The king's wrath was converted into compassion; and he wept at his own machinations.

verses.raw: For when he heard the cry, and saw them all on the verge of destruction, with tears he angrily threatened his friends, saying,
verses.text: For when he heard the cry, and saw them all on the verge of destruction, with tears he angrily threatened his friends, saying,

verses.raw: Ye have governed badly; and have exceeded tyrants in cruelty; and me your benefactor ye have laboured to deprive at once of my dominion and my life, by secretly devising measures injurious to the kingdom.
verses.text: Ye have governed badly; and have exceeded tyrants in cruelty; and me your benefactor ye have laboured to deprive at once of my dominion and my life, by secretly devising measures injurious to the kingdom.

verses.raw: Who has gathered here, unreasonably removing each from his home, those who, in fidelity to us, had held the fortresses of the country?
verses.text: Who has gathered here, unreasonably removing each from his home, those who, in fidelity to us, had held the fortresses of the country?

verses.raw: Who has thus consigned to unmerited punishments those who in good will towards us from the beginning have in all things surpassed all nations, and who often have engaged in the most dangerous undertakings?
verses.text: Who has thus consigned to unmerited punishments those who in good will towards us from the beginning have in all things surpassed all nations, and who often have engaged in the most dangerous undertakings?

verses.raw: Loose, loose the unjust bonds; send them to their homes in peace, and deprecate what has been done.
verses.text: Loose, loose the unjust bonds; send them to their homes in peace, and deprecate what has been done.

verses.raw: Release the sons of the almighty living Elohim (God) of heaven, who from our ancestors' times until now has granted a glorious and uninterrupted prosperity to our affairs.
verses.text: Release the sons of the almighty living Elohim of heaven, who from our ancestors' times until now has granted a glorious and uninterrupted prosperity to our affairs.

verses.raw: These things he said: and they, released the same moment, having now escaped death, praised Elohim (God) their holy Saviour.
verses.text: These things he said: and they, released the same moment, having now escaped death, praised Elohim their holy Saviour.

verses.raw: The king then departed to the city, and called his financier to him, and bade him provide a seven days' quantity of wine and other materials for feasting for the Yahudim (Jews). He decided that they should keep a gladsome festival of deliverance in the very place in which they expected to meet with their destruction.
verses.text: The king then departed to the city, and called his financier to him, and bade him provide a seven days' quantity of wine and other materials for feasting for the Yahudim. He decided that they should keep a gladsome festival of deliverance in the very place in which they expected to meet with their destruction.

verses.raw: Then they who were before despised and nigh unto Hades, yea, rather advanced into it, partook of the cup of salvation, instead of a grievous and lamentable death. Full of exultation, they parted out the place intended for their fall and burial into banqueting booths.
verses.text: Then they who were before despised and nigh unto Hades, yea, rather advanced into it, partook of the cup of salvation, instead of a grievous and lamentable death. Full of exultation, they parted out the place intended for their fall and burial into banqueting booths.

verses.raw: Ceasing their miserable strain of woe, they took up the subject of their fatherland, hymning in praise Elohim (God) their wonder-working Saviour. All groans, all wailing, were laid aside: they formed dances in token of serene joy.
verses.text: Ceasing their miserable strain of woe, they took up the subject of their fatherland, hymning in praise Elohim their wonder-working Saviour. All groans, all wailing, were laid aside: they formed dances in token of serene joy.

verses.raw: So, also, the king collected a number of guests for the occasion, and returned unceasing thanks with much magnificence for the unexpected deliverance afforded him.
verses.text: So, also, the king collected a number of guests for the occasion, and returned unceasing thanks with much magnificence for the unexpected deliverance afforded him.

verses.raw: Those who had marked them out as for death and for carrion, and had registered them with joy, howled aloud, and were clothed with shame, and had the fire of their rage ingloriously put out.
verses.text: Those who had marked them out as for death and for carrion, and had registered them with joy, howled aloud, and were clothed with shame, and had the fire of their rage ingloriously put out.

verses.raw: But the Yahudim (Jews), as we just said, instituted a dance, and then gave themselves up to feasting, glad thanksgivings, and psalms.
verses.text: But the Yahudim, as we just said, instituted a dance, and then gave themselves up to feasting, glad thanksgivings, and psalms.

verses.raw: They made a public ordinance to commemorate these things for generations to come, as long as they should be sojourners. They thus established these days as days of mirth, not for the purpose of drinking or luxury, but because Elohim (God) had saved them.
verses.text: They made a public ordinance to commemorate these things for generations to come, as long as they should be sojourners. They thus established these days as days of mirth, not for the purpose of drinking or luxury, but because Elohim had saved them.

verses.raw: They requested the king to send them back to their homes.
verses.text: They requested the king to send them back to their homes.

verses.raw: They were being enrolled from the twenty-fifth of Pachon to the fourth of Epiphi, a period of forty days: the measures taken for their destruction lasted from the fifth of Epiphi till the seventh, that is, three days.
verses.text: They were being enrolled from the twenty-fifth of Pachon to the fourth of Epiphi, a period of forty days: the measures taken for their destruction lasted from the fifth of Epiphi till the seventh, that is, three days.

verses.raw: The Ruler over all did during this time manifest forth his mercy gloriously, and did deliver them all together unharmed.
verses.text: The Ruler over all did during this time manifest forth his mercy gloriously, and did deliver them all together unharmed.

verses.raw: They feasted upon the king's provision up to the fourteenth day, and then asked to be sent away.
verses.text: They feasted upon the king's provision up to the fourteenth day, and then asked to be sent away.

verses.raw: The king commended them, and wrote the subjoined letter, of magnanimous import for them, to the commanders of every city.
verses.text: The king commended them, and wrote the subjoined letter, of magnanimous import for them, to the commanders of every city.

verses.raw: King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders throughout Egypt, and to all who are set over affairs, joy and strength.
verses.text: King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders throughout Egypt, and to all who are set over affairs, joy and strength.

verses.raw: We, too, and our children are well; and Elohim (God) has directed our affairs as we wish.
verses.text: We, too, and our children are well; and Elohim has directed our affairs as we wish.

verses.raw: Certain of our friends did of malice vehemently urge us to punish the Yahudim (Jews) of our realm in a body, with the infliction of a monstrous punishment.
verses.text: Certain of our friends did of malice vehemently urge us to punish the Yahudim of our realm in a body, with the infliction of a monstrous punishment.

verses.raw: They pretended that our affairs would never be in a good state till this took place. Such, they said, was the hatred borne by the Yahudim (Jews) to all other people.
verses.text: They pretended that our affairs would never be in a good state till this took place. Such, they said, was the hatred borne by the Yahudim to all other people.

verses.raw: They brought them fettered in grievous chains as slaves, nay, as traitors. Without enquiry or examination they endeavoured to annihilate them. They buckled themselves with a savage cruelty, worse than Scythian custom.
verses.text: They brought them fettered in grievous chains as slaves, nay, as traitors. Without enquiry or examination they endeavoured to annihilate them. They buckled themselves with a savage cruelty, worse than Scythian custom.

verses.raw: For this cause we severely threatened them; yet, with the clemency which we are wont to extend to all men, we at length permitted them to live. Finding that the Elohim (God) of heaven cast a shield of protection over the Yahudim (Jews) so as to preserve them, and that he fought for them as a father always fights for his sons;
verses.text: For this cause we severely threatened them; yet, with the clemency which we are wont to extend to all men, we at length permitted them to live. Finding that the Elohim of heaven cast a shield of protection over the Yahudim so as to preserve them, and that he fought for them as a father always fights for his sons;

verses.raw: and taking into consideration their constancy and fidelity towards us and towards our ancestors, we have, as we ought, acquitted them of every sort of charge.
verses.text: and taking into consideration their constancy and fidelity towards us and towards our ancestors, we have, as we ought, acquitted them of every sort of charge.

verses.raw: And we have dismissed them to their several homes; bidding all men everywhere to do them no wrong, or unrighteously revile them about the past.
verses.text: And we have dismissed them to their several homes; bidding all men everywhere to do them no wrong, or unrighteously revile them about the past.

verses.raw: For know ye, that should we conceive any evil design against, or in any manner aggrieve them, we shall ever have as our opposite, not man, but the highest Elohim (God), the ruler of all might. From Him there will be no escape, as the avenger of such deeds. Fare ye well.
verses.text: For know ye, that should we conceive any evil design against, or in any manner aggrieve them, we shall ever have as our opposite, not man, but the highest Elohim, the ruler of all might. From Him there will be no escape, as the avenger of such deeds. Fare ye well.

verses.raw: When they had received this letter, they were not forward to depart immediately. They petitioned the king to be allowed to inflict fitting punishment upon those of their race who had willingly transgressed the holy Elohim (God), and the law of Elohim (God).
verses.text: When they had received this letter, they were not forward to depart immediately. They petitioned the king to be allowed to inflict fitting punishment upon those of their race who had willingly transgressed the holy Elohim, and the law of Elohim.

verses.raw: They alleged that men who had for their bellies' sake transgressed the ordinances of Elohim (God), would never be faithful to the interests of the king.
verses.text: They alleged that men who had for their bellies' sake transgressed the ordinances of Elohim, would never be faithful to the interests of the king.

verses.raw: The king admitted the truth of this reasoning, and commended them. Full power was given them, without warrant or special commission, to destroy those who had transgressed the law of Elohim (God) boldly in every part of the king's dominions.
verses.text: The king admitted the truth of this reasoning, and commended them. Full power was given them, without warrant or special commission, to destroy those who had transgressed the law of Elohim boldly in every part of the king's dominions.

verses.raw: Their priests, then, as it was meet, saluted him with good wishes, and all the people echoed with the Hallelujah. They then joyfully departed.
verses.text: Their priests, then, as it was meet, saluted him with good wishes, and all the people echoed with the Hallelujah. They then joyfully departed.

verses.raw: Then they punished and destroyed with ignominy every polluted Yahudi (Jew) that fell in their way;
verses.text: Then they punished and destroyed with ignominy every polluted Yahudi that fell in their way;

verses.raw: slaying thus, in that day, above three hundred men, and esteeming this destruction of the wicked a season of joy.
verses.text: slaying thus, in that day, above three hundred men, and esteeming this destruction of the wicked a season of joy.

verses.raw: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
verses.text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el.

verses.raw: Having arrived at Ptolemais, called from the specialty of that district Rose-bearing, where the fleet, in accordance with the general wish, waited for them seven days,
verses.text: Having arrived at Ptolemais, called from the specialty of that district Rose-bearing, where the fleet, in accordance with the general wish, waited for them seven days,

verses.raw: they partook of a banquet of deliverance, for the king generously granted them severally the means of securing a return home.
verses.text: they partook of a banquet of deliverance, for the king generously granted them severally the means of securing a return home.

verses.raw: They were accordingly brought back in peace, while they gave utterance to becoming thanks; and they determined to keep these days during their sojourn as days of joyfulness.
verses.text: They were accordingly brought back in peace, while they gave utterance to becoming thanks; and they determined to keep these days during their sojourn as days of joyfulness.

verses.raw: These they registered as sacred upon a pillar, when they had dedicated the place of their festivity to be one of prayer. They departed unharmed, free, abundant in joy, preserved by the king's command, by land, by sea, and by river, each to his own home.
verses.text: These they registered as sacred upon a pillar, when they had dedicated the place of their festivity to be one of prayer. They departed unharmed, free, abundant in joy, preserved by the king's command, by land, by sea, and by river, each to his own home.

verses.raw: They had more weight than before among their enemies; and were honoured and feared, and no one in any way robbed them of their goods.
verses.text: They had more weight than before among their enemies; and were honoured and feared, and no one in any way robbed them of their goods.

verses.raw: Every man received back his own, according to inventory; those who had obtained their goods, giving them up with the greatest terror. For the greatest Elohim (God) wrought with perfectness wonders for their salvation.
verses.text: Every man received back his own, according to inventory; those who had obtained their goods, giving them up with the greatest terror. For the greatest Elohim wrought with perfectness wonders for their salvation.

verses.raw: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) unto everlasting. Amen.
verses.text: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el unto everlasting. Amen.

title: The Book of James, or Protevangelium

verses.raw: Under this heading I have put together the narratives of the birth of the Virgin, and birth and childhood of our Lord. The texts which may be called 'originar are two, the Book of James (Protevangelium), and the Gospel of Thomas. The Book of James we have largely in its original form. The Gospel of Thomas seems to be the skeleton of the original, the stories retained, the speeches, which conveyed the doctrinal teaching of the book, almost entirely removed. It is in fact an expurgated edition. All the other texts are variants and embroideries upon these: some contain details which probably are derived from the original text of the Gospel of Thomas. The latter of these names is a modem one: it was given to the book by Guillaume Postel, who in the sixteenth century introduced it to Europe. Origen mentions the Book of James (and the Gospel of Peter) as stating that the * brethren of the Lord' were sons of Joseph by a former wife. This is the first mention of it, and shows us that the book is as old as the second century. To collect later references to it is unnecessary. It is generally agreed that the story of the death of Zacharias (chs. xxii-xxiv) does not properly belong to the text. Origen and other early writers give a different account of the cause of his death: it was, they say, because, after the Nativity, he still allowed Mary to take her place among the virgins in the Temple. Difficulty is also caused by the sudden introduction of Joseph as the narrator in ch. xviii. 2 sqq. We cannot be sure whether this means that a fragment of a * Joseph-apocryphon' has been introduced at this point; or, if so, how far it extends. We are sure, from a sentence of Clement of Alexandria,* that some story of a midwife being present at the Nativity was current in the second century. We have the book in the original Greek and in several oriental versions, the oldest of which is the Syriac. But, oddly enough, there is no Latin version. The matter is found in an expanded and altered form in the 'Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew*, but we have yet to find an old Latin translation of the present text. Such a thing seems to have existed, for a book identifiable with ours is condemned in the Gelasian Decree. In the early chapters the Old Testament is extensively drawn upon, and imitated; but the author is not familiar with Yahudi (Jewish) life or usages. The best recent edition of this book is a French one, by Amann. There is as yet no really critical edition of the text, in which all manu- * Strom, vii. 93, 'for after she had brought forth some say that she was attended by a midwife, and was found to be a virgin'• scripts and versions are made use of. I follow Tischendorrs in the main. 1. In the histories of the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) it is written that there was one loaeim, exceeding rich: and he offered his gifts twofold, saying: That which is of my superfluity shall be for the whole people, and that which is for my forgiveness shall be for Yahuah (Lord), for a propitiation unto me.

verses.raw: Now the great day of Yahuah (Lord) drew nigh and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) offered their gifts. And Reuben stood over against him saying: It is not lawful for thee to offer thy gifts first, forasmuch as thou hast gotten no seed in Yashar'el (Israel). 3 And loacim was sore grieved, and went imto the record of the twelve tribes of the people, saying: I will look upon the record of the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), whether I only have not gotten seed in Yashar'el (Israel). And he searched, and found concerning all the righteous that they had raised up seed in Yashar'el (Israel). And he remembered the patriarch Abra ham, how in the last days Elohim (God) gave him a son, even Isaac.
verses.text: Now the great day of Yahuah drew nigh and the children of Yashar'el offered their gifts. And Reuben stood over against him saying: It is not lawful for thee to offer thy gifts first, forasmuch as thou hast gotten no seed in Yashar'el. 3 And loacim was sore grieved, and went imto the record of the twelve tribes of the people, saying: I will look upon the record of the twelve tribes of Yashar'el, whether I only have not gotten seed in Yashar'el. And he searched, and found concerning all the righteous that they had raised up seed in Yashar'el. And he remembered the patriarch Abra ham, how in the last days Elohim gave him a son, even Isaac.

verses.raw: And loacim was sore grieved, and showed not himself to his wife, but betook himself into the wilderness, and pitched his tent there, and fasted forty days and forty nights, sajring within himself: I will not go down either for meat or for drink until Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God) visit me, and my prayer shall be unto me meat and drink.
verses.text: And loacim was sore grieved, and showed not himself to his wife, but betook himself into the wilderness, and pitched his tent there, and fasted forty days and forty nights, sajring within himself: I will not go down either for meat or for drink until Yahuah my Elohim visit me, and my prayer shall be unto me meat and drink.

title: The Book of James, or Protevangelium

verses.raw: Now his wife Anna lamented with two lamentations, and bewailed herself with two bewailings, saying: I will bewail my widowhood, and I will bewail my childlessness.
verses.text: Now his wife Anna lamented with two lamentations, and bewailed herself with two bewailings, saying: I will bewail my widowhood, and I will bewail my childlessness.

verses.raw: And the great day of Yahuah (Lord) drew nigh, and Judith her handmaid said unto her: How long humblest thou thy soul? The great day of Yahuah (Lord) hath come, and it is not lawful for thee to mourn: but take this headband, which the mistress of my work gave me, and it is not lawful for me to put it on, for asmuch as I am an handmaid, and it hath a mark of royalty. And Anna said: Get thee from me. Lo! I have done nothing (or I will not do so) and Yahuah (Lord) hath greatly humbled me: peradventure one gave it to thee in subtilty, and thou art come to make me partaker in thy sin. And Judith said: How shall I curse thee, seeing Yahuah (Lord) hath shut up thy womb, to give thee no fruit in Yashar'el (Israel) ?
verses.text: And the great day of Yahuah drew nigh, and Judith her handmaid said unto her: How long humblest thou thy soul? The great day of Yahuah hath come, and it is not lawful for thee to mourn: but take this headband, which the mistress of my work gave me, and it is not lawful for me to put it on, for asmuch as I am an handmaid, and it hath a mark of royalty. And Anna said: Get thee from me. Lo! I have done nothing (or I will not do so) and Yahuah hath greatly humbled me: peradventure one gave it to thee in subtilty, and thou art come to make me partaker in thy sin. And Judith said: How shall I curse thee, seeing Yahuah hath shut up thy womb, to give thee no fruit in Yashar'el ?

verses.raw: And Anna was sore grieved [and mourned with a great mourning because she was reproached by all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). And coming to herself she said: What shall I do? I will pray with weeping unto Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God) that he visit me]. And she put off her momning garments and cleansed (or adorned) her head and put on her bridal garments: and about the ninth hour she went down into the garden to walk there. And she saw a laiu*el-tree and sat down underneath it and besought Yahuah (Lord) saying; O Elohim (God) of our fathers, bless me, and hearken unto my prayer, as thou didst bless the womb of Sarah, and gavest her a son, even Isaac.
verses.text: And Anna was sore grieved [and mourned with a great mourning because she was reproached by all the tribes of Yashar'el. And coming to herself she said: What shall I do? I will pray with weeping unto Yahuah my Elohim that he visit me]. And she put off her momning garments and cleansed (or adorned) her head and put on her bridal garments: and about the ninth hour she went down into the garden to walk there. And she saw a laiu*el-tree and sat down underneath it and besought Yahuah saying; O Elohim of our fathers, bless me, and hearken unto my prayer, as thou didst bless the womb of Sarah, and gavest her a son, even Isaac.

title: The Book of James, or Protevangelium

verses.raw: And looking up to the heaven she espied a nest of sparrows in the laurel-tree, and made a lamentation within herself, saying: Woe unto me, who begat me ? And what womb brought me forth, for I am become a curse before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and I am reproached, and they have mocked me forth out of the temple of Yahuah (Lord)? 2 Woe unto me, unto what am I likened ? I am not likened unto the fowls of the heaven, for even the fowls of the heaven are fruitful before thee, O Yahuah (Lord). Woe unto me, unto what am I likened? I am not likened unto the beasts of the earth, for even the beasts of the earth are fruitful before thee, O Yahuah (Lord). Woe unto me, unto what am I likened? I am not likened unto these waters, for even these waters are fruitful before thee, O Yahuah (Lord). 3 Woe unto me, unto what am I likened ? I am not likened unto this earth, for even this earth bringeth forth her fruits in due season and blesseth thee, O Yahuah (Lord).
verses.text: And looking up to the heaven she espied a nest of sparrows in the laurel-tree, and made a lamentation within herself, saying: Woe unto me, who begat me ? And what womb brought me forth, for I am become a curse before the children of Yashar'el, and I am reproached, and they have mocked me forth out of the temple of Yahuah? 2 Woe unto me, unto what am I likened ? I am not likened unto the fowls of the heaven, for even the fowls of the heaven are fruitful before thee, O Yahuah. Woe unto me, unto what am I likened? I am not likened unto the beasts of the earth, for even the beasts of the earth are fruitful before thee, O Yahuah. Woe unto me, unto what am I likened? I am not likened unto these waters, for even these waters are fruitful before thee, O Yahuah. 3 Woe unto me, unto what am I likened ? I am not likened unto this earth, for even this earth bringeth forth her fruits in due season and blesseth thee, O Yahuah.

verses.raw: And behold an angel of Yahuah (Lord) appeared, saying unto her: Anna, Anna, Yahuah (Lord) hath hearkened unto thy prayer, and thou shalt conceive and bear, and thy seed shall be spoken of in the whole world. And Anna said: As Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God) liveth, if I bring forth either male or female, I will bring it for a gift unto Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God), and it shall be ministering unto him all the days of its life.
verses.text: And behold an angel of Yahuah appeared, saying unto her: Anna, Anna, Yahuah hath hearkened unto thy prayer, and thou shalt conceive and bear, and thy seed shall be spoken of in the whole world. And Anna said: As Yahuah my Elohim liveth, if I bring forth either male or female, I will bring it for a gift unto Yahuah my Elohim, and it shall be ministering unto him all the days of its life.

verses.raw: And behold there came two messengers saying unto her: Behold loacim thy husband cometh with his flocks: for an angel of Yahuah (Lord) came down unto him saying: loacim, loacim, Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) hath hearkened unto thy prayer. Get thee down hence, for behold thy wife Anna hath conceived. 3 And loacim gat him down and called his herdsmen saying: Bring me hither ten lambs without blemish and without spot, and they shall be for Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God); and bring me twelve tender calves, and they shall be for the priests and for the assembly of the elders; and an hundred kids for the whole people.

verses.raw: And on the morrow he offered his gifts, saying in himself: If Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) be reconciled unto me, the plate that is upon the forehead of the priest will make it manifest unto me. And loacim offered his gifts and looked earnestly upon the plate of the priest when he went up unto the altar of Yahuah (Lord), and he saw no sin in himself. And loacim said: Now know I that Yahuah (Lord) is become propitious unto me and hath forgiven all my sins. And he went down from the temple of Yahuah (Lord) justified, and went unto his house.

verses.raw: And day by day the child waxed strong, and when she was six months old her mother stood her upon the ground to try if she would stand; and she walked seven steps and returned unto her bosom. And she caught her up, saying: As Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God) liveth, thou shalt walk no more upon this ground, until I bring thee into the temple of Yahuah (Lord). And she made a sanctuary in her bedchamber and suffered nothing common or unclean to pass through it. And she called for the daughters of the Hebrews that were undefiled, and they carried her hither and thither.

verses.raw: And the first year of the child was fulfilled^ and loacim made a great feast and bade the priests and the scribes and the assembly of the elders and the whole people of Yashar'el (Israel). And loacim brought the child to the priests, and they blessed her, saying: O Elohim (God) of our fathers, bless this child and give her a name renowned for ever among all generations. And all the people said: So be it, so be it. Amen. And he brought her to the high priests, and they blessed her, saying: O Elohim (God) of the high places, look upon this child, and bless her with the last blessing which hath no successor.

And Anna made a song unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), saying: 1. will sing an hymn unto Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God), because he hath visited me and taken away from me the reproach of mine enemies, and Yahuah (Lord) hath given me a fruit of his righteousness, single and manifold before him. Who shall declare unto the sons of Reuben that Anna giveth suck? Hearken, hearken, ye twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), that Anna giveth suck. And she laid the child to rest in the bedchamber of her sanctuary, and went forth and ministered unto them. And when the feast was ended, they gat them down rejoicing, and glorifying the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).

And loacim said: Let us bring her up to the temple of Yahuah (Lord) that we may pay the promise which we promised; lest Yahuah (Lord) require it of us (lit. send unto us), and our gift become unacceptable. And Anna said: Let us wait until the third year, that the child may not long after her father or mother. And loacim said: Let us wait.

verses.raw: And the child became three years old, and loacim said: Call for the daughters of the Hebrews that are undefiled, and let them take every one a lamp, and let them be burning, that the child turn not backward and her heart be taken captive away from the temple of Yahuah (Lord). And they did so until they were gone up into the temple of Yahuah (Lord). And the priest received her and kissed her and blessed her and said: Yahuah (Lord) hath magnified thy name among all generations; in thee in the latter days shall Yahuah (Lord) make manifest his redemption unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel). And he made her to sit upon the third step of the altar. And Yahuah (Lord) put grace upon her and she danced with her feet and all the house of Yashar'el (Israel) loved her.

verses.raw: And when she was twelve years old, there was a council of the priests, saying: Behold Mary is become twelve years old in the temple of Yahuah (Lord). What then shall we do with her? lest she pollute the sanctuary of Yahuah (Lord). And they said unto the high priest: Thou standest over the altar of Yahuah (Lord). Enter in and pray concerning her: And whatsoever Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal to thee, that let us do.

verses.raw: And the high priest took the vestment with the twelve bells and went in unto the Holy of Holies and prayed concerning her. And lo, an angel of Yahuah (Lord) appeared saying unto him: Zacharias, Zacharias, go forth and assemble them that are widowers of the people, and let them bring every man a rod, and to whomsoever Yahuah (Lord) shall show a sign, his wife shall she be. And the heralds went forth over all the country round about Judaea, and the trumpet of Yahuah (Lord) sounded, and all men ran thereto.

verses.raw: And Joseph cast down his adze and ran to meet them, and when they were gathered together they went to the high priest and took their rods with them. And he took the rods of them all and went into the temple and prayed. And when he had finished the prayer he took the rods and went forth and gave them back to them: and there was no sign upon them. But Joseph received the last rod: and lo, a dove came forth of the rod and flew upon the head of Joseph. And the priest said unto Joseph: Unto thee hath it fallen to take the virgin of Yahuah (Lord) and keep her for thyself. 2 And Joseph refused, saying: I have sons, and I am an old man, but she is a girl: lest I became a laughing-stock to the children of Yashar'el (Israel). And the priest said unto Joseph: Fear Yahuah (Lord) thy Elohim (God), and remember what things Elohim (God) did unto Dathan and Abiram and Korah, how the earth clave and they were swallowed up because of their gainsaying. And now fear thou, Joseph, lest it be so in thine house. And Joseph was afraid, and took her to keep her for himself. And Joseph said unto Mary: Lo, I have received thee out of the temple of Yahuah (Lord): and now do I leave thee in my house, and I go away to build my buildings and I will come again unto thee. Yahuah (Lord) shall watch over thee.

verses.raw: Now there was a council of the priests, and they said; Let us make a veil for the temple of Yahuah (Lord). And the priest said; Call unto me pure virgins of the tribe of David. And the officers departed and sought and found seven virgins. And the priests called to mind the child Mary, that she was of the tribe of David and was undefiled before Elohim (God): and the officers went and fetched her. And they brought them into the temple of Yahuah (Lord), and the priest said: Cast me lots, which of you shall weave the gold and the undefiled (the white) and the fine linen and the silk and the hyacinthine, and the scarlet and the true purple. And the lot of the true purple and the scarlet fell unto Mary, and she took them and went unto her house. [And at that season Zacharias became dumb, and Samuel was in his stead until the time when Zacharias spake again.] But Mary took the scarlet and began to spin it.

And she looked about her upon the right hand and upon the left, to see whence this voice should be: and being filled with trembling she went to her house and set down the pitcher, and took the purple and sat down upon her seat and drew out the thread.

verses.raw: And behold an angel of Yahuah (Lord) stood before her saying: Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace before Yahuah (Lord) of all things, and thou shalt conceive of his word. And she, when she heard it, questioned in herself, saying: Shall I verily conceive of the living Elohim (God), and bring forth after the manner of all women ? And the angel of Yahuah (Lord) said; Not so, Mary, for a x^ower of Yahuah (Lord) shall overshadow thee; wherefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of the Highest. And thou shalt call his name Yahusha (Jesus); for he shall save his people from their sins. And Mary said; Behold the handmaid of Yahuah (Lord) is before him; be it unto me according to thy word. XH. 1 And she made the purple and the scarlet and brought them unto the priest. And the priest blessed her and said: Mary, Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) hath magnified thy name, and thou shalt be blessed among all generations of the earth. 2 And Mary rejoiced and went away unto Elizabeth her kinswoman: and she knocked at the door. And Elizabeth when she heard it cast down the scarlet (al. the wool) and ran to the door and opened it, and when she saw Mary she blessed her and said: Whence is this to me that the mother of my Lord should come unto me? for behold that which is in me leaped and blessed thee. And Mary forgat the mysteries which Gabriel the archangel had told her, and she looked up unto the heaven and said; Who am I, Yahuah (Lord), that all the generations of the earth do bless me ? 3 And she abode three months with Elizabeth, and day by day her womb grew: and Mary was afraid and departed unto her house and hid herself from the children of Yashar'el (Israel). Now she was sixteen years old when these mysteries came to pass.

verses.raw: Now it was the sixth month with her, and behold Joseph came from his building, and he entered into his house and found her great with child. And he smote his face, and cast himself down upon the ground on sackcloth and wept bitterly, saying: With what countenance shall I look unto Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God)? and what prayer shall I make concerning this maiden? for I received her out of the temple of Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God) a virgin, and have not kept her safe. Who is he that hath ensnared me ? Who hath done this evil in mine house and hath defiled the virgin ? Is not the story of Adam repeated in me ? for as at the hour of his giving thanks the serpent came and found Eve alone and deceived her, so hath it befallen me also. 2 And Joseph arose from off the sackcloth and called Mary and said unto her O thou that wast cared for by Elohim (God), why hast thou done this? thou hast forgotten Yahuah (Lord) thy Elohim (God). Why hast thou humbled thy soul, thou that wast nourished up in the Holy of Holies and didst receive food at the hand of an angel? 3 But she wept bitterly, saying: I am pure and I know not a man. And Joseph said unto her: Whence then is that which is in thy womb ? and she said: As Yahuah (Lord) my Elohim (God) liveth, I know not whence it is come unto me.
